functions.name: PrepareCompositeUnitFrame
functions.comment:
Prepares composite unit frame by loading and drawing all COF components.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pUnit not NULL and has required bitmasks
2. Validate ptGfxInfo exists at pUnit[0x2e]
3. Search GFX info list for matching mode/direction entry
4. Get COF data pointer and calculate component byte offset
5. First pass: Load cel frames, track max width and loaded count
6. Second pass: Draw each component via Ordinal_10075

Parameters:
- pUnit (uint*): Composite unit structure pointer

Returns:
- void: No return value, draws directly to screen buffer

Magic Numbers:
- 0x2e (46): GFX info pointer offset in unit
- 0x1c (28): COF header size
- 0x0f (15): NUM_COMPONENTS - 1 max component check
- 0x12 (18): Cel data array clear count (72 bytes)

functions.name: DrawCompositeUnit
functions.comment:
Draws a composite unit with COF (Character animation) data.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pUnit is not NULL
2. Check if unit flags indicate drawing is enabled (gdwBitMasks[0])
3. If selection flag set (gdwBitMasks[0x28]), draw selection highlight cel
4. If unit has shadow data at offset 0xBC, draw shadow with color/direction
5. Lookup COF data from GfxInfo linked list matching unit token and mode
6. For each layer in COF, calculate direction from animation mode
7. Draw each layer using Ordinal_10072 with transform/palette lookup
8. Update animation frame counter and wrap at frame count limit
9. Advance animation tick timer every 0x42ms (66ms)
10. If squelch flag set (gdwBitMasks[0x24]), draw squelch/mute indicator

Parameters:
- pUnit: Pointer to composite unit structure (offset 0x14=X, 0x18=Y, 0xB8=GfxInfo, 0xBC=ShadowCel)
- nDrawMode: Draw mode passed to Ordinal_10072

Returns:
- 1 if unit was drawn successfully
- 0 if unit flags indicate no draw, or COF lookup failed

Magic Numbers:
- 0x12 (18): Number of DWORDs to clear in draw params struct
- 0x42 (66): Animation tick interval in milliseconds
- 0x40 (64): Max direction count for validation
- 0x1C (28): COF header size offset to layer data
- 0x100 (256): Palette/transform table stride

functions.name: RenderCompositeUnitText
functions.comment:
Renders text label for a composite unit (item/entity).

Algorithm:
1. Validate pUnit pointer, assert if NULL
2. Check visibility bit flag, return 0 if not visible
3. Determine font color based on unit type (0x10/0x12 = color 3, otherwise 0 or 1)
4. Check unit magic (D2VD/D2ST/D2XP) to select name offset
5. Build display text with optional title prefix
6. Append suffix text if present (player class, etc.)
7. Measure and truncate text if width exceeds 0x77 pixels, add ellipsis
8. Calculate centered X position from unit X and text width
9. Draw shadow text (if special type), then main text

Parameters:
- pUnit (uint*): Composite unit structure in ECX

Returns:
- 1 on success, 0 if unit not visible

Magic Numbers:
- 0x44324456: "D2VD" unit signature
- 0x44325354: "D2ST" unit signature
- 0x44325850: "D2XP" unit signature
- 0x77 (119): Max text width in pixels before truncation
- 0x10, 0x12: Unit types requiring shadow text (color 3)

functions.name: CallFunctionOnArrayElements
functions.signature: void CallFunctionOnArrayElements(void * pArrayBase, uint dwStride, int nCount, void * pfnCallback)
functions.comment:
Iterates over array elements and calls a callback on each.

Algorithm:
1. Check if nCount > 0 (count-1 >= 0)
2. Loop nCount times, calling pfnCallback with element address in ECX
3. Advance element pointer by dwStride each iteration

Parameters:
- pArrayBase (void*): Start address of array (passed in ECX to callback)
- dwStride (uint): Byte offset between elements
- nCount (int): Number of elements to process
- pfnCallback (void*): Function pointer called for each element

Returns:
- void

Notes:
- Used to initialize arrays of objects (e.g., Unicode default constructors)
- Callback receives element address via ECX register (__thiscall style)

functions.name: DrawChatUserTooltip
functions.comment:
Draws Battle.net chat user tooltip popup showing user type and account info.

Algorithm:
1. Validate composite unit pointer via ECX (FogAssert if null)
2. Initialize 256 Unicode string buffers for text lines
3. Check if unit flags indicate tooltip should display (bit 3)
4. Calculate tooltip rect based on unit X/Y position
5. Determine user type from offset +0x1C and format title line:
   - 0x10: Blizzard Rep
   - 0x11: Moderator (also shows realm info)
   - 0x12: Sysop
   - 0x13: Referee
   - 0x14: (unknown type)
   - 0x15: Speaker
   - 0x16: Open Character
   - Otherwise: Game product type (Starcraft, Diablo, Warcraft II, etc.)
6. Add realm info for D2DV/D2XP/D2ST products or Moderator
7. Add "Account Name: " line with account string from offset +0xCC
8. Calculate total tooltip width/height from string metrics
9. Clamp X position to screen bounds (0-800)
10. Draw each string line centered using Ordinal_10117

Parameters:
- IMPLICIT: ECX contains CompositeUnit pointer

Returns:
- 0 if unit is null or flags don't allow tooltip
- 1 on successful tooltip draw

Magic Numbers:
- 0x208 (520): Stride for Unicode string array entries
- 0x1E (30): Half-width offset for tooltip rect
- 0x50 (80): Height offset for tooltip rect
- 0x14 (20): Bottom padding for tooltip rect
- 0x320 (800): Screen width boundary

Related Functions:
- Ordinal_10170: Test if rect is visible
- Ordinal_10127: Set text color/style
- Ordinal_10131: Get string metrics (width/height)
- Ordinal_10117: Draw Unicode string at position

functions.name: ReleaseCompositeUnit
functions.comment:
Releases a composite unit and all associated COF (Component Object File) nodes.

Algorithm:
1. Validate unit pointer and graphics info pointer (assert if null)
2. Traverse linked list of COF node references from graphics info
3. For each COF node, decrement ref count and release if count reaches 0
4. Unlink released COF nodes from global g_piCofNodeList doubly-linked list
5. Release pool allocations for COF link entries
6. Clear graphics info pointer and release cached cel graphics via Ordinal_10041
7. If fRemoveFromList is set, unlink unit from g_pCompositeUnitList

Parameters:
- pUnit (void*): Pointer to composite unit structure (offset 0xB8 = GfxInfo, 0xBC = CelFile, 0xC4/0xC8 = list links)
- fRemoveFromList (int): If non-zero, remove unit from global composite unit list

Returns:
- void (no return value)

Magic Numbers:
- 0xB8: Offset to graphics info pointer in unit
- 0xBC: Offset to cel file pointer in unit
- 0xC4/0xC8 (196/200): Prev/next pointers for composite unit list
- 0x18/0x1C (24/28): Prev/next pointers for COF node list

Related Functions:
- Ordinal_10041: Releases cel graphics cache
- ReleasePoolAllocation: Fog memory pool deallocation

functions.name: SetCompositeUnitStrings
functions.signature: void SetCompositeUnitStrings(CompositeUnit * pUnit, Unicode * pwszStr1, Unicode * pwszStr2, Unicode * pwszStr3, Unicode * pwszStr4, DWORD dwOpt1, DWORD dwOpt2)
functions.comment:
Sets string fields and options on a CompositeUnit structure.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pUnit is not NULL (assert on failure, calls FUN_6f91436d to exit)
2. Copy pwszStr1 to pUnit->wszString1 at offset 0xCC via Unicode::strcpy
3. Copy pwszStr2 to pUnit->wszString2 at offset 0x14C via Unicode::strcpy
4. Copy pwszStr3 to pUnit->wszString3 at offset 0x1CC via Unicode::strcpy
5. Copy pwszStr4 to pUnit->wszString4 at offset 0x1EC via Unicode::strcpy
6. Store dwOpt1 at pUnit->dwOption1 (offset 0x22C)
7. Store dwOpt2 at pUnit->dwOption2 (offset 0x230)

Parameters:
- pUnit (CompositeUnit*): Pointer to CompositeUnit structure (asserted non-NULL)
- pwszStr1 (Unicode*): Unicode string copied to wszString1 field
- pwszStr2 (Unicode*): Unicode string copied to wszString2 field
- pwszStr3 (Unicode*): Unicode string copied to wszString3 field
- pwszStr4 (Unicode*): Unicode string copied to wszString4 field
- dwOpt1 (DWORD): Option value stored in dwOption1 field
- dwOpt2 (DWORD): Option value stored in dwOption2 field

Returns:
- void (no return value)

functions.name: SetCompositeMode
functions.comment:
Sets the animation mode for a composite unit by finding matching COF data.

Algorithm:
1. Validates composite unit handle is not null
2. Traverses linked list at offset 0xB8 searching for mode ID match
3. If mode found, copies COF header data to composite unit fields
4. Returns success/failure status

Parameters:
- pCompositeUnit (CompositeUnit*): Composite unit handle (ECX)
- nModeId (int): Animation mode identifier to set (EDX)

Returns:
- 1 if mode found and set successfully
- 0 if mode not found in linked list

Structure Offsets (CompositeUnit):
- +0x05: Direction count from COF
- +0x08: Frame index (reset to 0)
- +0x0C: Number of directions
- +0x10: Frame rate/speed from COF
- +0x20: Current mode ID
- +0xB8: Pointer to mode linked list

Magic Numbers:
- 0x897: Assert line for null handle check
- 0x3CE: Assert line for null COF data

functions.name: LoadExcelTableData
functions.signature: int * LoadExcelTableData(void * this, int nArchive, byte * pbTableName, void * pFieldDefs, int * pnRowCount, int nRowSize)
functions.comment:
Loads Excel table data from either binary cache or text file.

Algorithm:
1. Build file path: DATA\GLOBAL\EXCEL\{tableName}.{txt|bin}
2. Special case: if tableName matches "leveldefs", use "levels" instead
3. Load file data via FUN_6f913fa2
4. If text mode (g_fUseBinaryExcelData=0):
   a. Parse tab-delimited text to cell data
   b. Get row count from parsed data
   c. Allocate zeroed buffer (rowCount * rowSize)
   d. Populate table via PopulateExcelTableFromText
   e. Free parsed cell data
5. If binary mode: read row count and data pointer directly from buffer

Parameters:
- this (void*): Table loader context (ECX)
- nArchive (int): MPQ archive handle
- pbTableName (byte*): Table name string (e.g., "levels")
- pFieldDefs (void*): Field definition structure for parsing
- pnRowCount (int*): OUT - receives number of table rows
- nRowSize (int): Size of each table row in bytes

Returns:
- Pointer to allocated/loaded table data, NULL on failure

functions.name: LoadItemExcelTables
functions.comment:
Loads and initializes all item Excel data tables (weapons, armor, misc).

Algorithm:
1. Initialize 180+ field descriptors on stack defining item txt column parsing rules
2. Call LoadExcelTableData for weapons.txt, armor.txt, misc.txt
3. Calculate combined item count and allocate unified buffer (DAT_6f924bbc)
4. Copy all item records into combined buffer (weapons, armor, misc contiguous)
5. Build sorted index array for items with levelreq=0
6. Convert 3-char item codes to Unicode display names via GetStringIndex
7. Build sorted lookup by item code via InsertSortedIndexEntry

Parameters:
- nDataPtr (int): Pointer to data/file context passed to LoadExcelTableData

Returns:
- void (populates global item tables and indexes)

Magic Numbers:
- 0x250 (592): ItemRecord stride (bytes per item entry)
- 0x94 (148): ItemRecord stride in DWORDs (0x250/4)
- 0x80: Offset to 3-char item code in ItemRecord
- 0xe8: Offset to Unicode item name buffer in ItemRecord
- 0x40 (64): Max Unicode name length in chars
- 0x16: Offset to levelreq field for index building

Globals Modified:
- DAT_6f924bbc: Combined item table base pointer
- DAT_6f924bd8: Sorted index array pointer
- DAT_6f960900: Sorted code lookup table

Note: ~600 local_* variables are compile-time field descriptor array elements,
not runtime variables. Each 20-byte descriptor defines column name, parse type,
default value, struct offset, and flags for Excel txt parsing.

functions.name: LoadItemTypesTable
functions.comment:
Loads the itemtypes.txt Excel table and stores result in g_pItemTypesTable.

Algorithm:
1. Set up 4 linked column definitions on stack (code, equiv1, equiv2, end)
2. Call AllocAndZeroBuffer16 to allocate buffer, store in g_pItemTypesData
3. Call LoadExcelTableData with table name, column defs, row stride 0xEC (236)
4. Store returned table pointer in g_pItemTypesTable

Parameters:
- pBinFile (void*): ECX - binary file context for Excel loader

Returns:
- void (no return value)

Magic Numbers:
- 0x0A (10): Field type for "code" column
- 0x0D (13): Field type for linked columns (equiv1, equiv2)
- 4, 5: Column indices for equiv1 and equiv2 links
- 0xEC (236): Row stride in bytes for itemtypes table

functions.name: IsItemTypeEquivalent
functions.comment:
Checks if an item type is equivalent to or inherits from a target type.

Algorithm:
1. Return TRUE if target type is 0 (all types inherit from null)
2. Return FALSE if item type is 0 (null type inherits from nothing)
3. Push item type onto traversal stack
4. Loop: pop type, check equiv1/equiv2 parent types
5. Push non-zero parent types onto stack
6. Return TRUE if target found, FALSE if stack exhausted

Parameters:
- dwItemType: Item type code to check (from itemtypes.txt)
- dwTargetType: Target type code to match

Returns:
- TRUE (1): Item type is or inherits from target type
- FALSE (0): No inheritance relationship

Structure Layout:
- Offset +0x04: equiv1 (byte) - First parent type code
- Offset +0x05: equiv2 (byte) - Second parent type code
- Record size: 0xEC bytes per ItemTypeTxtRecord

Magic Numbers:
- 0xEC (236): ItemTypeTxtRecord stride
- 14 (0x0E): Maximum stack depth for type traversal

functions.name: SetCelGlobals
functions.comment:
Initializes global cel pointers and frame count limits for squelch/select UI.

Algorithm:
1. Store pSquelchCel in g_pSquelchCel
2. Get frame count from squelch cel, store in g_nSelectFrameMax
3. Store pSelectedCel in g_pSelectedCel
4. Get frame count from selected cel, store in g_nSquelchFrameMax

Parameters:
- pSquelchCel (uint*): Pointer to squelch cel file header
- pSelectedCel (uint*): Pointer to selected cel file header

Returns:
- void

functions.name: CreateCompositeUnit
functions.signature: CompositeUnit * CreateCompositeUnit(uint dwUnitType, uint dwMode, byte * pbComponents, byte * pbComponentIndices)
functions.comment:
Creates and initializes a new CompositeUnit for rendering composite sprites.

Algorithm:
1. Allocate 0x234 bytes for CompositeUnit structure
2. Zero-fill entire structure using REP STOSD
3. Allocate 4-byte GfxInfo pointer, store at offset 0xB8
4. Store unit type at offset 0x1C, call FUN_6f9057d0 if type < 7
5. Store mode at offset 0x20, apply bitmask flags at offset 0x00
6. Initialize 16 component slots (offset 0x38-0x78 and 0x78-0xB8)
7. Process 16 component indices from pbComponentIndices (offset 0x28)
8. Call FUN_6f904f30 and SetCompositeMode for validation
9. Link new unit into g_pCompositeUnitList doubly-linked list

Parameters:
- dwUnitType (uint): Unit type ID (0-6 use component lookup, 7+ skip)
- dwMode (uint): Initial composite mode for rendering
- pbComponents (byte*): Array of 16 component type bytes
- pbComponentIndices (byte*): Array of 16 component index bytes (0xFF = skip)

Returns:
- CompositeUnit* on success, NULL on allocation or validation failure

Magic Numbers:
- 0x234 (564): CompositeUnit structure size
- 0x8D (141): DWORD count for zero-fill (141*4 = 564)
- 0x10 (16): Number of component slots
- 0xC4: Offset of pNext pointer in linked list
- 0xC8: Offset of pPrev pointer in linked list

functions.name: LoadCompositeUnitCof
functions.comment:
Loads COF (Composite Object Format) data for a composite unit.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pCompositeUnit is not NULL (assert)
2. Check unit mode, class, and weapon class indices against limits
3. Reset to fallback values (7, 5, 1) if any index out of bounds
4. Get COF node list from pCompositeUnit->pGfxInfo (offset 0xB8)
5. Call LoadOrGetUnitCof with mode, class, weapon class code
6. On failure, retry with fallback mode=7, class=5, weapon=1
7. Assert on second failure

Parameters:
- pCompositeUnit (void*): Pointer to composite unit structure

Returns:
- 1: Always returns success (asserts on failure)

Magic Numbers:
- 0x1C: Offset to unit mode index
- 0x20: Offset to unit class index
- 0x24: Offset to weapon class index
- 0xB8: Offset to pGfxInfo (COF node list pointer)
- 7: Default unit mode (fallback)
- 5: Default unit class (fallback)
- 1: Default weapon class (fallback)

functions.name: InitItemTypesAndComponents
functions.comment:
Initializes item types and component type tables on first call.

Algorithm:
1. Check initialization flag (DAT_6f96094c) to prevent re-entry
2. Load ItemTypes.bin via Ordinal_10038 and LoadItemTypesTable
3. Zero g_adwComponentTypeTable array (0x2fd entries)
4. Build field descriptor array for Excel table loader (equiv1/2, order, repair, identify, shoots, quiver, throwable, reload, reequip, autostack, magic, normal, charm, beltable, costformula, varinvgfx, invgfx1-5)
5. Load itemtypes table via LoadExcelTableData -> g_pItemTypesTable
6. Load hitclass table via LoadExcelTableData
7. Call LoadItemExcelTables for additional item data
8. For each item in g_pItemTable:
   - Get component code from offset 0x84 or 0x80
   - Check if item type is armor/weapon via IsItemTypeEquivalent (types 0x2D, 3, 2, 0x25, 0x4B)
   - Find or create entry in g_adwComponentTypeTable
   - Store item type byte (offset 0x26) in g_adwComponentFrameTable
   - Lookup animation frame index from g_pItemTable+0x8C mapping
9. Set g_nComponentTypeCount to 0xFF

Parameters:
- None (void function)

Returns:
- void

Magic Numbers:
- 0x2fd (765): Component type table size
- 0x250 (592): Item record stride
- 0x84/0x80: Component code offsets in item record
- 0x26: Item type byte offset
- 0x8C: Animation mapping offset
- 0x2D (45): Armor type
- 0x32 (50): Shield type
- 0x4B (75): Jewel type

functions.name: GetCompositeWeaponClass
functions.comment:
Determines composite weapon class from two component slots.

Algorithm:
1. Read left-hand component (offset +5) and right-hand (offset +6)
2. For each slot: lookup base weapon class from component tables
3. If class is sheath (0xD/0xE) and unit type != 6, use alternate class
4. If IsItemTypeEquivalent(component, 0x32), use alternate class
5. Combine left/right classes using priority rules

Parameters:
- pbComponents (byte*): Component array, offsets +5/+6 are LH/RH slots
- nUnitType (int): Unit type (6 = special sheath handling)

Returns:
- Combined weapon class code (1-14), or 0 on invalid combination

Magic Numbers:
- 0x32 (50): Melee weapon item type
- 0xD (13), 0xE (14): Sheath weapon classes
- 0xB (11): Dual-wield combination class
- 0xA (10): Paired shield class
- 0xC (12): Component table stride

functions.name: RemapComponentIndex
functions.comment:
Remaps a component index based on item type equivalence checks.

Algorithm:
1. If nMode is 1-4 and component index > 3:
   - Check item type against shield (3), helm (0x10), armor (0xF), weapon (2)
   - For each matching type, search g_adwComponentTypeTable for matching record
   - If found, update component index; otherwise apply fallback (idx % 3 + 1)
2. If nMode is 0:
   - Check circlet type (0x25) against frame table and item type table
   - Remap to matching component or default to 1

Parameters:
- nMode (int): Processing mode (0=circlet check, 1-4=equipment types)
- pbyCompIdx (byte*): Pointer to component index to remap

Returns:
- void: Modifies *pbyCompIdx in place

Magic Numbers:
- 0x03: Shield item type
- 0x10 (16): Helm item type
- 0x0F (15): Armor item type
- 0x02: Weapon item type
- 0x25 (37): Circlet item type
- 0x0C (12): Component record stride

functions.name: InitCompositeUnitWeapon
functions.signature: void InitCompositeUnitWeapon(CompositeUnit * pCompositeUnit, uint dwWeaponClassInput, int dwMode, byte * pbComponentData, char * szComponentColors)
functions.comment:
Initialize CompositeUnit with weapon components and color data.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input CompositeUnit pointer
2. Allocate color buffer via FogMemAlloc(4)
3. Set weapon class; lookup composite weapon class if class < 7
4. Initialize component flag bits (multiple bitwise operations on unit state)
5. Loop through 16 components: fetch component data, remap indices
6. Copy color string data to unit structure (up to 16 bytes)
7. Load composite unit graphics via LoadCompositeUnitCof()
8. Apply composite mode via SetCompositeMode()

Parameters:
- pCompositeUnit (CompositeUnit*): Target unit structure (offset+0xb8=buffer, +0x1c=class, +0x24=composite, +0x20=mode)
- nWeaponClass (uint): Weapon class index (0-7 range)
- dwMode (uint): Composite mode flags
- pbComponentData (byte*): Component type array (16 bytes)
- szComponentColors (char*): Color string array (up to 16 bytes)

Returns:
- void; initializes structure in-place and applies graphics

Magic Numbers:
- 0xb8: Color buffer offset in CompositeUnit
- 0x1c: Weapon class field offset
- 0x24: Composite class field offset
- 0x20: Mode flags field offset
- 0x38: Component table start offset (offset 0x38, stride 0x4)
- 0x40: Component duration field offset (+0x40 per entry)
- 0x7: Weapon class range check boundary
- 0x10: 16 components per unit maximum

functions.name: ReleaseAllCompositeUnits
functions.comment:
Releases all composite units in the global linked list.

Algorithm:
1. Check if global composite unit list is empty; exit if so
2. Iterate through linked list of composite units
3. For each unit, call ReleaseCompositeUnit and ReleasePoolAllocation
4. Advance to next unit via offset 0xc4
5. After list exhausted, set global list pointer to null

Parameters:
- IMPLICIT: g_pCompositeUnitList (void*): Head of composite unit linked list

Returns:
- void

functions.name: GetCompositeUnitListHead
functions.comment:
Returns the head of the composite unit linked list.

Algorithm:
1. Load global composite unit list head pointer from g_pCompositeUnitList

Parameters:
- None

Returns:
- Pointer to first composite unit in the linked list, or NULL if empty

Related Functions:
- GetCompositeUnitNext: Returns next composite unit in list

functions.name: GetUnitField0xC4
functions.comment:
Retrieves 32-bit field from unit structure at offset 0xc4.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pUnit is not NULL (assert failure if NULL)
2. Read dword from pUnit + 0xc4
3. Return the field value

Parameters:
- pUnit (void*): Pointer to unit structure

Returns:
- uint: Value at unit structure offset 0xc4

Magic Numbers:
- 0xc4 (196): Unit structure field offset
- 0xded (3565): Assert line number

functions.name: SetDataFieldWithValidation
functions.comment:
Updates a data structure field with a byte value, applying validation constraints.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pData is not NULL, fail assertion if NULL
2. Apply conditional mask to byValue: if byValue <= 0, result is 0
3. Read constraint threshold from pData[5]
4. Clamp result to not exceed threshold value
5. Store clamped result to pData[4]

Parameters:
- pData (void*): Pointer to data structure
- byValue (byte): Value to set, subject to validation

Returns:
- void

functions.name: GetByteAtOffset5
functions.comment:
Retrieve a byte value from an object at a fixed offset.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input pointer is non-NULL
2. If NULL, call assertion handler with error details
3. Otherwise, load byte value from offset 0x5 within object
4. Return the byte value

Parameters:
- pData (void*): Pointer to data structure (checked for NULL)

Returns:
- Byte value from offset 0x5 within the object

Magic Numbers:
- 0x5: Fixed offset to access target byte

functions.name: GetUnitField0C
functions.comment:
Returns dword field at offset 0x0C from Unit structure.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pUnit is non-NULL
2. Assert failure if NULL (does not return)
3. Return *(uint*)(pUnit + 0x0C)

Parameters:
- pUnit (CompositeUnit*): Pointer to unit structure

Returns:
- uint: Field value at offset 0x0C

Magic Numbers:
- 0x0C (12): Offset of target field in unit structure
- 0xE0C (3596): Source line number for assertion

functions.name: SetUnitScaledValue
functions.comment:
Sets a scaled and clamped value in a unit structure field.

Algorithm:
1. Validate unit pointer (assert if NULL)
2. Read max value from unit+0xc field
3. Scale max value by 0x100 (256)
4. Clamp input value to non-negative (negate if negative)
5. Take minimum of clamped value and scaled max
6. Store result at unit+0x8 field

Parameters:
- pUnit (void*): Pointer to unit structure
- nValue (int): Value to clamp and store (can be negative)

Returns:
- void

Magic Numbers:
- 0x8: Offset of value field in unit
- 0xc: Offset of max value field in unit
- 0x100 (256): Scaling factor for max value

functions.name: SetUnitField14
functions.comment:
Sets a unit structure field at offset 0x14 to the specified value.

Algorithm:
1. Load pUnit from stack parameter
2. Test if pUnit equals null (zero)
3. If null, push assertion parameters (line 0xe22, file pointer, arg pointer)
4. Call FogAssert to report assertion failure
5. Call AssertFailure(0xffffffff) to terminate
6. If not null, load dwValue from second stack parameter
7. Store dwValue to memory at pUnit + 0x14
8. Return to caller with stack cleanup

Parameters:
- pUnit (CompositeUnit*): Pointer to unit structure, must not be null
- dwValue (dword): 32-bit value to store at unit structure offset 0x14

Returns:
- void (function does not return if pUnit is null, assertion fails)

functions.name: SetUnitFieldValue
functions.comment:
Validates unit pointer and stores a value at unit offset 0x18.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pUnit is not NULL, assert if invalid
2. Terminate process with code -1 if validation fails
3. Store dwValue at offset 0x18 within unit structure

Parameters:
- pUnit (void*): Pointer to unit structure, must be non-NULL
- dwValue (dword): Value to store at unit+0x18

Returns:
- void

functions.name: GetUnitIdFromPointer
functions.comment:
Dereferences and returns unit ID from pointer.

Algorithm:
1. Assert pdwUnitId pointer is not NULL (with CompositeUnit validation)
2. Dereference pointer to extract unit ID value
3. Return dereferenced unit ID

Parameters:
- pdwUnitId (uint*): Pointer to unit ID value, must not be NULL

Returns:
- Unit ID value (uint): The dereferenced unit ID from the pointer

functions.name: WriteValueToPointer
functions.comment:
Writes a value to the specified pointer with null validation.

Algorithm:
1. Assert that the pointer is not null
2. Dereference pointer and write the value to it
3. Return

Parameters:
- pdwValue (uint*): Target pointer to receive the value
- dwValue (uint): Value to write

Returns:
- void

functions.name: SetEmblemIcon
functions.signature: void SetEmblemIcon(uint dwUnit, byte byEmblemType, byte byEmblemColor, byte byEmblemMode)
functions.comment:
Sets emblem icon properties for a unit based on type, color, and mode.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pUnit is non-NULL (assert if invalid)
2. If nEmblemType in range [1, 32]:
   a. Build icon resource path using nEmblemType index
   b. Load emblem icon via Ordinal_10039
   c. Store icon ID at unit offset 0xBC
   d. Set color from g_abEmblemColorTable (nEmblemColor 1-10, else 0)
   e. Set mode from g_abEmblemModeTable (nEmblemMode 1-10, else 0)
3. Return without changes if nEmblemType is outside valid range

Parameters:
- dwUnit (uint): Unit structure pointer for emblem configuration
- byEmblemType (byte): Emblem type (1-32, table index minus 1 for icon lookup)
- byEmblemColor (byte): Emblem color index (0=default, 1-10=use table)
- byEmblemMode (byte): Emblem mode index (0=default, 1-10=use table)

Returns:
- void

functions.name: InitPaletteColorTables
functions.comment:
Initializes all game palette color transform tables by loading from resource files.

Algorithm:
1. For each of 8 palette categories (default, brown, greybrown, etc.):
   a. Construct full file path by concatenating base path with palette name
   b. Open async file handle using constructed path
   c. If file open succeeds:
      - Read binary palette data via ReadTransformData
      - Close file handle via CloseFileHandleIfValid
   d. If file open fails:
      - Log warning to debug output
      - Zero-initialize 0x540-entry (1344 dword) palette table
2. After all 8 palettes loaded, call LoadColorTransformData twice with special palette IDs

Parameters:
- IMPLICIT: No parameters

Returns:
- void

Magic Numbers:
- 0x100 (256): Temporary buffer size for path construction
- 0x540 (1344): Palette table entry count
- 0x1500 (5376): Palette data size in bytes (1344 * 4 bytes)
- 0x104 (260): Stack frame size for buffer and temporary variables

functions.name: LoadColorTransformData
functions.comment:
Loads color transform data from file and initializes global transform table.

Algorithm:
1. Read base palette path from global string
2. Append input palette path to create full path
3. Append gamma adjustment path to buffer
4. Validate transform data file using FUN_6f913e1e
5. If valid, initialize transform table with FUN_6f913efb and FUN_6f913e66
6. If invalid, clear transform table (0x540 DWORDs) and log warning

Parameters:
- szPalettePath (char*): Palette filename to load
- nTransformIndex (int): Index into global transform table (multiplies by 0x6900)

Returns:
- void (no return value)

functions.name: InitializeTransformTables
functions.comment:
Initializes two transformation lookup tables by applying a transform function to triplets of input bytes.

Algorithm:
1. Iterate through first input table (g_abTransformTable1Data) in strides of 3
2. Call Ordinal_10034 with each triplet (previous, current, next bytes)
3. Store result byte in output table (g_abTransformTable1Out)
4. Repeat for second input table (g_abTransformTable2Data) to output (g_abTransformTable2Out)

Parameters:
- IMPLICIT: ESI, EDI used for loop control
- Input tables: g_abTransformTable1Data, g_abTransformTable2Data
- Output tables: g_abTransformTable1Out, g_abTransformTable2Out

Returns:
- void

Magic Numbers:
- 0x3: Triplet stride (3-byte groups)
- Table boundaries: 0x6f91f1a7, 0x6f91f1c7 (loop termination addresses)

functions.name: CalculateCharacterTitleTier
functions.signature: void CalculateCharacterTitleTier(int nContext, int nLevel, int nBonus, int nClassId)
functions.comment:
Calculate skill tier based on character level and class.

Algorithm:
1. Determine base tier threshold based on nClassId (0 = standard, non-zero = special)
2. Map nLevel to base tier (0-3 levels): levels 0-3→0, 4-7→1, 8-11→2, 12+→3
3. Add 3 to tier if nBonus bonus is active and tier is non-zero
4. Pass calculated nTier to Ordinal_10160 for further processing

Parameters:
- hContext: Context handle
- nLevel: Character level (determines base tier)
- nBonus: Bonus flag (adds 3 to tier when set)
- nClassId: Class identifier (affects tier thresholds)

Returns:
- void (processes tier through Ordinal_10160)

functions.name: GetCharacterTitleString
functions.signature: char * GetCharacterTitleString(uint dwCharClass, uint dwTitle, int nFemale)
functions.comment:
Returns the title name string for a character class and title combination.

Algorithm:
1. Check bFemale flag to select gender-specific title table
2. Use dwCharClass (0-9) as index into class lookup table
3. Use dwTitle (1-6) as index into title string lookup
4. Return corresponding title name string pointer

Parameters:
- dwCharClass (uint): Character class code (0-9)
- dwTitle (uint): Title rank code (1-6 for standard titles)
- bFemale (int): Gender flag (0=male titles, non-zero=female titles)

Returns:
- Pointer to title name string (e.g., "Dame", "Lord", "Queen")
- Returns default string if parameters out of range

functions.name: CreateUnit
functions.signature: void * CreateUnit(dword nUnitType, dword nSubType, dword nX, dword nY, dword nGfxType, dword * pdwInitData)
functions.comment:
Allocates and initializes a unit object with specified attributes.

Algorithm:
1. Allocate 0x58 (88) bytes of memory for unit structure
2. Clear all fields to zero
3. Set type field (offset 0) to 0xc
4. Apply type and state bit masks to field at offset 2
5. Store parameters into structure fields (type, subtype, coordinates, gfx type)
6. Set function pointers for event handlers
7. Copy initialization data from pdwInitData or use defaults
8. Invoke post-initialization handler (FUN_6f90ea50)
9. Return allocated unit pointer

Parameters:
- nUnitType (ECX): Unit type identifier (stored at offset 0xc)
- nSubType (EDX): Unit subtype/class (stored at offset 0x14)
- nX (Stack+0x4): X coordinate (stored at offset 0x18)
- nY (Stack+0x8): Y coordinate (stored at offset 0x1c)
- nGfxType (Stack+0xc): Graphics type flag (stored at offset 0x4c)
- pdwInitData (Stack+0x10): Optional pointer to 2-dword initialization data

Returns:
- void*: Pointer to newly allocated and initialized unit structure

functions.name: ReleaseInventoryList
functions.comment:
Releases all items in an inventory list and cleans up the structure.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input is inventory type (0xc)
2. Iterate through linked list at offset 0x40
3. Release each pool allocation at offset 0x34
4. Call cleanup routine on inventory structure

Parameters:
- pInventory (void*): Pointer to inventory structure

Returns:
- void

Magic Numbers:
- 0xc: Inventory type identifier
- 0x40: List head offset
- 0x34: Next pointer offset (linked list stride)

functions.name: FreeListData
functions.comment:
Frees all allocated nodes in a linked list data structure.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input is correct type (0xc = list data type)
2. Get head of linked list from offset 0x10
3. Iterate through chain, following next pointer at offset 0x34
4. Release each node's pool allocation

Parameters:
- pListData (int*): Pointer to list data structure containing head pointer

Returns:
- void

Magic Numbers:
- 0xc: Expected list data type identifier
- 0x10: Offset to list head pointer
- 0x34: Offset to next pointer in linked list node

functions.name: AccountInsertName
functions.comment:
Inserts an account name record into a linked list.

Algorithm:
1. Validate account has expected type 0xc, assert on mismatch
2. Allocate 0x38 (56) bytes for account name node
3. Copy up to 0x32 (50) bytes from input string to node
4. Clear bytes 0x34-0x37 with null terminators
5. Link into account list at offset 0x40 (FIFO - new node points to old head, becomes new head)

Parameters:
- pAccount (int*): Pointer to account structure; offset 0x0 contains type field, offset 0x40 contains name list head
- szName (char*): Input string to copy (max 0x32 bytes, null-terminated not required)

Returns:
- void

Magic Numbers:
- 0xc (12): Account structure type identifier
- 0x38 (56): Size of allocated name node
- 0x32 (50): Maximum name string length
- 0x34-0x37: Null terminator quad-word in name node
- 0x40 (64): Offset of name list head in account structure

Structure Layout:
Name node [0x38 bytes]:
- [0x0:0x33] (52 bytes): Name string buffer
- [0x34:0x37] (4 bytes): Next pointer (linked list)

functions.name: FindAndRemoveListNode
functions.comment:
Searches for and removes a node from a linked list by value comparison.

Algorithm:
1. Validate list structure (check count at offset 0)
2. Get head node pointer from list offset 0x10
3. Traverse list comparing node data with search value byte-by-byte
4. If match found, unlink node from list (update previous->next or head)
5. Clear tail pointer if removing tail node (offset 0x11)
6. Deallocate matched node via ReleasePoolAllocation
7. Return true on match, false if no matching node found

Parameters:
- pList (int*): Pointer to list structure with count at [0], head at [0x10], tail at [0x11]
- pbSearchValue (byte*): Null-terminated byte sequence to match against node data

Returns:
- true (1): Node found and removed from list
- false (0): No matching node found

Magic Numbers:
- 0x0c: Expected list type identifier for validation
- 0x10: Offset to head node pointer in list structure
- 0x11: Offset to tail node pointer in list structure
- 0x34: Offset to next pointer in node structure

functions.name: CopyAccountString
functions.comment:
Copies a string from an account structure to destination buffer.

Algorithm:
1. Validate account data structure type (must be 0xC)
2. Get string pointer from offset 0x44 of account data
3. Calculate string length using strlen-like loop
4. Copy string in 4-byte chunks (optimization via MOVSD)
5. Copy remaining bytes individually
6. Return 1 on success, 0 if source is NULL

Parameters:
- pAccountData (dword *): Pointer to account structure
- pszDest (byte *): Destination buffer to receive string copy

Returns:
- 1 if copy succeeded
- 0 if source string was NULL

functions.name: RenderAccountListGrid
functions.comment:
Renders account list entries in a 6-column grid layout.

Classification: Callback/Handler - Render callback stored in list data structure at offset 0x1C.

Algorithm:
1. Validate list data type is 0xc (D2WIN_ACCOUNTLIST), assert and abort if not
2. Check visibility flags (bits 0 and 3) and list head pointer, return 0 if conditions not met
3. Set active font from pListData[0x14] (font index)
4. Initialize 512-character Unicode buffer for text conversion
5. Cache layout parameters: nBaseX from pListData[0xC], nSubtypeY from pListData[0x10], nY from pListData[0x18]
6. Get current font height from GetCurrentFontProperty()
7. Iterate through linked list (next pointer at node offset 0x34):
   a. Check if item index is within visible range [scrollOffset, scrollOffset + 24)
   b. Calculate grid X position: nBaseX + (index % 6) * 0x78 (120 pixels per column)
   c. Calculate grid Y position: fontHeight + (nSubtypeY - nY) + (index / 6) * 0x14 (20 pixels per row)
   d. Set clip region for item icon area (28x14 pixels)
   e. Convert account name (ANSI at node base) to Unicode
   f. Render text at (X + 32, Y) with no line height adjustment
   g. If current node matches selected node (pListData[0x44]), draw selection highlight rectangle
   h. Increment item index and continue to next node
8. Return 1 on successful render, 0 if visibility conditions not met

Parameters:
- pListData (ECX): Pointer to account list data structure (type 0xc)

Returns:
- 1: Successfully rendered visible account list items
- 0: Visibility flags not set or list is empty

Structure Layout (AccountListData at pListData):
Offset  Size  Field              Description
0x00    4     dwType             Must be 0xc for account list
0x08    4     dwFlags            Visibility/enabled bitmask
0x0C    4     nBaseX             X coordinate for grid base
0x10    4     nSubtypeY          Subtype Y offset
0x18    4     nY                 Y coordinate base
0x40    4     pListHead          Head of linked list (account nodes)
0x44    4     pSelectedNode      Currently selected node
0x48    4     nScrollOffset      First visible item index
0x50    4     nFontIndex         Font to use for rendering

Account Node Layout (at szCurrentNode):
Offset  Size  Field              Description
0x00    52    szAccountName      ANSI account name string
0x34    4     pNextNode          Pointer to next node in list

Magic Numbers:
- 0xc: Account list type identifier
- 0x78 (120): Grid column width in pixels (6 columns)
- 0x14 (20): Grid row height in pixels
- 0x18 (24): Maximum visible items in grid (6 columns x 4 rows)
- 0x1c (28): Icon clip width
- 0x0e (14): Icon clip height
- 0x20 (32): Text X offset from column start
- 0x55: Clip validation flag for icon area
- 0xff: Clip validation flag for selection highlight

Decompiler Artifacts:
- extraout_var (undefined3): Spurious high bytes from CONCAT31 operation in font height calculation

Variable Mappings (SSA temporaries):
- nItemIndex: Loop counter for item position in list
- nBaseX: X coordinate base loaded from pListData[0x0C]
- szCurrentNode: Current linked list node being rendered
- byFontHeight: Font height from GetCurrentFontProperty()
- nSubtypeY: Y offset from pListData[0x10]
- nY: Base Y from pListData[0x18]
- nGridX/nGridY: Calculated grid cell coordinates
- awUnicodeBuffer: 512-char Unicode buffer for text conversion

Cross-References:
- Called from CreateUnit as render callback (stored at offset 0x1C)
- Uses SelectListNodeByGridPosition for mouse selection logic

functions.name: SelectListNodeByGridPosition
functions.comment:
Selects a linked list node based on calculated grid position from screen coordinates.

Algorithm:
1. Dereference ppListData to get actual unit/list data pointer
2. Assert type field equals 0xc (list data type validation)
3. Check bitmask flags at offset 0x8 - both visibility and enabled bits must be set
4. If linked list at offset 0x40 is empty, return 0 (no selection possible)
5. Calculate target grid index from screen position:
   - Row = (g_nScreenHeight - unitY) / 120  (120 pixels per row)
   - Col = ((unitWidth - unitX) + 4 + g_nScreenWidth) / 20  (20 pixels per column)
   - Index = Row + Col * 6  (6 rows per column)
6. Walk linked list (next pointer at offset 0x34) until index reached
7. Store selected node at offset 0x44 (or 0 if list exhausted)
8. Return 1 on success, 0 if conditions not met

Parameters:
- ppListData: Pointer to pointer to list data structure (type 0xc)

Returns:
- 1: Successfully selected a node (or cleared selection if list exhausted)
- 0: Conditions not met (flags not set or no list)

Structure Layout (ListData at *ppListData):
Offset  Size  Field           Description
0x00    4     dwType          Must be 0xc for list data
0x08    4     dwFlags         Bitmask flags (visibility/enabled)
0x0c    4     nUnitY          Y coordinate for row calculation
0x10    4     nUnitX          X coordinate
0x18    4     nUnitWidth      Width for column calculation
0x40    4     pListHead       Head of linked list (nodes)
0x44    4     pSelectedNode   Currently selected node (output)

Linked List Node (at offset 0x34 is next pointer):
- Each node is 0x38+ bytes
- Offset 0x34: pNextNode pointer

Magic Numbers:
- 0xc: List data type identifier
- 0x78 (120): Grid row height in pixels
- 0x14 (20): Grid column width in pixels
- 6: Number of rows per column in grid layout

functions.name: CreateGameObject
functions.signature: void * CreateGameObject(uint dwValue1, uint dwValue2, uint dwValue3, uint dwValue4, uint dwValue5, uint dwValue6, uint dwValue7, int nInitParam, int nDefaultValue, uint dwValue10)
functions.comment:
Allocates and initializes a game object structure (96 bytes).

Algorithm:
1. Allocate 96-byte block via FogMemAlloc
2. Zero-initialize all fields via loop
3. Set base flags in fields [0] and [2] with bitmask values
4. Populate object fields from parameters
5. Link function pointers for callbacks
6. Call initialization callback FUN_6f90ea50

Parameters:
- dwValue1 (uint): Field [3] value
- dwValue2 (uint): Field [4] value
- dwValue3 (uint): Field [5] value
- dwValue4 (uint): Field [6] value
- dwValue5 (uint): Field [1] value
- dwValue6 (uint): Field [0x11] value
- dwValue7 (uint): Field [0xd] value
- nInitParam (int): Determines callback population at field [0xe]
- nDefaultValue (int): Defaults to 5, stored in field [0x15]
- dwValue10 (uint): Field [0x16] value

Returns:
- Pointer to allocated and initialized 96-byte structure

Magic Numbers:
- 0x60 (96): Structure size in bytes
- 0x18 (24): Loop count for 24 dword zero-initialization
- Field [0] is set to 2 (structure type marker)
- Field [0x12] populated with GetTickCount() timestamp

functions.name: GetAnimationField
functions.comment:
Returns animation data field after validating structure type.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pAnim type field equals 2
2. Assert on type mismatch (does not return)
3. Return animation field at offset 0x14

Parameters:
- pAnim (int*): Animation structure pointer
  - [0x00]: Type field (must equal 2)
  - [0x14]: Animation data field

Returns:
- int: Value from pAnim[0x14]

functions.name: AnimUpdateState
functions.comment:
Updates animation state transitions for the given animation object.

Algorithm:
1. Asserts animation type equals 2
2. Reads current state from field 0x14
3. If state == 3: transition to state 4, clear field 0x13, record current tick
4. If state == 2 or 4: return success
5. All other states: return success

Parameters:
- pAnimObj (int*): Pointer to animation object with state fields

Returns:
- 1 on successful state transition or valid state
- Does not return on assertion failure

functions.name: ValidateCelBounds
functions.comment:
Validates whether a Cel sprite fits within screen boundaries.

Algorithm:
1. Verify pCelInfo parameter type is 2
2. Extract table index from pCelInfo[0x10] and pCelInfo[0x14]
3. Load CelFileInfo for the cel (width, height, mode, etc.)
4. Check bounds: cel must fit within screen with margins
5. Return 1 if valid, 0 if out of bounds

Parameters:
- pCelInfo (int *): Cel information structure, pCelInfo[0] must equal 2

Returns:
- 1 if cel fits within screen bounds
- 0 if cel exceeds screen boundaries

Magic Numbers:
- 0x10, 0x14: Offsets into pCelInfo structure
- 0x73: Line number in FogAssert
- 0xffffffff: Error code for assertion failure

functions.name: RenderAnimatedGameObject
functions.comment:
Renders an animated game object by managing animation state, frame timing, and cel drawing.

Classification: Worker function (render callback for type 2 game objects)

Algorithm:
1. Validate object type == 2, assert failure if not
2. Zero-initialize 0x12 dwords of local CelFileInfo array
3. Early exit with success (1) if no cel data (field[1]) and no anim table (field[0x10])
4. Cache position from fields[3] (X) and [4] (Y)
5. If animation table exists (field[0x10] != 0):
   a. Get animation mode from field[0x14]
   b. If mode is 0 or 1, validate cel bounds and update mode
   c. If mode changed, invoke optional callback at field[0x16]
   d. Get frame count from current animation entry
   e. Handle animation state transitions:
      - State 2: If at end, reset to frame 0 and transition to state 3
      - State 4: If at end, reset to frame 0 and transition to state 1
   f. Reset timestamp via GetTickCount on state transition
   g. Clamp frame index to valid range
6. Load cel pointers:
   a. If no anim table: use field[1] as single cel, adjust position by cel dimensions
   b. If anim table: index by (field[0x10] + field[0x14] * 0x10) for primary/secondary cels
7. Render primary cel via GfxInterfaceCall84 if present
8. Render secondary cel via GfxInterfaceCall84 if present
9. Update frame animation based on elapsed time:
   a. Calculate frame duration: (direction * 1000) / 25 ms per frame
   b. For states 2/4: linear frame progression clamped to max
   c. For other states: looping frame calculation via modulo

Parameters:
- pAnimObject (int * via ECX): Pointer to 96-byte game object structure

Returns:
- 1: Always returns success

Game Object Structure Layout (offsets in dwords):
Offset  Size  Field              Description
0x00    4     dwType             Type identifier (must be 2)
0x01    4     pCelFile           Single cel file pointer (when no anim table)
0x03    4     dwPosX             X coordinate
0x04    4     dwPosY             Y coordinate
0x10    4     pAnimTable         Animation table base pointer
0x11    4     nDirection         Animation direction value
0x12    4     dwStartTick        Animation start timestamp
0x13    4     nCurrentFrame      Current frame index
0x14    4     nAnimState         Animation state (0-4)
0x15    4     dwPrimaryAlpha     Primary cel alpha value
0x16    4     pfnStateCallback   Optional state change callback
0x17    4     fAnimEnabled       Animation enabled flag

Animation Table Entry (16 bytes per state):
Offset  Size  Field              Description
0x00    4     ppCelPrimary       Pointer to primary cel pointer
0x04    4     ppCelSecondary     Pointer to secondary cel pointer
0x08    4     dwAlpha            Secondary cel alpha
0x0C    4     nDirection         Direction for this state

Animation States:
0 = Initial/Idle
1 = Active (looping)
2 = Playing forward (clamps at end, transitions to 3)
3 = Stopped at end
4 = Playing forward (clamps at end, transitions to 1)

Magic Numbers:
- 0x12 (18): Dwords to zero-initialize (72 bytes)
- 0x10 (16): Animation table entry stride
- 0x19 (25): Frame rate divisor (25 fps base)
- 1000: Milliseconds per second for timing
- 0xffffffff: Alpha parameter for GfxInterfaceCall84

Called From:
- CreateGameObject stores this at field[7] as render callback

functions.name: AnimCallbackUpdateState
functions.comment:
AnimCallbackUpdateState - Invokes animation update callback and manages state transitions.

Algorithm:
1. Dereference ppAnimHandle to get pAnimObj (D2WIN_IMAGE structure)
2. Assert pAnimObj->eType == 2 (D2WIN_IMAGE type validation)
3. Check if pAnimObj->pfnUpdateCallback (offset 0x34) is non-null
4. If null, return 0 (no callback to invoke)
5. Call pfnUpdateCallback(ppAnimHandle) and capture return value
6. If callback returns 0, return 0 (no state change needed)
7. Check current state at pAnimObj->nState (offset 0x50):
   - If state == 3: transition to state 4
   - If state == 1: transition to state 2
   - Otherwise: return callback result unchanged
8. Clear pAnimObj->nFrameCounter (offset 0x4C) to 0
9. Store GetTickCount() in pAnimObj->dwLastTick (offset 0x48)
10. Return callback result

Parameters:
- ppAnimHandle (int**): Double pointer to animation object handle

Returns:
- int: Result from pfnUpdateCallback, or 0 if no callback

State Transitions:
- State 1 -> 2: Animation starting -> playing
- State 3 -> 4: Animation stopping -> stopped

Structure Offsets (D2WIN_IMAGE, size 0x60):
Offset  Size  Field              Type        Description
0x00    4     eType              uint        Type marker (must be 2)
0x34    4     pfnUpdateCallback  code*       Update callback function pointer
0x48    4     dwLastTick         DWORD       Last update tick count
0x4C    4     nFrameCounter      int         Frame counter (reset on transition)
0x50    4     nState             int         Animation state (1-4)

functions.name: SetAnimImageField
functions.comment:
Sets a value field on an animation image structure.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pAnim type field equals 2 (IMAGE type)
2. Assert and abort if type mismatch
3. Write nValue to structure offset 0x5c (field index 0x17)
4. Return 1 (success)

Parameters:
- pAnim (int*): Pointer to animation/image structure (type must be 2)
- nValue (int): Value to write at offset 0x5c

Returns:
- 1: Always on success (asserts on type mismatch)

Magic Numbers:
- 2: Expected type for IMAGE structure
- 0x5c (92): Offset of target data field

functions.name: LoadCelImage
functions.comment:
Loads a CEL image file from the given path and allocates CEL image data.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate string length of input path via string scan
2. Copy input path to local buffer (260-byte stack buffer)
3. Retrieve game structure selector from parameter
4. Concatenate local path with game structure selector path
5. Call FUN_6f913fa2 to create CEL file handle
6. Allocate CEL image data via AllocateCelImageData
7. Return CEL file handle (or NULL if allocation failed)

Parameters:
- szPath (char*): CEL file path
- dwGameStructureId (DWORD): Game structure identifier

Returns:
- void*: Pointer to CEL file data structure, or NULL on failure

Magic Numbers:
- 0x104 (260): Local buffer size for path concatenation
- 0x41 (65): Flag parameter to FUN_6f913fa2
- 0x42 (66): Flag parameter to AllocateCelImageData

functions.name: LoadCelImageWithStructurePath
functions.signature: dword LoadCelImageWithStructurePath(char * lpszFilename, int * pdwOutput, dword dwStructId)
functions.comment:
Loads a CEL image file by combining game structure path with source filename.

Algorithm:
1. Measures and copies source filename to local 260-byte buffer
2. Gets game structure path via GetGameStructureSelector
3. Concatenates structure path with buffered filename
4. Loads CEL file data via LoadAsyncFileData
5. Allocates CEL image data structure via AllocateCelImageData

Parameters:
- lpszFilename (char*): Source CEL filename
- pdwOutput (int*): Output data pointer
- dwStructId (dword): Game structure selector ID

Returns:
- dword: Handle or status value (from EBX)

functions.name: ReleaseCelFile
functions.comment:
Release and cleanup a CEL (CelFile) graphics resource.

Algorithm:
1. Clear the CEL graphics cache for the given CEL file
2. If CEL file is non-null, release its memory pool allocation

Parameters:
- pCelFile (CelFile*): Pointer to CEL file structure to release

Returns:
- void

functions.name: ShowInsertExpansionDiscDialog
functions.comment:
Displays a message box requesting the Expansion Disc to be inserted.

Algorithm:
1. Calls Ordinal_10027 to get the main application window handle
2. Prepares message box parameters with "Insert Expansion Disc" text
3. Displays MessageBoxA dialog with MB_YESNO buttons (type 0x31)
4. Converts button response to boolean: IDYES (1) becomes true, others become false
5. Returns result to caller

Parameters:
- None (void)

Returns:
- true (1) if user clicked "Yes" to confirm
- false (0) if user cancelled or clicked "No"

Magic Numbers:
- 0x31: MB_YESNO | MB_ICONEXCLAMATION message box style

functions.name: ShowInsertPlayDiscDialog
functions.comment:
Display "Insert Play Disc" dialog and return success status.

Algorithm:
1. Get parent window handle via GetParentWindowHandle
2. Display MessageBoxA with title "Diablo II" and message "Insert Play Disc"
3. Return true if user clicked OK (button ID 1), false otherwise

Parameters:
- IMPLICIT: MessageBox uses standard Windows HWND and IDOK responses

Returns:
- bool: true (1) if user clicked OK, false (0) if user clicked Cancel

Magic Numbers:
- 0x31: MB_OKCANCEL | MB_ICONEXCLAMATION (MessageBox style flags)

functions.name: PromptInsertCinematicsDisc
functions.comment:
Displays a message box prompting the user to insert the Diablo II Cinematics Disc.

Algorithm:
1. Calls Ordinal_10027 to get the main window handle
2. Displays MessageBoxA with the message "Insert Cinematics Disc" on the obtained window
3. Converts the dialog result (IDOK=1) to bool: returns 1 if OK clicked, 0 otherwise

Parameters:
- IMPLICIT: Uses hardcoded strings and message box type 0x31 (MB_OKCANCEL | MB_ICONQUESTION)

Returns:
- true (1) if user clicked OK, false (0) if user clicked Cancel

Magic Numbers:
- 0x31: Message box type (MB_OKCANCEL | MB_ICONQUESTION)
- 0x6f920fb8: Address of "Diablo II" caption string
- 0x6f920fd8: Address of "Insert Cinematics Disc" message string
- 0x6f91d330: Address of MessageBoxA import

functions.name: InitializeDataMpqs
functions.comment:
Initialize Diablo II MPQ archives and validate expansion files.

Algorithm:
1. Load core MPQ files (D2Data, D2SFX, D2Speech, D2Delta, D2KFixup, PatchD2, D2Expansion)
2. Check if expansion is already active via GetExpansionFlag()
3. Return 1 (success) if expansion already enabled
4. Validate all core MPQ files are loaded successfully
5. If core files loaded, check expansion MPQ file via CheckExpansionMpqExists()
6. Return 1 if expansion MPQ exists and is available
7. Return 0 if core files not loaded or expansion validation failed

Parameters:
- IMPLICIT: None - function takes no parameters

Returns:
- 1 on success (expansion ready or already active)
- 0 if any core MPQ file failed to load or expansion validation failed

functions.name: CloseD2DataMpqs
functions.comment:
Closes all loaded Diablo 2 MPQ archives and sets handles to NULL.

Algorithm:
1. Iterate through each open MPQ file pointer (Data, Speech, SFX, Delta, KFixup, Expansion, Patch, and variant MPQ files)
2. Check if each MPQ pointer is non-NULL
3. If non-NULL, call close function and set pointer to NULL
4. Return with all MPQ resources released

Parameters:
- (none) - Function takes no parameters, operates on global MPQ pointers

Returns:
- void

Related Functions:
- FUN_6f9141f6 (MPQ close/cleanup function)

functions.name: GetDataFilePath
functions.comment:
Returns data file base path pointer (stub implementation).

Algorithm:
1. Clear EAX register via XOR EAX, EAX
2. Return 0 (null pointer)

Parameters:
- None (void)

Returns:
- 0: Always returns null; this is a stub function

Called By:
- LoadPaletteData, LoadOrGetUnitCof, InitItemTypesAndComponents, InitializeFontTable

Notes:
- Function appears to be a placeholder for file path retrieval
- Callers must handle the null return value appropriately

functions.name: IsCharExpansionPresent
functions.comment:
Checks if D2CHAR.MPQ expansion file is present, first in install path then in char path.

Algorithm:
1. Get installation path
2. Append d2char.mpq filename
3. Check file existence with GetFileAttributesA
4. If not found (0xffffffff), copy char path and retry
5. Return true if file not found, false if found (inverted logic)

Parameters:
- None

Returns:
- true if expansion is NOT present
- false if expansion file was found

Magic Numbers:
- 0x104: Buffer size (260 bytes for MAX_PATH)
- 0xffffffff: GetFileAttributesA INVALID_FILE_ATTRIBUTES

functions.name: InitializeMpqFiles
functions.signature: dword InitializeMpqFiles(char * szPath1, char * szPath2, dword dwFlags, int nExpansionId)
functions.comment:
Initialize MPQ file handles for D2 resources (debug, patch, music, expansion).

Algorithm:
1. Check if expansion flag is set; if so, bypass expansions
2. Check if expansion MPQ exists
3. If expansion unavailable or flag set: Load debug and music MPQs with pszPath1
4. If expansion available: Load all 5 MPQ types (debug, music, override, expansion)
5. Verify all required MPQs loaded successfully
6. On failure: Clean up and close all allocated MPQ handles

Parameters:
- pszPath1 (char*): Primary path (base game assets)
- pszPath2 (char*): Secondary path (expansion assets)
- dwFlags (dword): Load flags (priority/mode)
- nExpansionId (int): Expansion version identifier or 0 for base

Returns:
- 1 on success (all required MPQs loaded)
- 0 on failure (insufficient MPQs loaded)

functions.name: InitializeD2MpqData
functions.signature: uint InitializeD2MpqData(void * pMpqHandle, uint dwMpqPriority, int nExpansionIndex)
functions.comment:
Initializes D2 MPQ data by loading either base or expansion MPQ file.

Algorithm:
1. Check expansion flag via GetExpansionFlag()
2. Clear pMpqHandle if expansion is active
3. Load appropriate MPQ file via FUN_6f91404b based on nExpansionIndex:
   - If index=0: Load base D2VIDEO MPQ file
   - If index!=0: Load expansion D2EXPANSION MPQ file
4. Store result in g_pD2LocalMpq or g_pD2CdExpMpq

Parameters:
- pMpqHandle (void*): Placeholder buffer (cleared if expansion active)
- dwMpqPriority (uint): Priority value for MPQ loader
- nExpansionIndex (int): 0 for base, non-zero for expansion

Returns:
- 1 on successful MPQ load
- 0 if MPQ loading failed

functions.name: CloseAllMpqArchives
functions.comment:
Closes/releases all open MPQ file handles.

Algorithm:
1. Check if g_pD2PatchOptMpq handle is open (non-NULL)
2. If open, close it via CloseMpqArchive and set to NULL
3. Repeat for g_pD2DebugMpq, g_pD2LocalMpq, g_pD2OverrideMpq, g_pD2CdMpq, g_pD2CdExpMpq
4. All MPQ handles are cleared to prevent resource leaks

Parameters:
- (none)

Returns:
- void

Related Functions:
- CloseMpqArchive: MPQ handle close/cleanup function

functions.name: CreateUIElementType6
functions.signature: void * CreateUIElementType6(dword nClassId, dword nElementId, int nWidth, int nHeight, dword dwFlags, dword dwParam1, int nEventHandler, dword dwParam2, dword byFlags, int nStringId, dword dwParam3)
functions.comment:
Factory function that creates and initializes a UI element structure of type 6.

Algorithm:
1. Allocate 0x274 bytes (157 dwords) for UI element structure
2. Zero-initialize the entire structure with REP STOSD
3. Set base type field to 6 and apply bitmasked flags
4. Initialize element and class IDs, dimensions
5. Setup event handler function pointer (if provided)
6. Apply additional flags and parameters to structure fields
7. Validate and copy string resource if ID provided
8. Calculate tile dimensions from width/height with 256-unit scaling
9. Conditionally double tile count if flag 0x20 is set
10. Call initialization function FUN_6f90ea50

Parameters:
- nClassId (dword in ECX): Class/type identifier
- nElementId (dword in EDX): Element instance ID
- nWidth (int): Element width in units
- nHeight (int): Element height in units
- dwFlags (dword): Initialization flags
- dwParam1 (dword): Supplementary parameter
- nEventHandler (int): Event handler code (0=none)
- dwParam2 (dword): Additional parameter for handler
- byFlags (dword): Control flags with bit 0x20 for tile doubling
- nStringId (int): String resource ID to copy
- dwParam3 (dword): Final parameter

Returns:
- Pointer to newly allocated and initialized UI element structure (620 bytes)

functions.name: InventoryHandleType6
functions.comment:
Handles inventory type 6 processing.

Algorithm:
1. Check if item type is 6; if not, assert and exit
2. Process the item through FUN_6f90ea90

Parameters:
- pItem (int*): Pointer to item structure with type field at offset 0

Returns:
- void (asserts on invalid type)

Related: Part of inventory dispatch switch in Ordinal_10018

functions.name: IsButtonValid
functions.comment:
Validates button structure state and initialization.

Algorithm:
1. Assert button type is 6 (D2WIN_BUTTON), fail if not
2. Check if both field_2c and field_30 are non-zero
3. Return 1 if both set, 0 otherwise

Parameters:
- pButton (D2WinButton*): Pointer to button structure

Returns:
- 1 (true) if button fields field_2c and field_30 are both initialized
- 0 (false) if either field is zero or type mismatch

Note:
- Field offsets +0x2c (+44) and +0x30 (+48) represent button state flags
- These fields must be initialized for the button to be valid

functions.name: SetButtonFrameValues
functions.comment:
Sets button frame dimension values. Validates button data type before setting width/height fields.

Algorithm:
1. Verify button data structure type field equals 6 (BUTTON type)
2. Assert fails with diagnostic path/line if type mismatch, terminates execution
3. Write dwValue to button frame width field (offset 0x44)
4. Write dwValue to button frame height field (offset 0x48)

Parameters:
- pButtonData (dword*): Pointer to button structure, verified at offset 0x0
- dwValue (dword): Frame dimension value (width/height)

Returns:
- void (no return value)

Magic Numbers:
- 0x6: Expected button type constant
- 0x44 (68): Offset to frame width field
- 0x48 (72): Offset to frame height field

functions.name: InitButtonControl
functions.signature: void InitButtonControl(dword * pButton, int nType, Unicode * pszText, int nId)
functions.comment:
Initialize a button control with type, text, and identifier.

Algorithm:
1. Validate button type (must be 6)
2. Set button type field at offset 0x60
3. Set button ID at offset 0x264
4. Copy text string to button structure at offset 0x64

Parameters:
- pButton (dword*): Pointer to button structure
- nType (int): Button type value (must equal 6)
- pszText (Unicode*): Text label for button
- nId (int): Button identifier value

Returns:
- void (asserts on invalid type)

Magic Numbers:
- 0x6: Expected button type constant
- 0x60 (96): Button type field offset
- 0x64 (100): Button text field offset
- 0x264 (612): Button ID field offset

functions.name: SetButtonDataFields
functions.signature: void SetButtonDataFields(int * pBtnData, int nValue, ushort wStringId, int nState)
functions.comment:
Sets button data field values. Validates button type and configures text string and state.

Algorithm:
1. Verify button type is 6 (type check via assertion)
2. Store nValue at offset 0x18 in button structure
3. Store nState at offset 0x99 in button structure
4. Validate wStringId as valid string identifier
5. Copy string data to button text field at offset 0x19

Parameters:
- pBtnData (int*): Pointer to button data structure (must have type 6)
- nValue (int): Value to store at offset 0x18
- wStringId (ushort): String table ID to validate and copy
- nState (int): State value to store at offset 0x99

Returns:
- void (on success); aborts via FUN_6f91436d if type check fails

Magic Numbers:
- 6: Expected button type identifier
- 0x18 (24): Offset for value field
- 0x99 (153): Offset for state field
- 0x19 (25): Offset for text string field

functions.name: SetButtonFields
functions.signature: void SetButtonFields(int * pBtnData, int nParam1, int nParam2, int nParam3, int nParam4)
functions.comment:
Sets button data fields with validation.

Algorithm:
1. Validate structure type byte is 6 (button type)
2. Store nParam1 at offset 0xc
3. Store nParam2 at offset 0x10
4. Store nParam3 at offset 0x14
5. Store nParam4 at offset 0x18

Parameters:
- pBtnData: Pointer to button structure (type must = 6)
- nParam1: Value for field at offset 0xc
- nParam2: Value for field at offset 0x10
- nParam3: Value for field at offset 0x14
- nParam4: Value for field at offset 0x18

Returns:
- void

Note: Calls FUN_6f91436d(0xffffffff) if validation fails (fatal error)

functions.name: D2WIN_ButtonOnClick
functions.comment:
Invokes button click handler and callback functions.

Algorithm:
1. Verify button structure type (expect 0x6 at offset 0)
2. Call button click handler (function pointer at offset 0x24)
3. Set button state flag at offset 0x4c to 1
4. Call button callback (function pointer at offset 0x28) if present
5. Increment global counter, invoke callback with stack frame, decrement counter

Parameters:
- pButton (int*): Pointer to button structure with handlers and callbacks

Returns:
- void

Notes:
- Function does not return if button structure validation fails (fatal error)
- Global counter at 0x6f961530 tracks callback nesting depth

functions.name: SetStructFieldValue
functions.comment:
Sets a field value in a structure after validating the structure type.

Algorithm:
1. Validate that pStruct[0] == 6 (expected type marker)
2. If validation fails, assert with debug location info and exit
3. Set pStruct[0x17] = nValue

Parameters:
- pStruct (int*): Pointer to structure; pStruct[0] must equal 6
- nValue (int): Value to write to structure offset 0x5c (0x17 in array form)

Returns:
- void

Magic Numbers:
- 6: Expected structure type marker at pStruct[0]
- 0x5c (92): Target field offset for value assignment

functions.name: OnButtonPressed
functions.comment:
Validates and invokes button press callback if state conditions are met.

Algorithm:
1. Check if button type is 0x6
2. Verify button flags match required bit masks
3. Check button state fields (0x44, 0x48) are zero
4. Validate nDelta against flag bits (0x40): positive with bit 0x8, negative with bit 0x10
5. Clear 28-byte local array via REP STOSD
6. Increment global counter DAT_6f961530
7. Call button callback at offset 0x34 with pBtn
8. Decrement global counter and return 0

Parameters:
- pBtn (int*): Button structure pointer
- nDelta (int): Delta value (positive/negative)

Returns:
- 0 always

Magic Numbers:
- 0x6: Button type constant
- 0x40: Flags field offset in structure
- 0x44, 0x48: State field offsets

functions.name: SetButtonField
functions.comment:
Assigns a value to a button structure field at a fixed offset.

Validates the button structure type and sets field at offset 0x270 to the
provided value. Terminates execution if structure type validation fails.

Algorithm:
1. Check if structure type field (offset 0) equals 6
2. If type mismatch, call FogAssert with error details and abort
3. Write nValue to button field at offset 0x270 (0x9c * 4 bytes)
4. Return to caller

Parameters:
- pBtn (int*): Button/window structure pointer (ECX in __fastcall)
- nValue (int): Value to store in button field at offset 0x270

Returns:
- void: Function never returns on type validation failure (calls abort)
- void: Normal return after successful field assignment

Magic Numbers:
- 6: Expected button structure type indicator
- 0x270: Field offset in button structure (588 bytes, or 0x9c dwords)
- 0x100: Assertion line number (256)

functions.name: RenderButtonType6
functions.comment: Setting prototype: int RenderButtonType6(void *pButton)

functions.name: ProcessButtonClick
functions.comment:
Processes button click event and invokes registered callback if conditions are met.

Algorithm:
1. Validate button type is 6 (button assertion)
2. Check button state flags against bitmask conditions
3. If both conditions met, toggle or set button flags based on mode
4. Invoke button's registered callback if depth allows

Parameters:
- pBtnData (int*): Pointer to button data array [0] = pointer to button info structure

Returns:
- 1 if button callback executed, 0 if conditions not met

functions.name: FireButtonCallback
functions.comment:
Fires button callback if conditions are met.

Algorithm:
1. Validate button type is 6 (assert if not)
2. Set button state bits using gdwBitMasks
3. Check if button should fire based on state and mask flags
4. If conditions met and callback exists, invoke callback with button pointer
5. Clear fired state flag
6. Return callback result or 0

Parameters:
- pButton (int*): Pointer to button structure

Returns:
- Result from button callback, or 0 if callback not invoked

Magic Numbers:
- 6: Expected button type value
- 0x10, 0x11, 0x12, 0xd: Button structure offsets
- gdwBitMasks_exref: Global bit mask table

functions.name: InitializeVersionInfo
functions.comment:
Initializes or validates version information state.

Algorithm:
1. Returns a success indicator (1)
2. Called from program entry point initialization sequence

Parameters:
- None

Returns:
- 1 on success (always returns 1)

functions.name: CreateUIElementType1
functions.signature: void CreateUIElementType1(dword dwX, dword dwY, dword dwType, dword dwWidth, dword dwHeight, dword dwBgColor, dword dwFlags, dword dwFgColor, dword dwUnknown, dword dwExFlags, dword * pdwInitData)
functions.comment:
Create UI element of type 1. Allocates and initializes a 0x284-byte structure with display parameters.

Algorithm:
1. Allocate 0x284 bytes via FogMemAlloc
2. Zero-initialize entire structure (161 dwords)
3. Set type field to 1
4. Initialize display fields: position (dwX, dwY), dimensions, colors
5. Set function pointers for rendering based on dwFlags bit 3
6. Copy initial data from pdwInitData if provided
7. Call initialization function FUN_6f90ea50

Parameters:
- dwX: X coordinate position
- dwY: Y coordinate position
- dwType: Element type (stored but semantic type TBD)
- dwWidth: Width in pixels
- dwHeight: Height in pixels
- dwBgColor: Background color value
- dwFlags: Control flags (bit 3 selects render function)
- dwFgColor: Foreground color value
- dwUnknown: Purpose unclear, stored at offset 0xd*4
- dwExFlags: Extended flags (stored at offset 0x98*4)
- pdwInitData: Optional init data (2 dwords copied to offset 0x9c/0x9d)

Returns:
- Pointer to allocated UI element structure (0x284 bytes)

Magic Numbers:
- 0x284 (644): Structure size in bytes
- 0xa1 (161): Number of dwords to zero-initialize
- 0x100: Default value for field at offset 0x12*4
- 0xffffffff: Initialization value for field at offset 0x15*4

functions.name: InventoryHandleType1
functions.comment:
Handles inventory type 1 processing with validation.

Algorithm:
1. Validates pInventoryItem is not NULL (asserts if NULL)
2. Validates first dword of inventory item equals 1 (asserts if not)
3. Calls FUN_6f90ea90 to process the inventory item

Parameters:
- pInventoryItem (int*): Pointer to inventory item structure, must point to valid data with first dword == 1

Returns:
- void

Note: Called from inventory dispatch switch when item type is 1. Terminates via assertion if validations fail.

functions.name: SetEditFieldValue
functions.comment:
Sets a value in an edit field data structure after validating the data pointer and type.

Algorithm:
1. Validate that pEditData is not NULL
2. Validate that pEditData[0] == 1 (type check)
3. Set pEditData[0x9a] = nValue

Parameters:
- pEditData (int*): Pointer to edit field data structure, must be non-NULL
- nValue (int): Value to store at offset 0x9a in the edit field structure

Returns:
- void

Magic Numbers:
- 0x9a (154): Offset in edit field structure where value is stored
- 1: Expected type value at structure offset 0

functions.name: SetEditDataField9B
functions.comment:
Sets field at offset 0x9b (155) in EditData structure.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pEditData is not NULL (assert fails otherwise)
2. Validate pEditData->eType equals D2WIN_EDITBOX (1)
3. Store nValue to pEditData[0x9b]

Parameters:
- pEditData (EditData*): Pointer to edit box control data
- nValue (int): Value to store at offset 0x9b

Returns:
- void (asserts on invalid input)

functions.name: InitEditBoxSelection
functions.comment:
Initializes edit box selection state to no selection.

Algorithm:
1. Assert pEditData is not NULL
2. Assert pEditData->eType equals 1 (D2WIN_EDITBOX type)
3. Set nSelectionStart (offset 0x54) to -1 (no selection)
4. Set nSelectionEnd (offset 0x58) to 0

Parameters:
- pEditData (int*): Pointer to edit box data structure

Returns:
- void (aborts on validation failure)

Magic Numbers:
- 0x15 (21): Selection start field index (offset 0x54)
- 0x16 (22): Selection end field index (offset 0x58)
- -1: No active selection marker

functions.name: InitializeScreenshotConfig
functions.comment:
Initializes screenshot configuration by clearing image buffer and calculating string length.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pConfig pointer is non-null (calls FogAssert if null)
2. Validate type field at offset 0x0 equals 1 (calls FogAssert if not)
3. Clear image buffer field at offset 0x54
4. Get length of image path string at offset 0x5c
5. Store calculated length at offset 0x58
6. Return void

Parameters:
- pConfig (ScreenshotConfig*): Pointer to screenshot configuration structure to initialize

Returns:
- void (does not return on validation failure - calls FogAssert which terminates)

functions.name: EditBoxProcessClipboardInput
functions.comment:
Processes clipboard text input for edit control with character encoding conversion.

Algorithm:
1. Validates input parameter (ptEditData) and character mode (nCharMode)
2. Checks enabled state via flags (0x20, 0x8, 0x10, 0x4)
3. Handles callback invocation if mode is 0x9 and callback flag set
4. Validates character via Ordinal_10128 (character validity check)
5. Swaps selection if selection exists and mode not 0x1, 0x3, 0x18
6. Processes specific character modes: 0x1 (select all), 0xd/0xe (newline), 0x3 (copy), 0x16 (paste), 0x18 (delete)
7. For paste (0x16): Retrieves clipboard, filters CR/LF if mode bit 0x8 unset, concatenates text
8. For draw mode (bit 0x8): Calculates text rendering dimensions with line wrapping
9. Updates edit control text buffer and cursor position
10. Invokes change callback if set

Parameters:
- pEditData (void*): Pointer to ptEditData control structure (offset-based field access)
- nCharMode (Unicode): Character mode/command (0x1=select-all, 0x3=copy, 0x16=paste, 0x18=delete, 0xd/0xe=newline)

Returns:
- 0 on failure or early exit (validation failed, callback returned 0, no clipboard)
- 1 on success (after processing mode and updating edit control)

Magic Numbers:
- 0x268: Offset to callback function pointer in ptEditData
- 0x25c: Offset to character position (cursor) in ptEditData
- 0x54/0x58: Selection start/end positions in ptEditData
- 0x260: Offset to mode flags (0x20=enable input, 0x8=wrap-render, 0x10=special flag, 0x4=callback flag)
- 0x5c: Offset to text buffer pointer in ptEditData
- 0x48: Maximum text length in ptEditData
- 0x44/0x40/0x14/0x18: Layout dimensions for text rendering
- 0x6f960b90: Global clipboard memory handle
- 0x6f960988: Global paste buffer (0x200 bytes)

functions.name: SwapEditBoxSelection
functions.comment:
Swaps text between edit box selection and clipboard/buffer.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input pointer and type flag
2. Initialize two Unicode string buffers (local_400, aUStack_200)
3. Calculate min/max of selection range bounds
4. Copy selection range to local_400
5. Copy replacement text to aUStack_200
6. Concatenate and update edit box text
7. Update selection length field

Parameters:
- pEditData (int*): Edit box control data structure

Returns:
- void

Related: Uses Unicode string operations (strncpy, strcpy, strcat, strlen)

functions.name: EditBoxKeyHandler
functions.comment:
Processes keyboard input for edit box control, handling text insertion, deletion, navigation, selection, and callback invocation.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input: Ensure pEditBox is non-null and type==1
2. Check enabled state: Verify edit box is enabled via gdwBitMasks_exref flags
3. Calculate text pointer: pEditBox + pEditBox[0x97]*2 + 0x5C (text buffer)
4. Handle key by type:
   - Backspace/Delete: Remove selection or preceding character
   - Tab: Navigate to next/previous sibling edit box
   - Enter: Invoke user callback or close if not multi-line
   - Escape: Invoke close callback
   - Navigation (Home/End/PgUp/PgDn): Move cursor
   - Arrow keys: Adjust selection or cursor position
5. Update cursor offset (pEditBox[0x97]) relative to text pointer
6. Call OnChange callback if text was modified (nEdited==1)
7. Return 1 if handled (or multi-line+Enter), 0 if should propagate

Parameters:
- pEditBox (int*): Edit box structure [ECX], contains:
  - [0x0]: Type (must be 1)
  - [0x2]: Flags (validated against gdwBitMasks_exref)
  - [0x54]: Selection start (cursor position, -1=none)
  - [0x58]: Selection end
  - [0x97]: Text offset (in Unicode chars, offset from base)
  - [0x98]: Edit flags (0x8=accept special chars like +)
  - [0x99]: OnChange callback (called after text change)
  - [0x9A]: OnValidate callback (returns 0 to reject key)
  - [0x9B]: OnClose callback
  - [0x9E]: Previous sibling pointer
  - [0x9F]: Next sibling pointer
  - [0x25C]: Text length or offset (variable usage)
- cKeyCode (char [DL]): Keyboard character code

Returns:
- 1: Key handled successfully, edit box updated or callback invoked
- 0: Key rejected or invalid state (non-multi-line + non-special-key)

Special Cases:
- Backspace (0x08): Delete selection or previous char; block if no selection+cursor==0
- Delete (0x2E): Delete selection or next char
- Tab (0x09): Tab key with Shift traverses prev/next edit boxes
- Enter (0x0D): Invoke OnChange callback; return based on (flags & 0x2)
- Escape (0x1B): Invoke OnClose callback, always return 1
- Shift+Arrows: Extend selection; plain arrows move cursor only

functions.name: SetEditControlValue

Converts an 8-bit character string to Unicode and sets EditData.

functions.name: EditData_SetString
functions.comment:
Sets a Unicode string value in an EditData structure with validation and callback.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pEditData pointer is non-null and type field equals 1
2. Obtain string length via Unicode::strlen(pwszValue)
3. If length is 0, zero out the string buffer at offset 0x17
4. If length > 0, copy pwszValue to offset 0x17 via Unicode::strcpy()
5. Store string length at offset 0x97
6. Invoke post-processing function FUN_6f90b4a0 (likely updates display)
7. Check for callback at offset 0x9b and invoke if present (with param 0)
8. Return 1 on success

Parameters:

Returns:
- 1 on success

functions.name: D2Win_GetEditBoxChild

Extract child window pointer from D2Win edit control structure.

functions.name: LinkDoubleLinkedListNodes

Links two nodes in a bidirectional list by updating their cross-pointers.

2. Validate that pNextNode is non-NULL and contains type marker (1)
3. Set pPrevNode[0x9e] = pNextNode (forward link)
4. Set pNextNode[0x9f] = pPrevNode (backward link)

- void
