- 0x9f (159): Backward link offset in node structure
- 1: Type validation marker value

functions.name: RenderEditBoxControl
functions.comment:
Render callback for edit box UI controls. Draws text content with cursor and selection highlighting.

Source: D2WinEditBox.cpp

Classification: Callback/Handler - invoked as render function pointer from UI element structure

Algorithm:
1. Validate pEditData pointer and type field (must be D2WIN_EDITBOX = 1)
2. Check visibility flags via gdwBitMasks_exref bits 0 and 8
3. If not in game state, clear active selection state (offset 0xa0)
4. If selection active, send WM_LBUTTONDOWN message to ProcessEditBoxMessage
5. Initialize 600-byte Unicode display buffer (300 wchars)
6. If flags field set, clear EditData structure and call GfxInterfaceCall84 for background
7. Set active font from pEditData[0x9c]
8. Calculate render position: X = offset 0x10 + offset 0x03, Y = (0x11 - 0x06) + 16 + offset 0x04
9. Copy visible text substring from pEditData text buffer (offsets 0x13 to 0x14) to display buffer
10. If password mask flag (offset 0x98 bit 0) set, replace text with g_wLineSeparator characters
11. Validate type field again (assertion)
12. If no selection or collapsed selection (0x15 == -1 or 0x15 == 0x16):
    - Render full text with RenderUnicodeTextWithLineHeight using color from offset 0x9d
13. Else (active selection):
    - Find selection color via FindPaletteIndexForColor(0x40, 0x40, 0x40) for gray
    - Split text into 3 parts: before selection, selected text, after selection
    - Calculate pixel positions for each segment via GetUnicodeStringDimensions
    - Render pre-selection text normally
    - Render selected text with RenderTextWithShadow (highlighted)
    - Render post-selection text normally
14. Check if this control has input focus via GetLastInputTime
15. If focused and cursor blink phase active (GetTickCount / 250 is odd):
    - Calculate cursor X position via CalcStringCharWidthSum
    - Render cursor character (g_wLineEndMarker) at cursor position
16. Return 1 (success)

Parameters:
- pEditData (int*, ECX via __fastcall): Pointer to edit box control structure (0x284 bytes)

Returns:
- 1: Always returns success

Edit Box Structure Layout (offsets as dword indices):
Offset | Field | Description
0x00   | eType | Control type (1 = D2WIN_EDITBOX)
0x01   | dwFlags | State flags
0x02   | dwVisibility | Visibility bitmask (checked against gdwBitMasks_exref)
0x03   | nX | X position
0x04   | nY | Y position
0x06   | nWidth | Control width
0x10   | nXOffset | X render offset
0x11   | nYOffset | Y render offset
0x13   | nVisibleStart | First visible character index
0x14   | nVisibleEnd | Last visible character index
0x15   | nSelStart | Selection start (-1 if none)
0x16   | nSelEnd | Selection end
0x17   | wszText | Unicode text buffer (at byte offset 0x5c)
0x97   | nCursorPos | Cursor character position
0x98   | dwExFlags | Extended flags (bit 0 = password mask)
0x9c   | nFontId | Active font identifier
0x9d   | dwTextColor | Text color value
0xa0   | dwActiveState | Active/dragging state

Magic Numbers:
- 0xfa (250): Cursor blink period divisor in milliseconds
- 0x40, 0x40, 0x40: Selection highlight color (gray RGB)
- 0x5c (92): Byte offset to text buffer within structure
- 300: Display buffer size in Unicode characters

Related Functions:
- ProcessEditBoxMessage: Handles input events for this control
- CreateUIElementType1: Creates edit box and assigns this as render callback
- EditBoxHandleSelectionWrapper: Alternative handler for extended flags bit 3

functions.name: EditBoxCalcTextLayout
functions.signature: void EditBoxCalcTextLayout(int * pEditData, int * pnCursorX, int * pnCursorY)
functions.comment:
Calculate text layout and cursor position for edit box with text wrapping support.

Algorithm:
1. Validate edit data structure and initialize local Unicode buffers
2. Retrieve glyph width and current text dimensions from edit data
3. Process text line by line, measuring width with unicode2Win and Ordinal_10122
4. Track cursor position (X, Y) and detect wrapping boundaries
5. Handle carriage return and newline characters for line breaks
6. Return calculated cursor position via output parameters

Parameters:
- pEditData (int*): Pointer to EditBox structure containing text, dimensions, and settings (offset +0x17=text, +0x97=cursor offset)
- pnCursorX (int*): Output cursor X position
- pnCursorY (int*): Output cursor Y position

Returns:
- void (results written to pnCursorX and pnCursorY)

Magic Numbers:
- 0x258 (600): Unicode buffer size for full text
- 0x100 (256): Buffer size for line text conversion
- 0x17 (23): Text pointer offset in EditBox structure
- 0x97 (151): Cursor offset in EditBox structure
- 0x9c: Font/glyph reference offset
- 0x10, 0x11: Width/height field offsets

functions.name: ProcessEditBoxMessage
functions.comment:
Processes window messages for edit box controls (WM_LBUTTONDOWN, WM_KEYDOWN, etc).

Algorithm:
1. Validate edit box structure type and state flags
2. Calculate visible text bounds based on screen dimensions and control position
3. Determine if cursor position is within valid text area (fInBounds)
4. Check for double-click (time < 300ms) on same control for fast selection
5. Handle shift+click for text selection or cursor movement by character
6. Process keyboard input (GetKeyState for shift modifier)
7. Invoke control callback function if defined
8. Cache last edited control and tick count for double-click detection

Parameters:
- pEditData (EditData*): Pointer to edit box data structure containing position, size, text buffer, cursor state
- dwMessage (uint): Message type (0x201 = WM_LBUTTONDOWN, others from Windows API)

Returns:
- Result from control callback (if defined), 0 if no callback

Structure Layout (EditData offsets):
- 0x00: eType (1 = EDITBOX)
- 0x02: dwFlags (state and capability flags)
- 0x03-0x0d: Position/size fields (nX, nY, nWidth, nHeight, etc.)
- 0x10: nLineHeight
- 0x13: nCursorPos (character position)
- 0x15-0x16: nSelStart, nSelEnd (selection range)
- 0x97: dwCursorX (pixel position from line start)
- 0x9c: hFocus (window focus handle)
- 0xa0: dwState (active/focus state)
- 0x0d: pfnCallback (callback function pointer)

Related: Ordinal_10012 (render), Ordinal_10122 (char width), Ordinal_10127 (focus)

functions.name: EditBoxHandleSelection
functions.signature: uint EditBoxHandleSelection(uint * pEditBox, int nStartX, int nStartY)
functions.comment:
Processes text selection in edit box with mouse coordinates validation and text width measurement.

Algorithm:
1. Validate edit box structure pointer and type flags
2. Calculate clamped selection bounds from input coordinates and structure limits
3. Parse text line-by-line, measuring width with Unicode conversion
4. Find character position within visible width using metric calculations
5. Update selection start/end fields if Shift key pressed
6. Invoke callback handler if present (field at offset 0x34)

Parameters:
- pEditBox (uint *): Pointer to edit box structure (in ECX)
- nStartX (int): X coordinate for selection (in EDX)
- nStartY (int): Y coordinate for selection (on stack)

Returns:
- uint: Result from callback invocation, or 0 if no callback present

Related Functions:
- EditBoxKeyHandler: Caller that processes keyboard input
- Ordinal_10012 through Ordinal_10127: Font/text measurement and Unicode utilities

functions.name: EditBoxHandleSelectionWrapper
functions.comment:
Wrapper for EditBoxHandleSelection with screen-relative coordinate calculation.

Classification: Thunk/Wrapper - translates screen coordinates to edit box local coordinates

Algorithm:
1. Dereference pEditBox to get edit data pointer (pnEditData)
2. Assert pnEditData is non-NULL
3. Assert edit data type field equals 1 (EDITBOX type)
4. Calculate Y coordinate: g_nScreenHeight - pnEditData[0x10] - pnEditData[3]
   (screen height minus line height minus Y position)
5. Calculate X coordinate: pnEditData[6] - pnEditData[0x11] - pnEditData[4] + g_nScreenWidth
   (width minus left margin minus X position plus screen width)
6. Call EditBoxHandleSelection(pEditBox, nStartX, nStartY)

Parameters:
- pEditBox (dword *): Pointer to edit box wrapper containing edit data pointer at offset 0

Returns:
- void (no return value)

Structure Offsets (pnEditData array):
- [0x00]: eType - element type (1 = EDITBOX)
- [0x03]: nX - X position
- [0x04]: nY - Y position
- [0x06]: nWidth - total width
- [0x10]: nLineHeight - text line height
- [0x11]: nLeftMargin - left margin offset

Related Functions:
- EditBoxHandleSelection: Main selection handler this wrapper calls
- ProcessEditBoxMessage: Alternative message handler (non-wrapper version)
- CreateUIElementType1: Creates edit boxes, stores this function at pObject[9]

Usage Context:
Stored as callback at pObject[9] when CreateUIElementType1 is called with dwExFlags bit 3 set.
Provides simplified coordinate transformation compared to ProcessEditBoxMessage.

functions.name: IsCharDigit
functions.signature: int IsCharDigit(int nUnused1, int nUnused2, char * szChar)
functions.comment:
Checks if a character is a decimal digit (0-9).

Algorithm:
1. Load character from szChar pointer
2. Compare with ASCII '0' (0x30)
3. If less than '0', return 0
4. Compare with ASCII '9' (0x39)
5. If greater than '9', return 0
6. Return 1 if within range

Parameters:
- nUnused1 (int): Unused, passed for API compatibility
- nUnused2 (int): Unused, passed for API compatibility
- szChar (char*): Pointer to character to test

Returns:
- 1 if character is digit (0-9), 0 otherwise

Magic Numbers:
- 0x30 (48): ASCII '0'
- 0x39 (57): ASCII '9'

functions.name: IsCharAlpha
functions.signature: bool IsCharAlpha(uint dwUnused1, uint dwUnused2, char * szChar)
functions.comment:
Check if first character of string is alphabetic.

Algorithm:
1. Load first character from string pointer szChar
2. Check if character >= 'a' AND character <= 'z' (lowercase letter)
3. Check if character >= 'A' AND character <= 'Z' (uppercase letter)
4. Return 1 if either condition true, 0 if not alphabetic

Parameters:
- dwUnused1: Unused parameter (reserved, no functionality)
- dwUnused2: Unused parameter (reserved, no functionality)
- szChar (char*): Pointer to string/character to test

Returns:
- 1 if first character is alphabetic (a-z or A-Z)
- 0 if first character is not alphabetic

functions.name: EditBoxValidateInsert
functions.comment:
Validates and adjusts cursor position for inserting text into edit box while respecting width constraints.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate available width by subtracting used bytes from maximum allowed width
2. Convert input string to Unicode (if in binary mode) or copy directly
3. Measure width of converted/copied string and line ending
4. Determine if text fits without overflow
5. If fits, clear selection and set end position
6. If text overflow occurs, adjust cursor position via binary search:
   - When expanding selection: move backward from current position while text width < available
   - When shrinking selection: move forward from current position while text width < available
   - When within selection: search from current position toward limits

Parameters:
- pEditBox (ECX): Pointer to EditBoxData structure containing buffer, positions, and constraints

Returns:
- void

Magic Numbers:
- 0x5c: Offset of string buffer in EditBoxData
- 0x25c: Offset of selection end in EditBoxData
- 0x260: Offset of edit mode flags (bit 0 = binary mode)
- 300: Initial Unicode string capacity on stack
- 0x270: Offset for cleanup call

Related: EditData_SetString, ProcessEditBoxMessage, EditBoxKeyHandler

functions.name: InitStringBufferUnicode
functions.comment:
Initializes the global Unicode string buffer with 1024 elements.

Classification: Initialization function

Algorithm:
1. Set ESI to point to g_pszStringBuffer (0x6F960CC8)
2. Set loop counter EDI to 0x400 (1024)
3. Loop: Call Unicode::_default_constructor_closure_ via [0x6F91D05C]
4. Increment ESI by 2 (sizeof wchar_t)
5. Decrement EDI and loop until zero
6. Restore registers and return

Parameters: None

Returns: void

Memory Model:
- Modifies: g_pszStringBuffer (2048 bytes = 1024 wide chars)
- Preserves: ESI, EDI (saved/restored)

Related Globals:
- g_pszStringBuffer @ 0x6F960CC8: Unicode buffer being initialized
- PTR_default_constructor_closure @ 0x6F91D05C: Unicode element initializer

- Actual code spans 0x6f90b700 to 0x6f90b71c (29 bytes)

  6f90b71c: RET

functions.name: InitColorCodeToUnicode
functions.comment:
Converts color code characters to Unicode format.

functions.name: InitializeAnimationCodeStrings
functions.comment:
Initializes the global Unicode animation code string array.

Called during D2Win initialization to set up two Unicode string objects
at g_wsAnimationCode (0x6f9614dc) for animation sequence codes.

Algorithm:
1. Load pointer to g_wsAnimationCode global array
2. Set loop counter to 2 (two Unicode objects to initialize)
3. For each iteration:
   a. Call Unicode::_default_constructor_closure_ on current object
   b. Advance pointer by 2 bytes to next Unicode object
   c. Decrement counter
4. Loop until counter reaches 0
5. Return

Parameters:
None - void function

Returns:
void - No return value

Classification: Initialization function - sets up Unicode string state

Memory Model:
- Modifies: g_wsAnimationCode[2] - two Unicode objects initialized
- No allocations - operates on pre-allocated global storage
- Called once during module initialization

Cross-References:

functions.name: InitializeLocaleFontResources
functions.comment:
Initialize locale-specific UI and display data tables based on language ID.

1. Get system locale ID via GetLanguageLocaleId()
2. Initialize global palette and rendering constants per locale
3. Switch on locale ID to select appropriate string tables
4. Copy locale-specific font/image paths to working buffers
5. Load CEL images for fonts and monster indicators
6. Clear 0x200 dword buffer for rendering cache
7. Copy locale-specific data strings and convert to Unicode

Parameters:
- IMPLICIT: EBX contains context pointer

Returns:
- void

Magic Numbers:
- 0x10, 0x11, 0xe, 0xf (palette indices per locale)
- 0x200 (512 dwords = 2KB buffer for rendering cache)
- 0x4f (80 chars, sizeof font path buffer)

functions.name: GetFontPath
functions.signature: void GetFontPath(int nFontId, char * szOutputBuffer, int nBufferSize)
functions.comment:
Constructs the full font file path based on font ID and locale.

Algorithm:
1. Create temporary buffer for full path using format string
2. Calculate string length of intermediate result
3. Validate buffer size against required space
4. Select appropriate font pointer based on font ID and locale
5. Format final output path with selected font data

Parameters:
- nFontId (int): Font identifier index (0-12, special case 0xd)
- szOutputBuffer (char*): Output buffer for full path string
- nBufferSize (int): Size of output buffer

Returns:
- void (modifies szOutputBuffer in-place)

functions.name: InitializeFontTable
functions.comment:
Initialize font table entry by creating a font handle for the specified font index.

Algorithm:
1. Build full path string using wsprintfA with base path and flags
2. Validate string length doesn't exceed 0x4e (78 bytes)
3. Select font table based on game mode (in-game chat vs normal)
4. Format label string with path, table pointer, and font pointer
5. Release any existing allocation for this font index
6. Create new font handle via FUN_6f913fa2
7. Store handle in font heap and data pointer arrays

Parameters:
- nFontIndex (ECX): Font index in array (0-based)

Returns:
- void (results stored in g_pFontHeap and g_pFontDataPtrs arrays)

Related:
- g_pFontHeap: Array of font handles
- g_bGameMode: Flag indicating in-game chat mode (0x0d triggers chat font)
- ReleasePoolAllocation: Frees existing allocation before recreating

functions.name: ReleaseFontHeapResources
functions.comment:
Releases all cached CelFile and pool allocation resources.

Algorithm:
1. Load pointer to resource entry array from g_pFontHeap
2. Test CelFile handle at current offset minus 4 bytes (previous entry field)
3. Call ReleaseCelFile if handle is non-NULL to release CelFile resources
4. Clear the released CelFile handle to NULL
5. Test pool allocation handle at current offset
6. Call ReleasePoolAllocation if handle is non-NULL with size parameter 0x134
7. Clear the released pool allocation handle to NULL
8. Increment pointer by stride of 0x14 bytes (5 dwords) to next entry
9. Compare pointer against boundary address 0x6f960cb4
10. Loop back to step 2 until all entries processed
11. Load and release the master CelFile handle from g_dwDefaultCelIndex
12. Clear master CelFile handle to NULL

Parameters:
  IMPLICIT g_pFontHeap: Global array of resource entries to be released
  IMPLICIT g_dwDefaultCelIndex: Global master CelFile handle to be released

Returns:
  void: Function returns with no value

Special Cases:
  - Entry array uses stride of 0x14 (20) bytes = 5 dwords per entry
  - CelFile handle stored at offset -4 from current position (previous field)
  - Pool allocation size hardcoded as 0x134 (308) bytes
  - Array boundary check at address 0x6f960cb4 determines iteration count

functions.name: SetActiveFont
functions.comment:
Sets the active font and manages the font cache, loading new resources on demand.

Algorithm:
1. Store current font index, update time cache
2. If font changed, load new font CEL image if not cached
3. Initialize font table for newly loaded fonts
4. Periodically scan cache and release unused fonts (>240ms idle)
5. Update global font pointer and rendering callback

Parameters:
- nFontId (int): Font ID to activate (0-0xd)

Returns:
- int: Previous font ID value

Magic Numbers:
- 0x4f (79): Max font path length
- 0x14 (20): Font cache entry stride (5 DWORDs)
- 0xf0 (240): Idle threshold (ms) for releasing fonts
- 0x258 (600): Scan interval (ms) for cache cleanup

functions.name: GetCharacterGlyphData
functions.comment: Setting prototype: int * GetCharacterGlyphData(ushort wCharCode)

functions.name: SearchGlyphDataBinary
functions.comment:
Binary search for character glyph data in East Asian font tables.

Used as g_pfnValueProcessor callback for East Asian locales (Chinese, Japanese,
Korean) and font ID 0xd. Unlike GetCharacterGlyphData which uses direct array
indexing for ASCII fonts, this performs binary search through sorted Unicode
glyph tables containing thousands of entries.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize search bounds: low=0, high=(glyph count - 1)
2. Loop with iteration limit (max 1001 iterations for safety)
3. Calculate mid index, compare character codes
4. If match found, return pointer to glyph entry
5. Adjust bounds: if target < mid, search lower half; else upper half
6. If not found, return pointer to default glyph at offset 0x1b2 (entry 31)

Parameters:
- wCharCode (ushort via CX): Unicode character code to look up

Returns:
- int *: Pointer to 14-byte glyph data entry in font table
         Returns default glyph (offset 0x1b2) if not found

Magic Numbers:
- 0x14 (20): Font cache entry stride (5 DWORDs per font slot)
- 0xe (14): Glyph entry size in bytes
- 0x3e9 (1001): Maximum search iterations (safety limit)
- 0x1b2 (434): Offset to default/fallback glyph entry (31 * 14)
- +8: Offset to glyph count field in font header

Globals Referenced:
- g_nCurrentFontIndex: Currently active font slot index
- g_pFontHandles: Font header pointers array (glyph count at +8)
- g_pFontDataPtrs: Font glyph data pointers array

Related Functions:
- GetCharacterGlyphData: Direct lookup for ASCII/Western fonts
- SetActiveFont: Sets g_pfnValueProcessor to this or GetCharacterGlyphData

functions.name: MeasureTextWidthWithEscapes
functions.comment:
Scans and validates a ushort array, accumulating results from matched patterns.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize sum (nSum) and index (nIdx) to 0
2. Return 0 immediately if input array pointer is null
3. Set position counter (nPos) to 3
4. Loop through array until null terminator:
   - Return accumulated sum if current index exceeds nLimit
   - If value equals 0x0A (newline), skip and advance all counters
   - Otherwise validate: value must be 0xFF followed by two digits (0x30-0x36)
   - If validation fails, call g_pfnValueProcessor and add byte at offset +3 to sum
   - Advance array pointer, index, and position counters appropriately
5. Return accumulated sum

Parameters:
- pData (ushort*): Pointer to null-terminated ushort array to process
- nLimit (int): Maximum index/position limit for array traversal

Returns:
- int: Accumulated sum based on matched pattern conversions from g_pfnValueProcessor

functions.name: CalcStringCharWidthSum
functions.comment:
Calculates total character width for a string up to a maximum length.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize nTotalWidth and loop counter nIndex to 0
2. Load first character from pwString array
3. Check if character is null (0) or loop limit reached - if so, exit loop
4. For each character, if not newline (0x0A), call DAT_6f9614e4 callback
5. Callback returns character-specific width info at offset +3
6. Accumulate all non-newline character widths into nTotalWidth
7. Advance to next character in array, increment loop counter
8. Return accumulated nTotalWidth sum

Parameters:
- pwString (short*): Null-terminated array of character codes to measure
- nMaxLength (int): Maximum number of characters to process

Returns:
- Total character width sum as int, 0 if empty string

functions.name: SumCharacterValues
functions.comment:
Sums character values from a Unicode string.

Algorithm:
1. Get string length via Unicode::strlen()
2. Iterate through each character in the string
3. Skip newline characters (0x000A)
4. For each other character, call g_pfnValueProcessor() to get character value
5. Add the low byte (offset +3) of the returned value to the running sum
6. Return total sum

Parameters:
- lpwszText (Unicode*): Pointer to null-terminated Unicode string

Returns:
- Sum of character values (excluding newlines)

Related Functions:
- g_pfnValueProcessor: Function pointer used to process each character
- Unicode::strlen: String length calculation

functions.name: GetCurrentFontProperty
functions.comment:
Returns a property byte from the current font handle structure.

Algorithm:
1. Load current font handle index from g_nCurrentFontIndex
2. Calculate entry offset using index * 0x14 (20-byte stride)
3. Load font structure pointer from table
4. Extract and return byte value at offset +0xa

Parameters:
- IMPLICIT: g_pFontHandles (font handle array)
- IMPLICIT: g_nCurrentFontIndex (current font index)

Returns:
- byte: Property value from font handle at offset +0xa

Magic Numbers:
- 0x14 (20): Font handle entry stride
- 0xa (10): Property byte offset in structure

functions.name: RenderCelShadedText
functions.signature: void RenderCelShadedText(Unicode * pszString, uint nX, int nY, undefined4 nMinVal, int nMaxVal, int param_6)
functions.comment:
Renders text with cel-shaded character animations, parsing escape codes.

Algorithm:
1. Validate nMaxVal >= 0 (max pixel count)
2. Initialize CEL file cache (aCStack_48) to zero
3. Iterate through Unicode string characters
4. On 0xFF escape: identify code type (color 'a'/'b' or animation 'v')
5. On LF (0x0A): apply line height, advance Y position
6. For normal glyphs: lookup CEL data, validate width bounds
7. Render via Ordinal_10074, advance X position

Parameters:
- pszString (Unicode*): Unicode string with embedded escape codes
- nX (int): X starting position in pixels
- nY (int): Y starting position in pixels
- nMinVal (int): Minimum allowed pixel width
- nMaxVal (int): Maximum allowed pixel width (-1 = unlimited)

Returns:
- void

functions.name: ProcessUnicodeTextWithFormatting
functions.signature: void ProcessUnicodeTextWithFormatting(ushort * pszText, int nX, int nY, int nCharIndex, int nMaxWidth, int nFontIndex)
functions.comment:
Processes Unicode text with special character formatting and font rendering.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize output buffer (18 dwords)
2. Iterate through Unicode string characters
3. For each character, check if it's escape sequence (0xFF) or newline (0x0A)
4. Handle escape sequences via font processor callback
5. Accumulate rendered dimensions (width, height)

Parameters:
- pszText (Unicode*): Input Unicode string to process
- nX (int): Starting X position
- nY (int): Starting Y position
- nCharIndex (int): Character index parameter
- nMaxWidth (int): Maximum width limit or baseline width
- nFontIndex (int): Font index for rendering

Returns:
- void (modifies output buffer and updates coordinates)

Magic Numbers:
- 0xFF: Escape sequence marker
- 0x100: Character type boundary
- 0x30: Digit character offset ('0')
- 0x0C: Maximum digit value threshold
- 0x0A: Newline character code
- 0x14: Font handle structure stride
- 0x10: Font advance scaling factor (divide by 16)

functions.name: RenderWrappedUnicodeText
functions.comment:
Renders Unicode text with dynamic line wrapping based on width and height constraints.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize with current font index and get text length via Unicode::strlen
2. Calculate line count by counting newline characters (0x0a) in string
3. Compute total text height based on character metrics and line count
4. Check if text fits in available space, break if insufficient height
5. Conditionally set font for alignment (mode 1 vs 6) via Ordinal_10127
6. Calculate horizontal position based on alignment mode and available width
7. Compute scaled height and effect offset for rendering
8. If effect enabled: render effect layer with scale calculations
9. Render main text layer with computed positioning parameters
10. Call FUN_6f90c6a0 to finalize text output
11. Restore original font if changed

Parameters:
- IMPLICIT: g_nCurrentFontIndex contains active font
- IMPLICIT: g_pszStringBuffer points to Unicode text to render

Returns:
- void

Magic Numbers:
- 0x8: Byte offset for character height in font structure
- 0x14: Font handle array stride (20 bytes per entry)
- 0xa: Character code for newline in Unicode strings
- 0x1f: Height padding constant (31 pixels)
- 0x5: Width margin/padding (5 pixels)
- 0x66666667: Magic constant for signed division by 10
- 0x7: Right shift count for effect scale calculation
- 0x50: Character code passed to Ordinal_10034 (font char)

Related Functions:
- Ordinal_10041: Get drawable area dimensions
- Ordinal_10055: Render text layer with positioning
- Ordinal_10127: Set font mode
- Ordinal_10034: Get character properties
- FUN_6f90c5d0: Calculate text metrics
- FUN_6f90c6a0: Finalize text rendering

functions.name: GetStringDisplayWidth
functions.comment:
Calculate the maximum display width of a Unicode string.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input string is not null
2. Get string length via Unicode::strlen()
3. Loop through each character in the string
4. For line feed (0x0A), update max width if current exceeds it, reset current width
5. For non-ASCII characters (>0xFF) or animation codes, call g_pfnValueProcessor to get character width
6. Accumulate character widths into current line width
7. Update maximum width at loop end

Parameters:
- pwszText (wchar_t*): Unicode string to measure; cannot be null

Returns:
- Maximum display width in pixels of the text string

functions.name: RenderUnicodeStringWithColors
functions.signature: void RenderUnicodeStringWithColors(Unicode * pszText, int nX, int nY, int nWidth, int nColorIndex, int nCentered)
functions.comment:
Renders Unicode text with embedded color codes at specified screen location.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate text length and initial X position (handle centering if requested)
2. Initialize CEL_DATA structure (18 dwords) for sprite rendering
3. Set current color from global font table: g_pdwCelDataTable
4. Main loop - iterate through text characters:
   - If 0xFF escape: Parse color code (next char - 0x30), validate range [0,12]
   - If 0x0A newline: Reset X to column start, advance Y by line height
   - Otherwise: Render character via Ordinal_10073, advance X by char width
5. Exit when cursor exceeds text length

Parameters:
- pszText (Unicode*): Pointer to Unicode string (UTF-16LE encoded)
- nX (int): Initial X coordinate for rendering
- nY (int): Y coordinate (modified by newlines)
- nWidth (int): Available width for centering calculation
- nColorIndex (int): Default color index (0-12)
- nCentered (int): If non-zero, center text horizontally

Returns:
- void

Magic Numbers:
- 0xFF: Color escape prefix character
- 0x30: ASCII '0', subtracted from next char to get index
- 0x0C: Color range limit (13 colors, indices 0-12)
- 0x12: CEL_DATA structure size (18 dwords)

functions.name: CalcUnicodeStringWidth
functions.comment:
Calculates the width in pixels of a Unicode string, handling color codes.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input string is not NULL
2. Iterate through each character in string until newline (0x0A)
3. If character is 0xFF (color code prefix), skip next 4 bytes and call value processor
4. Otherwise, call value processor for normal character
5. Accumulate width values from value processor
6. Return total width

Parameters:
- pStr (Unicode*): Pointer to null-terminated Unicode string

Returns:
- int: Total calculated width in pixels

functions.name: InitializeStringBuffer
functions.signature: void InitializeStringBuffer(Unicode * pszInputStr, dword dwMaxWidth, dword dwBaseHeight, dword dwOutputValue, dword dwAlignMode)
functions.comment:
Initializes global string buffer with input string or clears if invalid.

Algorithm:
1. Check if input string is null or length exceeds 0x3FF (1023)
2. If invalid, clear entire buffer with 0x200 (512) dwords
3. Otherwise copy input string to global buffer
4. Set global configuration: max width, base height, output value, alignment mode

Parameters:
- pszInputStr (Unicode*): Input string or NULL
- dwMaxWidth (dword): Maximum width value
- dwBaseHeight (dword): Base height value
- dwOutputValue (dword): Output value setting
- dwAlignMode (dword): Alignment mode flags

Returns:
- void

Magic Numbers:
- 0x3FF (1023): Maximum input string length
- 0x200 (512): Buffer size in dwords (2048 bytes)

functions.name: CopyStringWithBufferInit
functions.signature: void CopyStringWithBufferInit(wchar_t * lpwszSource, dword dwMaxWidth, dword nBaseHeight, dword dwOutputValue, dword dwAlignMode, dword dwEffectScale)
functions.comment:
Initializes the global string buffer and configures text rendering settings.

Algorithm:
1. Check if lpwszSource is NULL or its length exceeds 0x3FF (1023)
2. If invalid: Clear the 0x800-byte (2048 dword) global string buffer
3. If valid: Copy lpwszSource into the global string buffer using Unicode::strcpy
4. Store rendering configuration parameters in globals:
   - g_dwMaxWidth: Maximum text width limit
   - g_nBaseHeight: Base line height
   - g_dwOutputValue: Output/destination value
   - g_dwAlignMode: Text alignment mode flags
   - g_dwEffectScale: Effect/shadow scale factor

Parameters:
- lpwszSource (wchar_t *): Pointer to source Unicode string or NULL
- dwMaxWidth (dword): Maximum width constraint
- nBaseHeight (dword): Base height value
- dwOutputValue (dword): Output destination specification
- dwAlignMode (dword): Alignment flags
- dwEffectScale (dword): Scale factor for effects

Returns:
- void

Notes:
- Buffer overflow protection: Strings exceeding 1023 characters reset buffer
- Operates on global buffer at g_pszStringBuffer (512 dword slots = 2048 bytes)
- Used for configuring text rendering pipeline

functions.name: RenderUnicodeTextWithLineHeight
functions.signature: void RenderUnicodeTextWithLineHeight(Unicode * pszText, int nX, int nY, int nColor, int nLineHeight)
functions.comment:
Renders Unicode string with colors, calculating width if line height is specified.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize width to 0
2. If line height is non-zero, calculate string display width and add 8-pixel padding
3. Call RenderUnicodeStringWithColors with calculated width

Parameters:
- pszText (Unicode*): String to render
- nX (int): X coordinate
- nY (int): Y coordinate
- nColor (int): Text color
- nLineHeight (int): Line height (if 0, width calculated as 0)

Returns:
- void

functions.name: DrawUnicodeTextWithColors
functions.signature: void DrawUnicodeTextWithColors(Unicode * pszText, int nXPos, int nYPos, int nColor, int nCenter, dword dwFlags)
functions.comment:
Draws Unicode text with color codes and optional centering.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate display width (with optional centering adjustment)
2. Compute string length and initial x-offset based on centering flag
3. Initialize character data array and set Cel data table pointer
4. For each character in string:
   - Detect color codes (0xFF prefix): Extract color index, validate range, adjust color
   - Detect newline (0x0A): Reset x-offset to baseline (with centering recalc)
   - Draw regular character using processor, advance x-offset
5. Return after processing all characters

Parameters:
- wsText (Unicode*): Unicode string to draw (may contain color/newline codes)
- nXPos (int): Starting x-coordinate
- nYPos (int): Starting y-coordinate
- nColor (int): Default color index for characters
- fCenter (int): Non-zero to center text horizontally
- dwFlags (dword): Rendering flags (purpose unknown)

Returns:
- void

Magic Numbers:
- 0xFF: Color code prefix in Unicode string
- 0x30: ASCII '0' for color digit offset
- 0x0C: Maximum color index (0-12)
- 0x0A: Newline character code
- 0x10: Negative font height multiplier denominator
- 18: Size of character data array (auStack_48)
- 8: Display width padding offset

functions.name: RenderTextString
functions.signature: void RenderTextString(ushort * pSrcString, uint nXPos, Unicode * pDstBuffer)
functions.comment:
Renders a Unicode text string at specified position with font metrics handling.

Algorithm:
1. Get source string length and clear 18-dword metrics buffer
2. Set initial font index and metrics from global state
3. Iterate through source string characters:
   - Skip multi-byte characters (0xFF prefix, 6-byte sequences)
   - Handle newline (0x0A): reset X, adjust Y down by font descender height
   - Process normal character: fetch glyph metrics, render via Ordinal_10072, advance X
4. Update font index from global state after each non-newline character

Parameters:
- pwszSrc (Unicode*): Input text string to render
- nXPos (int): Starting X position in pixels
- pwszDst (Unicode*): Output buffer for rendered text data

Returns:
- void

Magic Numbers:
- 0x12 (18): Stack buffer size in dwords (72 bytes)
- 0x0A: Newline character code
- 0xFF: Multi-byte character prefix
- 0xF: Font height divisor for descender calculation
- 0x14 (20): Font handle structure stride

functions.name: RenderTooltipText
functions.signature: void RenderTooltipText(Unicode * pszText, dword nX, int nY)
functions.comment:
Renders tooltip text within bounds, calculating dimensions and handling line wrapping.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate display width of text and line count
2. Validate text pointer is non-NULL
3. Measure total height required for all lines
4. Clamp X position and height within display boundaries
5. Render text with color support at calculated position

Parameters:
- pszText (Unicode*): Unicode string to render
- nX (dword): X position for text rendering
- nY (int): Y position for text rendering
- IMPLICIT: EBX contains maximum Y boundary, ESI contains maximum X boundary

Returns:
- void

Related Functions:
- RenderUnicodeStringWithColors: Handles actual text rendering
- GetStringDisplayWidth: Calculates string width in pixels

functions.name: RenderTextWithShadow
functions.signature: void RenderTextWithShadow(Unicode * pszText, int nWidth, int nHeight)
functions.comment:
Renders Unicode text with shadow effect using current font settings.

Algorithm:
1. Get character display width and font handle info
2. Clamp text position to viewport bounds (ESI is viewport width, EBX is viewport height)
3. Calculate text height with 2-pixel shadow offset
4. Call rendering functions to draw shadow and text with colors

Parameters:
- pszText (Unicode*): Null-terminated Unicode string to render
- nWidth (int): X coordinate offset for text rendering
- nHeight (int): Y coordinate offset for text rendering
- IMPLICIT: EBX contains viewport height, ESI contains viewport width

Returns:
- void

Magic Numbers:
- 0xa: Offset in font handle structure to character width byte
- 0x1f: Height padding/margin (31 pixels)
- 0x2: Shadow offset (2 pixels)

functions.name: GetUnicodeStringDimensions
functions.signature: void GetUnicodeStringDimensions(Unicode * pString, int * pnWidth, int * pnHeight)
functions.comment:
Measures the display dimensions (width and height) of a Unicode string.

Algorithm:
1. Get string display width via GetStringDisplayWidth
2. Count newline characters (0x0A) in string
3. Calculate height = (font_height * line_count) / 10

Parameters:
- pString (Unicode*): Pointer to Unicode string to measure
- pnWidth (int*): Output parameter for display width
- pnHeight (int*): Output parameter for calculated height

Returns:
- void (results stored in output parameters)

functions.name: CheckBitFlagIndex
functions.comment:
Returns bit flag indicating whether byCheck index is valid in the global bit flags array.

Algorithm:
1. Check if byCheck is 0xFF (special invalid case)
2. If byCheck >> 5 is less than 8, extract and return bit at position (byCheck & 0x1F) from g_dwBitFlags[byCheck >> 5]
3. Otherwise, fail assertion and call fatal error handler

Parameters:
- byCheck (byte): Index to check validity in bit flags

Returns:
- 1 if bit is set at index position, 0 if clear
- Does not return on invalid index (calls FUN_6f91436d)

functions.name: RenderMultilineUnicodeText
functions.signature: void RenderMultilineUnicodeText(Unicode * pszText, int nX, int nY, dword dwColor)
functions.comment:
Renders multi-line Unicode text with color styling at specified position.

Algorithm:
1. Validate text pointer is non-null (assert if invalid)
2. Count newlines (0x000a) in Unicode string to determine total line count
3. Fetch current font height from g_pFontHandles using g_nCurrentFontIndex
4. Calculate total text height: (font_height * g_dwHeightScale * line_count) / 10
5. Adjust nX coordinate to fit within ESI-retaddr bounds
6. Adjust nY coordinate to fit within EBX-0x1f bounds
7. Reserve top margin and adjust rendering Y if needed
8. Call Ordinal_10055 to clear/prepare rendering area with background
9. Call RenderUnicodeStringWithColors to render text with dwColor style

Parameters:
- pszText (Unicode*): Null-terminated Unicode string; may contain newlines (0x000a)
- nX (int): Target X coordinate for text position
- nY (int): Target Y coordinate for text position  
- dwColor (dword): Color/style flags passed to RenderUnicodeStringWithColors

Returns:
- void

Magic Numbers:
- 0x14 (20): Font handle array element stride
- 10 (0xa): Height/width scaling divisor
- 0x1f (31): Width boundary offset constant
- 2: Multiline text margin adjustment factor

functions.name: ProcessCelFileData
functions.signature: void ProcessCelFileData(void * this, void * pThis, int nFrameIndex, dword dwParam, int nStartOffset)
functions.comment:
Processes cel file frame data with optional transformations and rendering.

Algorithm:
1. Get total frame count from cel file
2. Initialize CelFileInfo structures for processing
3. If transformation mode (dwParam==1 or 2): Calculate cumulative offsets across frames
4. For each frame: Call appropriate rendering function (Ordinal_10072/10073) with calculated offset
5. Increment offset by 0x100 for next frame iteration

Parameters:
- pThis (void*): Cel file object pointer
- nFrameIndex (int): Frame index for processing
- dwParam (dword): Transformation mode (1=mode1, 2=mode2, other=default)
- nStartOffset (int): Initial offset value for first frame

Returns:
- void

Magic Numbers:
- 0x12: Loop counter for structure initialization (18 dwords)
- 0x100: Frame offset increment per iteration
- 0xffffffff: Sentinel value for parameter (-1 in signed context)

functions.name: RenderUnicodeStringWithOverlay
functions.signature: void RenderUnicodeStringWithOverlay(ushort * pString, uint param_2, int nY, int nOpacity, int nAlignment, int param_6)
functions.comment:
Renders a Unicode string with text sizing, line breaks, and optional color overlay.

Algorithm:
1. Validate string is non-empty and calculate display width
2. Count line breaks (0x0A) to determine number of lines
3. Query current font metrics (height and scale factor)
4. Determine horizontal offset based on alignment parameter:
   - If nAlignment=1, center text (nX - width/2)
5. Query color overlay values from Ordinal_10041
6. Clamp X offset to valid range [0, max), apply minimum constraints
7. If nOpacity=0, render background rectangle
8. If nOpacity≠0, scale color fill width by opacity (multiply, shift right 7 bits)
9. Render background rectangle for remaining non-colored portion
10. Render the Unicode string with calculated dimensions and colors

Parameters:
- pString (Unicode*): Unicode string to render
- nX (uint): Horizontal position
- nY (int): Vertical position
- nOpacity (int): Color overlay opacity (0=no color, 1-128=varying transparency)
- nAlignment (int): Text alignment (1=center, other=left)

Returns:
- void

Magic Numbers:
- 0x14: Font handle structure stride
- 0x0A: Line break character (newline)
- 10: Height scaling divisor
- 0x1F: Minimum X coordinate offset
- 0x50: Default color value (80 decimal)

functions.name: ReleaseLinkedListWithAllocation
functions.comment:
Iterates through a linked list and releases allocated nodes.

Algorithm:
1. Check if pListHead is non-NULL; if NULL, return immediately
2. Enter loop at first node
3. Load next node pointer from current node's pNext field
4. Call ReleasePoolAllocation for current node's data
5. Call ReleasePoolAllocation for current node itself
6. Move to next node and repeat while pNext is non-NULL

Parameters:
- pListHead (LinkedListNode*): Pointer to first node in linked list; NULL terminates immediately

Returns:
- void: Function always succeeds; does not return status code

Structure Layout:
- LinkedListNode.data (offset 0x0, uint): Node payload data
- LinkedListNode.pNext (offset 0x4, void*): Pointer to next node

functions.name: WrapUnicodeText
functions.signature: int * WrapUnicodeText(Unicode * pwsText, int * pnLineCount, int nMaxWidth)
functions.comment:
Wraps Unicode text to fit within a maximum display width by breaking at word boundaries.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate text length via Unicode::strlen
2. Check if entire text fits via Ordinal_10123 (width calculator)
3. If fits, allocate single line node and return
4. Otherwise, iterate from start finding longest segment that fits width
5. For each oversized segment, search backwards for line break point
6. Allocate node for fitting segment and link to previous node
7. Continue from next segment until entire text is processed

Parameters:
- pwsText (Unicode*): Pointer to Unicode string to wrap
- pnLineCount (int*): Pointer to receive count of created line nodes
- nMaxWidth (int): Maximum display width for each line

Returns:
- Pointer to head of linked list of line nodes (int* with [1] as next pointer)
- NULL if text was empty or allocation failed

functions.name: CreateUnicodeString
functions.signature: int * CreateUnicodeString(Unicode * pString, int nMaxLen, int nApplyTransform)
functions.comment:
Allocates and initializes a Unicode string header structure.

Algorithm:
1. Assert nMaxLen < 200 characters, terminate if invalid
2. Allocate 8-byte header structure via FogMemAlloc
3. If nApplyTransform and first character < 0x100, apply character transformation
4. Decrement nMaxLen after successful transform
5. Allocate string buffer (nMaxLen * 2 + 2 bytes for Unicode + null terminator)
6. Store allocated buffer pointer in header[0]
7. Store zero in header[1] (unused/reserved field)
8. Copy source string to buffer with null termination

Parameters:
- pString (Unicode*): Pointer to source Unicode string
- nMaxLen (int): Maximum string length in characters (validated < 200)
- nApplyTransform (int): Non-zero to apply character transformation

Returns:
- int*: Pointer to allocated 8-byte header structure; header[0] contains string pointer

functions.name: CreateUIElementType2
functions.signature: void * CreateUIElementType2(dword dwParam1, dword dwParam2, dword dwParam4, dword dwParam5, dword dwFlags, dword dwParam8, dword dwParam9, dword dwParam10)
functions.comment:
Creates a Type 2 UI element with initialized structure fields.

Algorithm:
1. Allocate 0x4c (76) bytes for UI element structure via FogMemAlloc
2. Initialize all dwords to 0 using REP STOSD loop
3. Set type field to 2 and apply bit masks from gdwBitMasks_exref
4. Copy parameters into structure fields at offsets [1], [3], [4], [5], [6], [8], [9], [10], [0xc], [0xd], [0x12]
5. Set function pointers and callback addresses at offsets [7], [9]
6. Call FUN_6f90ea50 to finalize initialization
7. Return pointer to initialized structure

Parameters:
- dwParam1 (ECX): Stored at structure offset [3]
- dwParam2 (EDX): Stored at structure offset [4]
- dwParam4: Stored at structure offset [5]
- dwParam5: Stored at structure offset [6]
- dwFlags: Stored at structure offset [1], combined with bit masks
- dwParam8: Stored at structure offset [8]
- dwParam9: Stored at structure offset [9]
- dwParam10: Stored at structure offset [0xc]

Returns:
- Pointer to allocated and initialized UI element structure (never NULL)

Magic Numbers:
- 0x4c (76): Total structure size in bytes
- 0x13 (19): Number of dwords to zero-initialize
- 2: Type identifier for this UI element class
- Offsets [0]-[0x12]: Structure field indices

functions.name: InitializeImageDimensions
functions.signature: void InitializeImageDimensions(int * pImageData, int nWidth, int nHeight)
functions.comment:
Initialize image data structure with width and height. Validates that image data has eType field set to 2, then sets width at offset +4 and height at offset +0x48.

Algorithm:
1. Check if pImageData->eType == 2 (assertion check)
2. On failure, trigger assertion failure with FogAssert
3. Set pImageData[1] = nWidth (offset +4)
4. Set pImageData[0x12] = nHeight (offset +0x48, 18*4)
5. Return 1 (success)

Parameters:
- pImageData (int*): Pointer to image data structure, must have eType=2
- nWidth (int): Image width value to set at offset +4
- nHeight (int): Image height value to set at offset +0x48

Returns:
- 1 on success (always, or triggers assertion failure)

Notes:
- Field at offset 0 contains eType (must be 2)
- Field at offset 4 is width storage
- Field at offset 0x48 (72 bytes) is height storage

functions.name: ImageData_ValidateAndSetFields
functions.signature: void ImageData_ValidateAndSetFields(int * pImageData, int nFieldValue2, int nFieldValue3)
functions.comment:
Validates and sets image data fields.

Algorithm:
1. Validate that pImageData points to type 2 structure
2. Assert on type mismatch and terminate process
3. Set field at offset 0xc (param [3]) to nFieldValue2
4. Set field at offset 0x10 (param [4]) to nFieldValue3
5. Return 1 (success)

Parameters:
- pImageData (int *): Pointer to image structure; [0] must equal 2
- nFieldValue2 (int): Value for field at offset 0xc
- nFieldValue3 (int): Value for field at offset 0x10

Returns:
- 1 on success
- Does not return on type validation failure (FUN_6f91436d terminates)

functions.name: InitializeCelFrameCount
functions.comment:
Initializes cel animation frame count from image data.

Algorithm:
1. Verify pCelData->eType == 2 (DT_CelData), assert if not
2. Call GetCelFrameCount to get frame count from cel image at pCelData[1]
3. Calculate requested max - 1, clamped to frameCount - 1
4. Clamp negative values to 0

functions.name: ProcessType2UIElementClick
functions.comment:
Processes click events on Type 2 UI elements with sub-region hit testing.

Algorithm:
1. Get image data pointer from UI element structure at offset [0]
2. Assert element type equals 2 (Type 2 UI element validation)
3. Check visibility flags via gdwBitMasks_exref bitmasks at offsets +0 and +8
4. If not visible (either bitmask fails), return 0 immediately
5. Get sub-region table pointer from offset [0x12]
6. Calculate adjusted X position: (element[6] - element[4]) + g_nScreenWidth
7. If sub-region table exists, iterate through regions (5 dwords each):
   a. Check Y bounds: regionY <= (g_nScreenHeight - elementY) < (regionY + regionHeight)
   b. Check X bounds: (regionX - regionWidth) <= adjustedX < regionX
   c. If hit, call region handler at piSubRegions[regionIndex * 5 + 4](pUIElement)
   d. Advance by 5 dwords per region, check next entry flag at offset +9
8. If no sub-region matched and default handler exists at offset [0xd]:
   a. Call default handler: element[0xd](pUIElement)
9. Return handler result or 0 if no handler invoked

Parameters:
- pUIElement (Stack+4): Pointer to UI element structure

Returns:
- uint: Handler return value, or 0 if no click processed

Structure Layout (UI Element Type 2, 0x4c bytes):
Offset  Size  Field           Description
0x00    4     eType           Element type (must be 2)
0x04    4     dwFlags         Flags combined with gdwBitMasks
0x08    4     dwMaskBits      Visibility mask bits
0x0c    4     nY              Y coordinate
0x10    4     nX              X coordinate
0x14    4     nWidth          Width
0x18    4     nHeight         Height
0x34    4     pfnCallback     Default click handler function pointer
0x48    4     pSubRegions     Pointer to sub-region table

Sub-Region Entry (20 bytes / 5 dwords):
Offset  Size  Field           Description
0x00    4     nY              Region Y position
0x04    4     nX              Region X position
0x08    4     nHeight         Region height
0x0c    4     nWidth          Region width
0x10    4     pfnHandler      Region click handler

Special Cases:
- Returns 0 if element type assertion fails (after crash)
- Returns 0 if visibility flags not set
- Returns 0 if no sub-region matched and no default handler
- Sub-region iteration stops when entry flag at offset +9 is 0

   a. If at last item, wrap to first item
   b. Set new active item and recalculate selection index

- 0: Event not handled (passed through)

functions.name: ProcessMouseInputAndFindNearestWidget
functions.comment:
Processes mouse input coordinates and finds the nearest UI widget for interaction.

Algorithm:
1. Extract mouse X (low word) and Y (high word >> 16) from packed dwMouseCoords+8/+0xc
2. Calculate scroll division: Y / 0x78 (120 pixels per scroll unit)
3. Call DispatchVirtualMethod to get screen boundaries, then decrement both by 1
4. Call Ordinal_10047 (D2gfx.GetVideoMode) to check if cursor adjustment needed
5. If adjustment needed, clamp mouse X to screen width and Y to screen height, call SetCursorPos
6. Store clamped coordinates in g_nScreenHeight (X) and g_nScreenWidth (Y) - note reversed naming
7. Check IsScreenPopupActiveBitSet - if popup active, return immediately
8. Get starting widget from g_dwLastInventoryItem or g_pInventoryList
9. Iterate through widget linked list (offset 0x3c = next pointer):
   a. Check widget type == 5 (scrollbar widget type)
   b. Verify visibility bits set in gdwBitMasks_exref
   c. Call GetScrollbarHeight to verify positive height
   d. Calculate distance from mouse to widget bounds using squared distance formula
   e. Track nearest widget based on Euclidean distance comparison
10. If nearest scrollbar found, call ScrollbarAdjustPosition
11. Otherwise iterate widgets looking for type 6 (button), call OnButtonPressed
12. Call InsertCacheNodeWithCookie to cache the interaction

Parameters:
  dwMouseCoords - Packed structure containing mouse coordinates at offsets +0x8 and +0xc

Returns: void

Special Cases:
  - Returns early if IsScreenPopupActiveBitSet returns non-zero
  - Widget linked list traversal via offset 0x3c (field index 15)
  - Distance calculation uses squared values to avoid sqrt
  - SSA temporaries (iVar3, piVar4, etc.) are decompiler-generated and cannot be renamed

Ordinal References:
  - Ordinal_10047: D2gfx.GetVideoMode - returns current video mode for cursor boundary check

Widget Structure Layout:
  Offset  Size  Field       Description
  0x00    4     dwType      Widget type (5=scrollbar, 6=button)
  0x08    4     dwFlags     Visibility/state flags
  0x0C    4     nPosY       Widget Y position
  0x10    4     nPosX       Widget X position
  0x14    4     nHeight     Widget height
  0x18    4     nWidth      Widget width
  0x3C    4     pNext       Next widget in linked list

functions.name: SetStoredValue
functions.comment:
Stores a value to the global storage variable.

Algorithm:
1. Load parameter from stack
2. Store to global variable g_dwStoredValue
3. Return to caller

Parameters:
- dwValue: Value to store in global variable

Returns:
- void

functions.name: SetUnitFlags
functions.comment:
Sets or clears a bit flag at offset +8 in a unit structure based on mode.

Algorithm:
1. Test if nMode is non-zero
2. If nMode != 0: OR the flag at pUnit+8 with mask from gdwBitMasks_exref[0xc]
3. If nMode == 0: AND the flag at pUnit+8 with inverted mask from gdwInvBitMasks_exref[0xc]
4. Return to caller

Parameters:
- pUnit (uint*): Pointer to unit structure; flag value modified at offset +8
- nMode (int): Mode selector: non-zero sets flag, zero clears flag

Returns:
- void; modifies unit structure in-place

Magic Numbers:
- 0x8: Offset of flag field within unit structure
- 0xc: Offset within bit mask tables

functions.name: SetCurrentInputItem
functions.comment:
Sets the current input item identifier in global state.

Algorithm:
1. Load input item ID from stack parameter (dwInputItem)
2. Store ID to global variable g_dwCurrentInputItem
3. Return to caller

Parameters:
- dwInputItem (uint): Input item identifier to store globally

Returns:
- void (no return value)

functions.name: GetGameState
functions.comment:
Get the current game state value.

Algorithm:
1. Load the global game state variable
2. Return the value in EAX

Parameters:
- IMPLICIT: No parameters

Returns:
- EAX: Current game state value from g_dwGameState

Notes:
- Simple getter function used to query game state throughout the codebase

functions.name: SetLastInventoryItem
functions.comment:
Stores the last selected inventory item and next item reference.

Algorithm:
1. Store dwItem to global g_dwLastInventoryItem
2. Store dwItemNext to global g_dwLastInventoryItemNext
3. Return success (1)

Parameters:
- dwItem (dword): Inventory item ID to store
- dwItemNext (dword): Next item reference

Returns:
- 1 (success)

functions.name: SafeDereferencePointer
functions.comment:
Safely dereferences a pointer with NULL check.

Algorithm:
1. Check if input pointer is NULL
2. If NULL, return NULL (pass through)
3. Otherwise, dereference and return pointed value

Parameters:
- pdwValue (uint*): Pointer to dereference (can be NULL)

Returns:
- NULL if input is NULL, otherwise the dereferenced value as pointer

functions.name: GetLastInventoryItem
functions.comment:
Returns the last inventory item ID that was accessed.

Algorithm:
1. Load global dwLastInventoryItem from memory at 0x6f961540
2. Return the value in EAX register

Parameters:
- None

Returns:
- uint: Last inventory item ID or 0 if none accessed

functions.name: ComparePaletteBuffers
functions.comment:
Compares two palette buffers and returns comparison result.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize two 260-byte palette buffers
2. Load palette data into both buffers via FUN_6f914ae4
3. Compare buffers using FUN_6f90ff10
4. Update palette reference via Ordinal_10048
5. Return comparison result

Parameters:
- None (uses global palette data g_pPaletteData)

Returns:
- Result of palette comparison (1=match, 0=mismatch or error)

functions.name: LoadPaletteData
functions.comment:
Loads palette data from WAD files and initializes color mapping tables.

Algorithm:
1. Load base palette (256 colors, 3-byte RGB) from WAD file dwPaletteId via Ordinal_10038/FUN_6f913fa2
2. Copy palette into local buffer abPaletteBuffer with 4-byte stride (RGB + padding)
3. Load mode-specific palette tables from WAD file dwModeId via Ordinal_10038/FUN_6f913fa2
4. Copy 11 pre-allocated palette subtables from loaded data to global memory (256 colors to 49152 entries)
5. Initialize all color table entries in DAT_6f9c5997 with value 5
6. Build color lookup tables via FindClosestColorMatch() for palette matching

Parameters:
- dwPaletteId (ECX): Palette ID from resource WAD file
- dwModeId (EDX): Mode identifier for palette subtables
- IMPLICIT: EBX contains base context pointer

Returns:
- 1 (success constant)

functions.name: GetDataTableEntry
functions.comment:
Returns pointer to indexed entry in data table.

Algorithm:
1. Shift index left by 8 bits (multiply by 256) to convert array index to 64-byte offset (256 >> 2 = 64)
2. Add base address of data table (0x6f9c5994)
3. Return computed pointer

Parameters:
- nIndex (int): Zero-based array index

Returns:
- void *: Pointer to the indexed entry in the data table. Each entry is 64 bytes apart.

Magic Numbers:
- 0x8: Left shift amount (multiply index by 256, which equals 64 * 4 for 32-bit pointer arithmetic)
- 0x40 (64): Entry stride in bytes

functions.name: ProcessPaletteCleanup
functions.comment:
Manages periodic palette data cleanup with timer-based rate limiting.

Algorithm:
1. Check if cleanup is active (g_dwCleanupActive)
2. If inactive, exit immediately
3. If active but timer not enabled, disable cleanup
4. If timer enabled, check elapsed time since last update
5. If less than 2001ms (0x7d1) elapsed, exit to throttle calls
6. Update last tick count and decrement countdown counter
7. When countdown reaches 0, reset cleanup flags and call cleanup handler

Parameters:
- IMPLICIT: g_dwCleanupActive: Cleanup active flag
- IMPLICIT: g_dwTimerEnabled: Timer enabled flag  
- IMPLICIT: g_dwLastTickCount: Last recorded tick count
- IMPLICIT: g_dwCountdown: Remaining cleanup iterations

Returns:
- void

Magic Numbers:
- 0x7d0 (2000): Minimum milliseconds between cleanup calls
- GetTickCount(): System timer for rate limiting

functions.name: InitializeCleanupTimer
functions.comment:
Initializes or disables application cleanup timer and palette refresh.

Algorithm:
1. Check enable flag
2. If enabled: set timer globals, record current tick count, enable cleanup
3. If disabled: disable timer and cleanup flags
4. Call palette cleanup handler in both cases

Parameters:
- fEnable (bool): Enable (non-zero) or disable (zero) cleanup timer

Returns:
- void

Related Functions:
- Ordinal_10048: Palette data cleanup handler
- GetTickCount: Windows API for elapsed time

functions.name: InitActPalette
functions.comment:
Initialize palette and color transformation tables.

Algorithm:
1. If nAct == 0: Use default ACT1 palette files
   - Build path to palette .act and .pl2 files in DATA_GLOBAL
   - Load palette data and initialize transform tables
2. If nAct != 0: Use provided buffer pointers
   - Load palette data from nAct and dwParam2 buffers
   - Initialize color transformation lookup tables

Parameters:
- nAct (int): Act ID or pointer to palette buffer (0 = default ACT1)
- dwParam2 (uint): Pointer to palette data buffer or palette param

Returns:
- 1 (always succeeds)

functions.name: FindPaletteIndexForColor
functions.signature: uint FindPaletteIndexForColor(byte byRed, byte byGreen, byte byBlue)
functions.comment:
Finds the palette index for an RGB color.

Algorithm:
1. Extract R, G, B color components (8-bit values)
2. Call FindClosestColorMatch with palette pointer and RGB values
3. Returns palette index of closest matching color

Parameters:
- byRed (byte): Red component (0-255)
- byGreen (byte): Green component (0-255)
- byBlue (byte): Blue component (0-255)

Returns:
- Palette index (0-255) of the closest matching color

functions.name: CopyDwords
functions.comment:
Copies 0xc40 (3136) dwords from global data to destination buffer.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize source pointer to global data table (0x6f98156c)
2. Loop 3136 times, copying dword-sized chunks
3. Increment both source and destination pointers after each copy
4. Return to caller

Parameters:
- pdwDest (dword*): Destination buffer for copied dwords

Returns:
- void

Notes:
- Copies exactly 0xc40 = 3136 dwords (12544 bytes total)
- Source data is from global data region

functions.name: InitializeScreenObject
functions.comment:
Allocates and initializes a screen object structure (1128 bytes). Sets default screen dimensions, flags, and event handlers. Returns pointer stored in global g_pCurrentScreenData.

Algorithm:
1. Check if screen object already exists; if so, process and release it
2. Allocate new structure (0x468 bytes) via FogMemAlloc
3. Zero-fill entire structure using REP STOSD (282 dwords)
4. Set object type field to 0xB
5. Configure bit flags from gdwBitMasks_exref (3 flag sources)
6. Store screen dimensions from globals g_nScreenHeight, g_nScreenWidth
7. Install function pointers for event handlers at offsets [7] and [8]
8. Initialize remaining fields to 0
9. Link object to global list via LinkObjectToList
10. Store reference in g_pCurrentScreenData

Parameters:
- No explicit parameters
- IMPLICIT: Uses global variables g_nScreenHeight, g_nScreenWidth, gdwBitMasks_exref

Returns:
- void (result stored in global g_pCurrentScreenData)

Magic Numbers:
- 0x468 (1128): Structure size in bytes
- 0x11A (282): Number of dwords to zero-fill
- 0xB: Screen object type constant
- Offsets [2-0xD]: Structure field indices storing flags and dimensions

functions.name: ProcessAndClearScreenInventory
functions.comment:
Process and clear the current screen inventory data.

Algorithm:
1. Check if g_pCurrentScreenData is non-null
2. If valid, process the inventory item data
3. Clear the global pointer to null
4. Return result of processing

Parameters:
- IMPLICIT: g_pCurrentScreenData (void*): Screen inventory context to process

Returns:
- Result code from ProcessInventoryItem, or 0 if no data to process

functions.name: IsScreenPopupActiveBitSet
functions.comment:
Checks if screen popup is active and specific bits are set.

Algorithm:
1. Check if current screen data is initialized
2. Assert screen type is popup (0xb)
3. Test if both bit masks 0x0 and 0x8 are set in screen data[2]
4. Return 1 if both bits set, 0 otherwise

Parameters:
- None (uses global screen data)

Returns:
- 1 if screen is popup and both active bits are set
- 0 otherwise

Magic Numbers:
- 0xb: Screen type for popup
- 0x6f91d164: Pointer to bit masks array
- 0x8: Offset to flags field in screen data

functions.name: ValidateCharacterData
functions.comment:
Validates and registers a character in the current screen data.

Algorithm:
1. Verify current screen is popup type (0xb), assert if not
2. Check if character count (at offset 0x10) exceeds 7, return 0 if true
3. Copy character data (33 dwords) to screen data at calculated offset
4. Call Ordinal_10127 to trigger character redraw update
5. Calculate character value via SumCharacterValues
6. Update max value field, increment character count, update display stride

Parameters:
- pCharName (Unicode *): Pointer to character data to register

Returns:
- 1 on success, 0 if character limit exceeded or screen type invalid

functions.name: TryInvokeScreenHandler
functions.comment:
Attempts to invoke the current screen's event handler if conditions are met.

Algorithm:
1. Verify current screen type is popup (0xb), assert otherwise
2. Check if both bit flags in gdwBitMasks are set on g_pCurrentScreenData[2]
3. Verify screen has a valid handler index (g_pCurrentScreenData[0x119] != -1)
4. Calculate handler function pointer from screen data using stride 0x21 (33) bytes
5. If pointer is non-null, invoke it and return 1, otherwise return 0

Parameters:
- None

Returns:
- 1 if handler was invoked
- 0 if conditions not met or handler pointer is null

functions.name: CalculatePopupHoverColumn
functions.comment:
Calculates which column the mouse is hovering over in a popup window.
Called as a callback from the screen object event system.

Algorithm:
1. Validate object type is 0xB (D2WIN_POPUP)
2. Check visibility flags via gdwBitMasks_exref (offset +8 AND offset +0)
3. If not visible/interactive, return 0 (not handled)
4. Initialize selected column to -1 at offset 0x464
5. Calculate relative X position from popup bounds
6. Validate mouse Y is within popup height bounds
7. Validate mouse X is within popup width bounds
8. If within bounds, calculate column index: X / 20 pixels

Parameters:
- pPopupData (ECX): Pointer to popup structure (type 0xB)
  - [0x00] eType: Object type, must be 0xB
  - [0x08] dwFlags: Visibility/interaction flags
  - [0x0C] nY: Top Y coordinate
  - [0x10] nWidth: Popup width
  - [0x14] nHeight: Popup height
  - [0x18] nRight: Right X coordinate
  - [0x464] nSelectedColumn: Output hover column index

Returns:
- 1: Mouse within popup bounds (column calculated)
- 0: Mouse outside bounds or popup not visible

Magic Numbers:
- 0xB: D2WIN_POPUP object type constant
- 0x14 (20): Column width in pixels
- 0x119 (281): DWORD index for selected column field (offset 0x464)
- -1 (0xFFFFFFFF): Invalid/no column selected

functions.name: RenderPopupContent
functions.comment:
Renders popup menu content with multiple text lines and selection highlighting.
Called as a callback from the screen object event system at offset 0x1C.

NOTE: Function boundary is broken (single instruction detected). Variable types and
names documented here but cannot be applied via MCP tools until boundary is fixed.

Algorithm:
1. Validate object type is 0xB (D2WIN_POPUP) via FogAssert
2. Check visibility flags in gdwBitMasks (bits at offset +0 and +8)
3. If not visible, return 0 (not handled)
4. Find palette index for gray color (0x3F, 0x3F, 0x3F) for background
5. Calculate background rectangle bounds from popup dimensions with 5px padding
6. Draw semi-transparent background via Ordinal_10052 (D2Gfx.DrawFilledRect)
7. Validate clip coordinates via GfxValidateClipCoordinates
8. Set active font to index 1
9. Loop through all text lines (count at offset 0x40):
   a. Get text pointer from popup+0x44 (0x84 bytes per line)
   b. Calculate Y position: baseY + ((lineIndex - lineCount) + 1) * 0x14
   c. Determine text color: 3 if selected (matches offset 0x464), 0 otherwise
   d. Call RenderUnicodeTextWithLineHeight for each line
10. Return 1 (handled)

Parameters:
- pPopupData (ECX): Pointer to popup structure (type 0xB)
  [0x00] eType: Object type constant 0xB
  [0x08] dwFlags: Visibility/interaction flags
  [0x0C] nY: Top Y coordinate
  [0x10] nX: Left X coordinate
  [0x14] nHeight: Popup height
  [0x18] nWidth: Popup width
  [0x40] nLineCount: Number of text lines
  [0x44] szLines[]: Unicode text lines (0x84 bytes each = 66 wchar_t)
  [0x464] nSelectedLine: Currently highlighted line index (-1 if none)

Returns:
- 1: Popup was visible and rendered
- 0: Popup not visible (flags not set)

Magic Numbers:
- 0xB: D2WIN_POPUP object type constant
- 0x14 (20): Line height in pixels
- 0x84 (132): Bytes per text line (66 wchar_t)
- 0x3F: Gray color component (63/255)
- 0xFF: Alpha value for background rectangle
- 5: Padding pixels around popup content

Ordinal Calls:
- Ordinal_10052: D2Gfx.DrawFilledRect - Draws filled rectangle with alpha

Variable Mapping (cannot rename due to broken boundary):
- uVar1 -> byPaletteIndex (byte): Palette index for gray background color
- iVar2 -> nLineCount (int): Number of text lines from offset 0x40
- iVar3 -> nLineIndex (int): Loop counter for rendering text lines
- pszText -> pwszLineText (Unicode*): Pointer to current Unicode text line
- unaff_ESI, unaff_EBX: Phantom registers from decompiler (ignore)
- iStack_10..iStack_4: Background rectangle coordinates (nTop, nBottom, nLeft, nRight)

functions.name: AllocateAndInitializeObject
functions.signature: void AllocateAndInitializeObject(uint dwParam1, uint dwParam2, uint dwParam3, uint dwParam4)
functions.comment:
Allocates and initializes a 0x44-byte object structure with parameters and flags.

Algorithm:
1. Allocate 0x44 bytes via FogMemAlloc
2. Zero-initialize entire structure (0x11 dwords)
3. Set offset 0x0 to 10
4. OR bit flags from gdwBitMasks_exref into offsets 0x8 and 0x8 again with additional mask
5. Store parameters at offsets 0xc, 0x10, 0x14, 0x18
6. Store callback function pointer at offset 0x1c
7. Zero remaining fields
8. Link object to global list via LinkObjectToList
9. Return allocated and initialized object

Parameters:
- nParam1 (uint): Parameter stored at offset 0xc
- nParam2 (uint): Parameter stored at offset 0x10
- nParam3 (uint): Parameter stored at offset 0x14
- nParam4 (uint): Parameter stored at offset 0x18

Returns:
- Pointer to allocated and initialized 0x44-byte object structure

functions.name: SetProgressBarValue
functions.comment:
Sets the progress value in a progress bar control.

Algorithm:
1. Validate that control type is 10 (progress bar type)
2. Trigger assertion if type validation fails
3. Write value to control structure at offset 0x10
4. Return success code

Parameters:
- pControl (int *): Pointer to control structure
- nValue (int): Progress value to set

Returns:
- 1 on success (after setting value)

functions.name: ProcessInventoryItemWrapper
functions.comment:
Wrapper that processes an inventory item through linked list management.

Algorithm:
1. Passes inventory item handle to ProcessInventoryItem
2. Returns result (success/failure status)

Parameters:
- nItem (int): Inventory item handle to process

Returns:
- 1 on success, 0 if inventory list is empty

Related Functions:
- ProcessInventoryItem: Actual linked list processing implementation

functions.name: RenderProgressBar
functions.comment:
Renders a progress bar UI element by drawing a colored rectangle.

Classification: Callback/Handler - render callback for D2WIN_PROGRESSBAR type (eType=10)

Algorithm:
1. Validate pProgressBarData->eType == D2WIN_PROGRESSBAR (10), assert if invalid
2. Check visibility flags at offset 0x8 against gdwBitMasks_exref[0] and gdwBitMasks_exref[2]
3. If not visible, return 0 (nothing drawn)
4. Find red color palette index via FindPaletteIndexForColor(0xff, 0, 0)
5. Extract coordinates from progress bar structure:
   - nMinX = pProgressBarData[3] (offset 0xC)
   - nMinY = pProgressBarData[4] (offset 0x10)
   - nMaxY = nMinY + pProgressBarData[6] (offset 0x18 = height)
6. Calculate nMaxX using FPU value (progress percentage * width)
7. Call GfxValidateClipCoordinates to draw clipped rectangle
8. Return 1 (rendered successfully)

Parameters:
- pProgressBarData (int * in ECX): Pointer to 0x44-byte progress bar structure
  Offset 0x00: eType (must be 10 for D2WIN_PROGRESSBAR)
  Offset 0x08: dwFlags (visibility bit flags)
  Offset 0x0C: nMinX (left coordinate)
  Offset 0x10: nMinY (top coordinate)
  Offset 0x14: nWidth (bar width)
  Offset 0x18: nHeight (bar height)
  Offset 0x40: flProgress (float, current progress 0.0-1.0)

Returns:
- 1: Progress bar was rendered
- 0: Progress bar not visible (flags not set)

Special Cases:
- Assert failure if eType != 10 (not a progress bar)
- Returns 0 without rendering if visibility flags not set

Caller Context:
- Stored at offset 0x1C in progress bar object by AllocateAndInitializeObject
- Called as render callback during UI draw cycle

functions.name: CreateScrollbarObject
functions.signature: void * CreateScrollbarObject(dword nX, dword nY, dword nWidth, dword nHeight, dword nStyle, dword nIndex)
functions.comment:
Allocates and initializes a scrollbar UI object (0x60 bytes).

Algorithm:
1. Allocate 96-byte structure via FogMemAlloc
2. Zero-initialize all 24 dword fields
3. Set object type to 5 (scrollbar)
4. Apply global bit flags from gdwBitMasks_exref
5. Store position/size params in object fields
6. Set callback to ProcessScrollbarMousePos
7. Link to global object list

Parameters:
- nX (ECX): X position, stored at offset 0x0C
- nY (EDX): Y position, stored at offset 0x10
- nWidth: Width, stored at offset 0x14
- nHeight: Height, stored at offset 0x18
- nStyle: Style flags, stored at offset 0x04
- nIndex: Index value, stored at offset 0x34

Returns:
- Pointer to initialized scrollbar object

Magic Numbers:
- 0x60 (96): Object struct size
- 0x18 (24): Number of dwords to zero
- 5: Object type ID (scrollbar)

functions.name: GetScrollbarHeight
functions.comment:
Validates and returns the height of a scrollbar control.

Algorithm:
1. Assert that pScrollbar points to scrollbar type (eType == 5)
2. Return height value at offset 0x12

Parameters:
- pScrollbar: Pointer to scrollbar control structure

Returns:
- Height of scrollbar at offset 0x12

functions.name: SetScrollbarPosition
functions.comment:
Sets scrollbar position if valid type detected.

Algorithm:
1. Verify scrollbar type field equals 5 (scrollbar type)
2. Assert failure if type mismatch
3. Validate position value > 0
4. Store position at offset 0x48 if valid, otherwise store 0
5. Always returns 1 (success)

Parameters:
- pScrollbar (int*): Pointer to scrollbar structure; offset 0 = type, offset 0x48 = position
- nPosition (int): New position value to set if positive

Returns:
- 1 (always succeeds)

functions.name: ScrollbarSetValue
functions.comment:
Sets the value of a scrollbar after validating type. Clamps to max if needed.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pScrollbarData type field equals 5
2. Get current max value from field offset 0x12
3. Clamp nValue to not exceed max
4. Store clamped value at offset 0x13
5. Return success (1)

Parameters:
- pScrollbarData (int *): Pointer to scrollbar structure
- nValue (int): New value to set

Returns:
- 1 on success
- Does not return on validation failure (calls FUN_6f91436d)

functions.name: ScrollbarGetValue
functions.comment:
Retrieves the current value from a scrollbar control.

Algorithm:
1. Verify the scrollbar control structure (validate type field equals 5)
2. If type check fails, trigger assertion and invoke abort handler
3. Dereference scrollbar pointer to get offset 0x4c (value field)
4. Return the value

Parameters:
- pScrollbar (void*): Pointer to scrollbar control structure

Returns:
- int: Current scrollbar value from structure offset 0x4c (0-based range)

Notes:
- Asserts if pScrollbar does not point to valid scrollbar (type != 5)
- Called from UI event handlers to retrieve user input values

functions.name: SetScrollbarValue
functions.comment:
Sets the current value field of a scrollbar object.

Algorithm:
1. Validate that pScrollbar points to a valid scrollbar (type == 5)
2. Call FogAssert if validation fails (non-recoverable)
3. Write nValue to object field at offset 0x15
4. Return success

Parameters:
- pScrollbar (int*): Pointer to scrollbar object; [0] must equal 5
- nValue (int): New value to assign to scrollbar field at offset 0x15

Returns:
- 1 (success)

Note: Function is a critical setter and calls FogAssert on invalid input.

functions.name: SetScrollbarValue
functions.comment:
Validates and updates scrollbar value.

Algorithm:
1. Validate that pScrollbar->eType == 5 (SCROLLBAR_TYPE)
2. If invalid, assert and exit
3. Write nValue to scrollbar's value field at offset 0x5c

Parameters:
- pScrollbar (int*): Pointer to scrollbar structure
- nValue (int): New value to set

Returns:
- 1 on success

functions.name: ScrollbarAdjustPosition
functions.signature: int ScrollbarAdjustPosition(int nScrollbar, int * pScrollbarData, int nDelta)
functions.comment:
Adjusts scrollbar position by a delta value and enforces bounds.

Algorithm:
1. Verify scrollbar structure type is valid, abort if not
2. Return early if scrollbar is disabled (eType == 0x16)
3. Adjust position based on nDelta: set flag if negative (up/back) or positive (down/forward)
4. Add/subtract delta from current position field (offset 0x13)
5. Clamp position to valid range: [0, max_position at offset 0x12]
6. Execute optional position change callback if pointer at offset 0x15 exists
7. Execute optional custom callback if function pointer at offset 0x17 exists

Parameters:
- pScrollbar (int): Scrollbar handle/context (passed via ECX)
- pScrollbarData (int *): Pointer to scrollbar structure (D2WIN_SCROLLBAR)
- nDelta (int): Position delta (positive = forward/down, negative = back/up)

Returns:
- 0 (success)

Structure Layout (pScrollbarData offsets):
- 0x13 (19): Current position (clamped)
- 0x12 (18): Maximum position
- 0x10 (16): Forward flag
- 0x11 (17): Backward flag
- 0x15 (21): Position change callback
- 0x16 (22): Disabled flag
- 0x17 (23): Custom change callback

functions.name: SetScrollbarValue
functions.comment:
Sets the value field of a scrollbar control structure.

Algorithm:
1. Validate control type == 5 (scrollbar), assert on mismatch
2. Write nValue to control field at offset 0x50 (index 0x14)

Parameters:
- pControl (int*): Pointer to scrollbar control structure
- nValue (int): Value to write at offset 0x50

Returns:
- void: Asserts on type validation failure

functions.name: ScrollbarGetField14
functions.comment:
Retrieves scrollbar field at offset 0x14.

Algorithm:
1. Validate scrollbar structure type (eType must be 5)
2. If invalid, trigger FogAssert and terminate with error code
3. Return field at offset 0x14 (20 bytes) from scrollbar

Parameters:

functions.name: RenderScrollbarControl
functions.comment:
Renders scrollbar control visual elements (up arrow, track, thumb, down arrow).

Classification: Callback - Assigned at offset 0x1c in CreateScrollbarObject, invoked for rendering.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pScrollbarData != NULL (assert ptChild)
2. Validate *pScrollbarData == 5 (scrollbar type check)
3. Check visibility flags via gdwBitMasks_exref bits 0x01 and 0x08
4. Extract style (offset 0x04), Y pos (offset 0x0C), X pos (offset 0x10), height (offset 0x18)
5. If max scroll value (offset 0x48) is 0, return 1 (nothing to render)
6. Check game state - clear mouse tracking if not in game
7. If mouse tracking active (offset 0x58), call ProcessScrollbarMousePos
8. Initialize 18-dword render params array to zero
9. Render up arrow: style = pressed(2) or normal(1), call GfxInterfaceCall84
10. Loop: render track segments every 10 pixels with style=5
11. Render down arrow: style = pressed(2) or normal(0)
12. Calculate thumb position: ((height-30) * currentPos / maxPos) - height + 19 + Y
13. Render thumb with style=4
14. Return 1

Parameters:
- pScrollbarData (ECX): Pointer to 96-byte scrollbar control structure
  Offset 0x00: eType (must be 5 for scrollbar)
  Offset 0x04: nStyle
  Offset 0x08: dwFlags (visibility/enabled bits)
  Offset 0x0C: nY
  Offset 0x10: nX  
  Offset 0x18: nHeight
  Offset 0x40: fUpArrowPressed
  Offset 0x44: fDownArrowPressed
  Offset 0x48: nMaxScrollValue
  Offset 0x4C: nCurrentScrollPos
  Offset 0x58: fMouseTracking

Returns:
- 1: Rendered successfully or nothing to render (max=0)
- 0: Control not visible or not enabled

Magic Numbers:
- 5: Scrollbar type ID
- 0x12 (18): Render params array size in dwords
- 10: Track segment height in pixels
- 0x1e (30): Combined arrow button heights (15 + 15)
- 0x13 (19): Thumb position offset adjustment

Caller: Referenced as callback at offset 0x1c by CreateScrollbarObject
