functions.name: ResetScrollbarStateFields
functions.comment:
Resets scrollbar state tracking fields to zero.

NOTE: Function body is malformed in Ghidra (single instruction visible).
Manual recreation needed to fix boundaries. Full code extends to 0x6f91106d.

Classification: Callback - invoked from scrollbar objects (stored at +0x28)

Algorithm:
1. Get scrollbar object pointer from stack parameter [ESP+4]
2. Dereference to get pointer to ScrollbarObject structure
3. Verify dwObjectType field == 5 (scrollbar type), assert fatal if not
4. Check if dwStateField1 (offset 0x40) is non-zero
5. Check if dwStateField2 (offset 0x44) is non-zero
6. Check if dwStateField3 (offset 0x58) is non-zero
7. If all three fields are zero, return FALSE (nothing to reset)
8. If any field is non-zero, clear all three state fields to zero
9. Return TRUE indicating state was reset

Parameters:
- pScrollbar (ScrollbarObject*): Pointer to scrollbar UI object structure

Returns:
- TRUE (1): State fields were non-zero and have been cleared
- FALSE (0): All state fields were already zero, no action taken

ScrollbarObject Structure Layout:
Offset  Size  Field            Type    Description
+0x00   4     dwObjectType     uint    Must be 5 for scrollbar
+0x04   4     dwStyle          uint    Style flags
+0x08   4     dwFlags          uint    Bit mask flags
+0x0C   4     nX               int     X position
+0x10   4     nY               int     Y position
+0x14   4     nWidth           int     Width
+0x18   4     nHeight          int     Height
+0x1C   4     pfnCallback1     void*   First callback function
+0x24   4     pfnMouseHandler  void*   ProcessScrollbarMousePos
+0x28   4     pfnStateCallback void*   This function (ResetScrollbarStateFields)
+0x34   4     nIndex           int     Index value
+0x40   4     dwStateField1    uint    First tracked state value
+0x44   4     dwStateField2    uint    Second tracked state value
+0x58   4     dwStateField3    uint    Third tracked state value

Magic Numbers:
- 5: Object type ID for scrollbar
- 0x1B0 (432): Assert error code (source line number)

Cross-References:
- CreateScrollbarObject stores this callback at object +0x28
- ProcessScrollbarMousePos stored at +0x24 for mouse input handling

functions.name: ValidateSmackDataAndInitGraphics

Validates Smack video data structure and initializes graphics interface.

KNOWN ISSUE: Function has incomplete boundaries in Ghidra (only entry byte 0x6f9112c0

   - Mask2: gdwBitMasks_exref[2] (offset +8)

      - Call Ordinal_10038(pSmackData+0x140) - D2Gfx path resolution
      - Call Ordinal_10036(pSmackData+0x40, pSmackData+0x140, EBP) - D2Gfx path combine

   b. Clear g_dwFileDeleteDisabled to 0

6. Call InitializeGraphicsInterface(pSmackData+0x140)
7. Return 1 (success)

Parameters:

  - Offset 0x00: eType - Must be 9 for valid SMACK type
  - Offset 0x08: dwFlags - Checked against gdwBitMasks for initialization conditions
  - Offset 0x40: szFilename[256] - Video filename buffer
  - Offset 0x140: GraphicsData - Graphics interface data (passed to init)

Returns:

- 0 (FALSE): Bit mask conditions not met, no initialization performed

- Ordinal_10036: D2Gfx - Combines filename with resolved path (3 params)

functions.comment:

1. Validate pTextBox is non-NULL and type is 4 (TEXTBOX)

5. Apply CJK font height adjustments for locales 7 (Chinese) and 9 (Korean)
6. Calculate initial render Y from font height, text area, and margins
7. Handle horizontal auto-scroll (flag 0x40): adjust scroll offset by text width
8. Handle vertical auto-scroll (flag 0x80): advance to next line if offset < -lineHeight
9. Iterate through text line linked list starting at pTextBox[0x14]
10. For each line, iterate through columns (0 to pTextBox[0x19])
11. Calculate column X position based on alignment: 0x02=center, 0x10=right-align
12. Copy column text to buffer, truncate to fit available column width
13. Render text: selected line uses RenderMultilineUnicodeText, others use standard render
14. Advance Y by line height + line spacing (pTextBox[0x28] or pTextBox[0x29])
15. Continue until lines exhausted or remaining height insufficient
16. Restore default font (1) and return success (1)

Parameters:
- pTextBox (ECX): Pointer to text box UI object (type 4)
  Offset 0x00: Type (must be 4)
  Offset 0x04: Parent handle
  Offset 0x08: Visibility flags
  Offset 0x0C: X position
  Offset 0x10: Y position
  Offset 0x14: Width
  Offset 0x18: Height
  Offset 0x40: Padding left
  Offset 0x44: Padding top
  Offset 0x50: Text line list head (linked list of text lines)
  Offset 0x58: Highlighted line index
  Offset 0x5C: Options flags
  Offset 0x60: Selected line index
  Offset 0x64: Column count
  Offset 0x94: Font index
  Offset 0x9C: Scroll X offset
  Offset 0xA0: Line spacing (char)
  Offset 0xA4: Line spacing (non-char)

Options Flags (offset 0x5C):
  0x01: Selectable (enable line selection highlighting)
  0x02: Center align text
  0x10: Right align text  
  0x20: Auto-enabled with 0x01
  0x40: Horizontal auto-scroll
  0x80: Vertical auto-scroll

Returns:
- 0: Text box invisible or invalid
- 1: Rendered successfully

Special Cases:
- Locales 7 and 9 get CJK-specific font height adjustments (6-8 pixels extra)
- Selected line (flag 0x01) renders with multiline function for highlight
- Horizontal scroll (flag 0x40) auto-scrolls text wider than box
- Vertical scroll (flag 0x80) advances visible line when scrolled past top

Text Line Structure (at pTextBox[0x14]):
  Offset 0x00-0x10: Column text pointers (up to 5 columns)
  Offset 0x14: Color/style value
  Offset 0x18: Char flag (affects line spacing)
  Offset 0x1C: Next line pointer (linked list)

5. Check bit mask at gdwBitMasks[0] against flags - return 0 if not set
6. Check nLineCount (offset 0x54) >= 1 - return 0 if no lines
7. Check dwOptions bit 0x1 (offset 0x5C) - skip calculation if not set
8. Calculate relative Y: nRelativeY = (nY - nX) + g_nScreenWidth
9. Set active font to pTextData->nFontId (offset 0x94)

    - Get font height property
    - If height < 14: g_dwCJKFontHeight = (height > 7) ? 7 : 6
    - Else: g_dwCJKFontHeight = 8

13. If dwOptions bit 0x8 set: clamp to [0, nLineCount-1]
14. Else: if out of bounds [0, nLineCount), set to -1
15. If pMessageHandler (offset 0x34) is null, return 0
16. Call pMessageHandler(ppParams) and return its result

ppParams - Pointer to pointer to TextData structure (stack param)

0x08    4     dwFlags         Bit mask flags
0x10    4     nX              X position

0x5C    4     dwOptions       Option flags (bit 0x1, 0x8)
0x60    4     nHoverLine      Calculated hover line index

functions.name: HandleTextListKeyNavigation
functions.comment:
Handles keyboard navigation input for text list UI controls.

Classification: Callback/Handler - stored at UIObject offset 0x0C when dwOptions & 1.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pUIObject pointer is non-null (assert pParams->window)
2. Validate object type equals 4 (TextDataType assertion)

4. Check item count at offset 0x54 (piVar1[0x15]) is >= 1
5. Check selection index at offset 0x60 (piVar1[0x18]) is not -1
6. Call GetLastInputTime() - return 0 if input recently processed
7. Cache scroll position (offset 0x58), selection (0x60), item count (0x54)
8. Calculate visible row count using font metrics:
   - SetActiveFont with font ID from offset 0x94
   - Apply CJK font height adjustment for locales 7 (Chinese) and 9 (Korean)
   - visibleRows = (height - 2*margin - charHeight) / (fontHeight + CJKOffset)
9. Switch on key code at pUIObject[2]:
   - 0x21 (VK_PRIOR/Page Up): Scroll up by visible rows
   - 0x22 (VK_NEXT/Page Down): Scroll down by visible rows  
   - 0x23 (VK_END): Jump to last item
   - 0x24 (VK_HOME): Jump to first item
   - 0x26 (VK_UP): Move selection up one row
   - 0x28 (VK_DOWN): Move selection down one row
10. Update selection index at offset 0x60
11. If scroll position changed, call ScrollbarNavigateToIndex
12. If selection changed and callback at offset 0x34 exists, invoke it
13. Return 0

Parameters:
- pUIObject (int *): Pointer to UI object structure, key code at [2]

Returns:
- 0: Always returns 0 (navigation handled)

Offset  Field               Description
0x00    pChildWindow        Pointer to child window structure
0x08    dwFlags             Visibility/state flags
0x18    nY                  Y position
0x34    pfnSelectionChanged Selection change callback  
0x44    nHeight             Control height
0x54    nItemCount          Total items in list
0x58    nScrollPosition     Current scroll offset
0x60    nSelectedIndex      Currently selected item (-1 = none)
0x94    nFontId             Font identifier

Virtual Key Codes:
0x21 = VK_PRIOR (Page Up)
0x22 = VK_NEXT (Page Down)
0x23 = VK_END
0x24 = VK_HOME
0x26 = VK_UP
0x28 = VK_DOWN

Special Cases:
- Returns early (0) if control invisible, empty, or no selection
- Returns early if GetLastInputTime() returns non-zero (rate limiting)
- CJK locales (7=Chinese, 9=Korean) use adjusted font height calculation
- Selection callback at offset 0x34 only invoked when selection actually changes

Algorithm:
1. Iterate through critical section array starting at g_ppCriticalSections
2. For each critical section pointer encountered before g_pCriticalSection1:
   - Skip if NULL pointer
   - Skip if pointer matches one of the special critical sections (g_pCriticalSection1-3 or g_pCriticalSectionArray)
   - Delete the critical section with DeleteCriticalSection()
   - Call cleanup handler FUN_6f916a9e() on the section
3. Increment pointer by 4 bytes and continue until reaching g_pCriticalSectionArray end
4. Explicitly delete the four special critical sections

Parameters:
- None

Returns:
- void (implicit EDI = DeleteCriticalSection function pointer loaded from [0x6f91d264])

functions.name: AcquireCriticalSectionIndex
functions.comment:
Acquire critical section by index, initializing if necessary.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate pointer to critical section entry in global array
2. Check if already initialized; if yes, enter and return
3. Allocate memory for CRITICAL_SECTION structure (0x18 bytes)
4. If allocation fails, exit with error code 0x11
5. Lock initialization via AcquireCriticalSectionIndex(0x11) (recursive)
6. Initialize critical section if still null
7. Unlock initialization via FUN_6f914e7d(0x11)
8. Enter the critical section

Parameters:
- nIndex (uint): Index into global critical section array (0x11 is special init lock)

Returns:
- void

Related Functions:
- FUN_6f914e7d: Release critical section lock

functions.name: ReleaseCriticalSectionIndex
functions.comment:
Releases a critical section by index from the global critical section table.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve critical section pointer from g_ppCriticalSections array using index
2. Call LeaveCriticalSection on the retrieved critical section

Parameters:
- nIndex (dword): Index into g_ppCriticalSections array

Returns:
- void

functions.name: ConvertCharacter
functions.comment:
Converts a character using either simple ASCII uppercase-to-lowercase conversion or a complex lookup-based conversion.

Algorithm:
1. Check if g_dwStringCompareMode is 0 (simple conversion mode)
2. If simple mode and input is uppercase letter (0x41-0x5A), return input + 0x20 (convert to lowercase)
3. If complex mode, acquire semaphore/critical section 0x13
4. Call FUN_6f914f01 for character conversion lookup
5. Release critical section and decrement semaphore count
6. Return converted character value

Parameters:
- chInput (uint): Character code to convert

Returns:
- uint: Converted character code

functions.name: TransformCharacterCase
functions.signature: dword TransformCharacterCase(void * this, void * pThis, dword nChar)
functions.comment:
Transforms character case based on global character transformation mode.

Algorithm:
1. Check g_dwStringCompareMode for transformation strategy
2. If mode 0 (ASCII): Convert uppercase A-Z (0x41-0x5A) to lowercase by adding 0x20
3. If mode > 0: Check character code against 0x100 threshold
4. For chars < 0x100, check g_dwCharacterTransformMode:
   - If < 2: Use lookup in g_pCharacterTransformTable at offset param*2
   - If >= 2: Call FUN_6f91508e for transformation
5. If transformable, extract high/low bytes and apply table flag 0x80
6. Call FUN_6f917328 to perform full string comparison transformation
7. Extract result byte(s) from comparison and mask appropriately

Parameters:
- pThis (void*): Context pointer (ECX register, __thiscall)
- nChar (dword): Character code to transform (0x0-0x10000)

Returns:
- dword: Transformed character value (8-16 bits used, upper bits 0)

functions.name: CalculateItemSlotPosition
functions.signature: int CalculateItemSlotPosition(int nCharCode, int nEquipSlot, int nBaseOffset, int nRow, int nCol, int nPageOffset, int nCopyMode)
functions.comment:
Calculates the memory position of an item slot for display/storage.

Algorithm:
1. Validate nCharCode is in valid range (0x76c - 0x7f6)
2. Look up base offset for equipment slot from table at DAT_6f9221f4
3. Apply slot alignment adjustment if nCharCode is 4-byte aligned and nEquipSlot > 2
4. Calculate position as (nRow + (slot offset * 0x18)) * 0x3c + nCol, then * 0x3c
5. Add base table offset (DAT_6f922110 + 0x7c558180 + nPageOffset)
6. If nCopyMode==1 or copy verification succeeds, add DAT_6f922118 offset

Parameters:
- nCharCode (int): Character/item code to validate (0x76c-0x7f6 range)
- nEquipSlot (int): Equipment slot index for lookup table
- nBaseOffset (int): Base offset to add to table value
- nRow (int): Row coordinate for position calculation
- nCol (int): Column coordinate for position calculation
- nPageOffset (int): Page/view offset value
- nCopyMode (int): 1=copy mode enabled, -1=conditional copy, other=normal

Returns:
- Calculated position value (typically memory offset), or -1 if nCharCode is invalid

functions.name: TransformCharacterWithFlags
functions.signature: dword TransformCharacterWithFlags(void * this, void * pThis, int nCharCode, dword dwMask)
functions.comment:
Transforms a character code using the character transformation table with a bitmask.

Algorithm:
1. Check if character code is in valid range (0-256)
2. If in range, look up transformed value from table directly
3. If out of range, check high byte flag in table for multi-byte transformation
4. If flag set, construct 2-byte transform data and call handler; otherwise 1-byte
5. AND result with provided bitmask and return

Parameters:
- pThis (void*): Context pointer
- nCharCode (int): Character code to transform
- dwMask (dword): Bitmask to apply to result

Returns:
- Transformed character value masked with dwMask, or 0 on transform failure

functions.name: BufferWriteByte
functions.comment:
Write a byte value to a buffer, handling buffer state transitions and overflow conditions.

Algorithm:
1. Extract buffer state flags from pBuffer[3]
2. If buffer is uninitialized (flags & 0x82 == 0) or already has data flag (flags & 0x40), set DATA_PRESENT flag
3. Otherwise, handle existing data:
   - If current pointer at start (flags & 1), reset buffer to beginning
   - Mark buffer modified (flags &= ~0x1)
   - Clear flags indicating data state, set modified flag (flags |= 0x2)
4. If buffer is not protected (!(flags & 0x10c)), validate buffer node:
   - Skip special nodes (g_pDefaultBufferNode1, g_pDefaultBufferNode2)
   - Call validation function if conditions met
5. Write byte:
   - If write area is empty, allocate from buffer pool
   - Otherwise append to existing data
6. Return byte value if write succeeds, 0xFFFFFFFF if fails

Parameters:
- byteValue (dword): Byte to write (masked to 0xFF)
- pBuffer (int*): Pointer to buffer node structure

Returns:
- 0xFF if write succeeds
- 0xFFFFFFFF on failure

functions.name: SprintfxVa
functions.signature: int SprintfxVa(int * pBuffer, byte * pFormat, int * pVaList)
functions.comment:
Format string processing engine for sprintfx family.

Algorithm:
1. Parse format string byte by byte, using state machine (g_abStateTable)
2. For each format specifier, extract modifiers (flags, width, precision)
3. Process conversion specifiers (d,i,u,x,X,o,c,s,S,p,n,e,E,f,F,g,G)
4. Handle width/precision padding with spaces and zeros
5. Output formatted data via buffer callback (param_1)
6. Return total characters output in pBuffer[0]

Parameters:
- pBuffer (int*): Output buffer control block (pBuffer[0]=callback routine)
- pFormat (byte*): Format string in ASCII (null-terminated)
- pVaList (int*): Variable argument list pointer array

Returns:
- Count of characters written to output buffer

Flag Bits (dwFlags/local_8):
- 0x001: Force sign (+)
- 0x002: Space padding for positives
- 0x004: Left-align (negate 0x008)
- 0x008: Zero-pad
- 0x010: Short integer (h modifier)
- 0x020: Char conversion or unsigned short
- 0x040: Float/double conversion (e,E,f,F,g,G)
- 0x080: # modifier (alternate form)
- 0x100: Negative value flag (internal)
- 0x200: Octal alternate (0 prefix)
- 0x800: Wide character (w modifier)
- 0x1000: Uppercase hex
- 0x8000: 64-bit integer (I64 modifier)

State Machine (g_abStateTable):
- State 0: Initial, output literal characters
- State 1: Start format specifier (%)
- State 2: Parse flags (-, +, space, #, 0)
- State 3: Parse width or * wildcard
- State 4: Period before precision
- State 5: Parse precision digits or * wildcard
- State 6: Length modifiers (h, l, L, w, I64)
- State 7: Conversion specifier (d, s, f, etc)

Related: ProcessBufferCleanup, FUN_6f9159fa (va_arg), _strlen

functions.name: BufferWriteByteWithCount
functions.signature: void BufferWriteByteWithCount(dword byValue, int * pnByteCount, int * pnErrorCount)
functions.comment:
Writes a byte to a buffer and tracks the byte count.

Algorithm:
1. Decrement byteCount to check if space available
2. If count < 0: Call BufferWriteByte (buffer full)
3. Else: Write byte directly to buffer and increment buffer pointer
4. Check for error (0xffffffff) and update error counter

Parameters:
- byValue (dword): Byte value to write (0-255)
- pnByteCount (int*): Pointer to buffer position/available count
- pnErrorCount (int*): Pointer to error/written count tracker

Returns:
- void

functions.name: WriteCharacterRepeated
functions.signature: void WriteCharacterRepeated(uint dwByteChar, int nCount, int * pBuffer, int * pStatus)
functions.comment:
Outputs a single character repeated multiple times to a formatted output buffer.

Algorithm:
1. Loop while nCount > 0, decrementing nCount each iteration
2. Call sub-function to write byChar to buffer
3. Check for write error (*pStatus == -1) and exit early if detected

Parameters:
- byChar (uint): Character to output (0x00-0xFF)
- nCount (int): Number of times to repeat the character
- pBuffer (int*): Output buffer state/context pointer
- pStatus (int*): Output status; incremented on each write, set to -1 on error

Returns:
- void; status reported via *pStatus output parameter

functions.name: BufferWriteBytes
functions.signature: void BufferWriteBytes(char * pchSrc, int nCount, int * pdwBuffer, int * pnResult)
functions.comment:
Writes a sequence of bytes to a buffer, checking for errors.

Algorithm:
1. Loop while nCount > 0
2. Decrement nCount
3. Read byte from pbSrc and advance pointer
4. Call BufferWriteByteWithCount to write byte
5. Exit if result indicates error (pnResult == -1)

Parameters:
- pbSrc (char*): Source bytes to write
- nCount (int): Number of bytes to write
- pdwBuffer (int*): Buffer pointer for output
- pnResult (int*): Result counter, set to -1 on error

Returns:
- void (modifies pdwBuffer and pnResult by reference)

functions.name: VaArgExtractor
functions.comment:
Extract next argument from variable argument list.

Algorithm:
1. Increment the argument list pointer by 4 bytes (sizeof int)
2. Return value at pointer offset -4 bytes (previous position)

Parameters:
- pVaList (int*): Pointer to current position in argument array

Returns:
- uint: Next argument value from the variable argument list

functions.name: ExtractVaArg64
functions.comment:
Extracts and advances a 64-bit value from a va_arg list.

Algorithm:
1. Load the argument offset pointer from stack parameter
2. Retrieve the current offset value from the pointer
3. Extract the 8-byte value at (offset - 8)
4. Increment the offset by 8 bytes
5. Return the extracted 64-bit value in EDX:EAX

Parameters:
- pArgOffset (int*): Pointer to current argument offset counter
  Incremented by 8 after extraction for next va_arg call

Returns:
- 64-bit unsigned value (ulonglong) at current va_arg position

functions.name: VaArgExtractWide
functions.comment:
Extract wide character from va_list, advancing pointer by 4 bytes.

Algorithm:
1. Load pointer from pVaList parameter
2. Increment the value at that pointer by 4 (advance va_list)
3. Extract upper 16 bits of new value and lower 16 bits from offset -4
4. Return combined 32-bit value

Parameters:
- pVaList (int*): Pointer to va_list pointer (modified by function)

Returns:
- dword: Extracted value combining upper 16 bits of current and lower 16 bits of previous value

Related: SprintfxVa (caller), wide character format specifier processing

functions.name: InitializeProcessorCache
functions.comment:
Initializes processor cache and memory management subsystem.

Algorithm:
1. Invoke cache configuration routine with context pointer
2. Pass cache block size constant (0x10000)
3. Pass cache range limit constant (0x30000)
4. Configure processor memory optimization settings

Parameters:
- pContext (void*): Processor context structure, passed via ECX register for __fastcall

Returns:
- void

Magic Numbers:
- 0x10000 (65536): Cache block/page size in bytes
- 0x30000 (196608): Cache range limit for memory management

functions.name: CheckCycleModuloThreshold
functions.comment:
Checks if the modulo remainder of dividend exceeds threshold.

Algorithm:
1. Load divisor from global
2. Load dividend from global
3. Compute (dividend / divisor) * divisor to get quotient product
4. Subtract from dividend to compute remainder
5. Compare remainder against threshold from global
6. Return 1 if remainder < threshold, 0 otherwise

Parameters:
- IMPLICIT: g_dDivisor - divisor for modulo operation
- IMPLICIT: g_dDividend - dividend value
- IMPLICIT: g_dCycleThreshold - threshold for comparison

Returns:
- 1 if (dividend % divisor) < threshold
- 0 otherwise

functions.name: DetectProcessorFeature
functions.comment:
Detects processor features using Windows API.

Algorithm:
1. Load KERNEL32 module
2. Get address of IsProcessorFeaturePresent API
3. Call IsProcessorFeaturePresent(0) if available
4. Fall back to FUN_6f915a37 if API unavailable

Parameters:
- IMPLICIT: None (no parameters)

Returns:
- void

Related Functions:
- InitializeProcessorState (caller)
- FUN_6f915a37 (fallback initialization)

functions.name: TransformStringCharacters
functions.comment:
Transforms and swaps characters in a string using conversion table.

Algorithm:
1. Convert first character to determine if any transformation needed
2. If transformation required, iterate through string characters
3. For each character, check transformation mode and apply conversion rules
4. Once done, perform reverse swap starting with global swap byte value
5. Swap characters from start until null terminator reached

Parameters:
- szString (char*): Pointer to string to transform and swap

Returns:
- void

Magic Numbers:
- 0x65: Character value for 'e' (transformation check)
- 0x4: Transform flags bit mask
- 0x2: Stride in character transformation table

functions.name: FormatDoubleToString
functions.signature: char * FormatDoubleToString(double * pdblValue, char * pszBuffer, int nWidth, int nFlags)
functions.comment:
Converts a double-precision floating-point number to a formatted string representation.

Algorithm:
1. Extract lower and upper 32-bits of the double value
2. Format the mantissa and exponent into local buffers
3. Adjust output buffer pointer based on sign and field width
4. Write the formatted digits to the output buffer

Parameters:
- pdblValue (double*): Pointer to the double value to convert
- pszBuffer (char*): Output buffer for the formatted string
- nWidth (int): Minimum field width for output (0 or positive)
- nFlags (int): Format flags controlling precision and notation

Returns:
- char*: Pointer to the output buffer (same as pszBuffer)

functions.name: FormatExponentString
functions.signature: BYTE * FormatExponentString(BYTE * pbBuffer, int nDigitCount, int nExponent, int * pnExponentState, char cNegative)
functions.comment:
Formats floating-point number in exponential notation (e.g., "1.23e+045").

Algorithm:
1. If cNegative flag set, prepend '-' sign to buffer
2. If nDigitCount > 0, move first digit to output position and place swap character (g_byCharacterSwapValue)
3. Call FUN_6f916ea0 to append exponent string "e+000" to buffer
4. If nExponent != 0, write 'E' marker and format exponent digits (hundreds, tens, ones)
5. Return pointer to start of buffer

Parameters:
- pbBuffer (BYTE*): Output string buffer for exponential format
- nDigitCount (int): Number of significant digits to format
- nExponent (int): Exponent value to append
- pnExponentState (int*): Exponent state flags [0]=sign mode, [1]=exponent value, [3]=digits ready
- cNegative (char): Non-zero if number is negative (adds leading '-')

Returns:
- Pointer to pbBuffer (input buffer)

functions.name: DoubleToDecimalString
functions.signature: char * DoubleToDecimalString(double * pdValue, char * pszBuffer, size_t nSize)
functions.comment:
Converts a double-precision float to a decimal string representation.

Algorithm:
1. Extracts sign bit and exponent from the double value
2. Formats the significant digits into a buffer with proper padding
3. Appends null terminator to the output string
4. Returns the formatted buffer pointer

Parameters:
- pdValue (double*): Pointer to the double value to convert
- pszBuffer (char*): Output buffer for the decimal string
- nSize (size_t): Size of the output buffer

Returns:
- Pointer to pszBuffer containing the formatted decimal string

functions.name: FormatNumberString
functions.signature: char * FormatNumberString(char * szBuffer, size_t nDecimalPlaces, int * pnValues, char cCondition)
functions.comment:
Formats a numeric value into a string with sign, decimal point, and zero-padding.

Algorithm:
1. If condition flag set and decimal places equals remaining string length, append '0' and null terminator
2. If value is negative (0x2d = '-'), prepend '-' to output string
3. If decimal places < 1, write '0' at current position and advance pointer
4. Otherwise advance pointer by decimal places count
5. If decimal places > 0, write decimal separator character at current position
6. If decimal places < 0 (fractional part), fill remaining positions with padding zeros

Parameters:
- szBuffer (char*): Output string buffer
- nDecimalPlaces (size_t): Decimal point position or count
- pnValues (int*): Array containing [sign_value, decimal_position]
- fCondition (char): Flag controlling null-termination behavior

Returns:
- Pointer to szBuffer (start of formatted string)

functions.name: FormatDoubleString
functions.signature: void FormatDoubleString(double * pValue, char * szBuffer, size_t nSize, int nFormat)
functions.comment:
Formats a double value to a decimal or exponential string representation.

Algorithm:
1. Extract mantissa and exponent from double via FUN_6f91888e
2. Format mantissa digits with FUN_6f918817
3. Determine if exponential format needed (exponent < -4 or >= size)
4. If exponential: format with exponent using FormatExponentString
5. If normal: adjust decimal point and format with FormatNumberString

Parameters:
- pValue (double*): Pointer to double value to format
- szBuffer (char*): Output buffer for formatted string
- nSize (size_t): Maximum buffer size
- nFormat (int): Format flags (precision/type)

Returns:
- void (string written to szBuffer)

Notes:
- local_2c: Temporary storage for mantissa digits (6 uint slots)
- Register temporaries (EAX, EDI) used for intermediate calculations

functions.name: InsertStringAtOffset
functions.comment:
Inserts space at offset by shifting string contents.

Algorithm:
1. Check if offset is non-zero
2. Get length of source string (including null terminator)
3. Copy string and terminator from source to offset position

Parameters:
- pszBuffer (char*): Null-terminated string buffer with space at offset
- nOffset (int): Byte offset to insert at

Returns:
- void

functions.name: InitializeThreadLocalStorage
functions.comment:
Initializes thread-local storage (TLS) for the module.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize synchronization objects
2. Allocate TLS slot via TlsAlloc()
3. Allocate TLS data structure (0x74 bytes)
4. Associate data with TLS slot
5. Initialize thread ID and sync marker in TLS data

Parameters:
None

Returns:
1 on success, 0 if allocation or initialization fails

functions.name: CleanupThreadLocalStorage
functions.comment:
Cleanup thread-local storage resources during module termination.

Algorithm:
1. Call CleanupCriticalSections to destroy all critical section objects
2. Free the TLS index if it has been allocated (not INVALID_INDEX 0xFFFFFFFF)
3. Reset TLS index to INVALID_INDEX to prevent reuse

Parameters:
- IMPLICIT: Uses global g_dwThreadLocalStorageIndex

Returns:
- void (no return value)

functions.name: InitializeThreadLocalStorageData
functions.comment:
Initializes thread-local storage (TLS) data structure fields.

Algorithm:
1. Set offset 0x50 to point to function pointer table (0x6f9224e0)
2. Set offset 0x14 to 1 (initialization flag)

Parameters:
- pTlsData (void*): Pointer to allocated TLS data structure (0x74 bytes)

Returns:
- void

functions.name: GetThreadLocalStorage
functions.comment:
Acquires or initializes thread-local storage for the current thread.

Algorithm:
1. Save current error code to restore later
2. Get TLS slot from global storage index
3. If slot is empty, allocate and initialize new TLS block
4. Store thread ID and initialize default value (-1) in TLS
5. Restore original error code
6. Return pointer to TLS block

Parameters:
- None (implicit: Uses global g_dwThreadLocalStorageIndex)

Returns:
- DWORD*: Pointer to thread-local storage block (never NULL, calls exit on failure)

functions.name: CleanupThreadLocalStorage
functions.comment:
Cleans up thread-local storage by destructing pointers.

Algorithm:
1. Check if TLS index is valid (not 0xFFFFFFFF)
2. Get TLS data pointer from parameter or from TlsGetValue()
3. For each cleanup pointer offset (0x24, 0x28, 0x30, 0x38, 0x40, 0x44, 0x50):
   - Read pointer from structure
   - If non-NULL and not the function table, call cleanup function
4. Call cleanup on the structure itself
5. Clear TLS value via TlsSetValue(0)

Parameters:
- pTlsData (void*): TLS data structure pointer; if NULL, retrieves from TlsGetValue()
- IMPLICIT: g_dwThreadLocalStorageIndex contains TLS slot index

Returns:
- void

Magic Numbers:
- 0x24, 0x28, 0x30, 0x38, 0x40, 0x44, 0x50: Offsets to cleanup pointers in structure
- 0xFFFFFFFF: Invalid TLS index sentinel

functions.name: InitializeStdioHandles
functions.comment:
Initializes standard I/O handle tables from startup info.

Algorithm:
1. Allocate primary buffer table (0x480 bytes) storing 288 handle entry slots
2. Initialize each slot: set handle to 0xffffffff, flags to 0, reserve byte to 10
3. Call GetStartupInfoA to retrieve inherited startup parameters
4. If startup info provides inherited handles, process each via GetFileType
5. Allocate extended buffers if inherited handle count exceeds 288
6. Initialize extended buffer entries with same default values
7. Map each inherited handle to appropriate table entry based on handle index
8. For stdin/stdout/stderr (indices 0-2), retrieve via GetStdHandle
9. Validate file types and set appropriate flags (regular/pipe/device)
10. Call SetHandleCount to register total handle count with runtime

Parameters:
- IMPLICIT: g_dwHandleLimit (initial handle limit, incremented as buffers allocated)
- IMPLICIT: g_pBufferTable (main handle table allocated by _malloc)
- IMPLICIT: g_pBufferTableExtended (extended buffer pointers for overflow)

Returns:
- void (initializes global handle management structures)

Magic Numbers:
- 0x480: Bytes per handle buffer (288 entries * 4 bytes + 96 overhead)
- 0x120: Maximum entries per primary buffer table
- 0x7ff: Maximum inherited handle count (2047)
- 0x800: Clamped handle limit (2048)
- 0x20: Initial handle increment (32 entries)
- 0xffffffff: Sentinel for uninitialized handle slot

functions.name: CleanupBufferTables
functions.comment:
Cleanup all buffer tables by destroying critical sections and freeing allocated memory.

Algorithm:
1. Iterate through array of buffer table pointers at 0x6f9cf1c0-0x6f9cf2c0
2. For each buffer table, iterate through 0x480 bytes of entries (stride 0x24)
3. If entry has active critical section (SpinCount != 0), call DeleteCriticalSection
4. Call FUN_6f916a9e to free the entire buffer table
5. Clear the buffer table pointer

Parameters:
- IMPLICIT: Global buffer table array at 0x6f9cf1c0

Returns:
- void (always succeeds)

Magic Numbers:
- 0x480 (1152): Size of each buffer table allocation
- 0x24 (36): Stride between entries in buffer table
- 0xc: Offset to critical section from buffer entry
- 0x6f9cf1c0-0x6f9cf2c0: Array of buffer table pointers

functions.name: InitializeCommandLineArguments
functions.comment:
Initializes parsed command-line arguments array and sets initialization flags.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize module library if not already done
2. Count non-null argument entries in command line string
3. Allocate array for argument pointers
4. Copy each argument from command line to allocated buffers
5. Mark processing complete and set parsed arguments pointer

Parameters:
- IMPLICIT: g_pCommandLine contains raw command-line string

Returns:
- void (exits program on allocation failure via __amsg_exit)

Magic Numbers:
- 4: Size of pointer in allocated array
- 0x0: Sentinel value to mark array end

functions.name: InitializeModuleData
functions.comment:
Initializes module item data structures.

Algorithm:
1. Check if module is already initialized (g_fInitialized)
2. Get module file path via GetModuleFileNameA
3. Use command line path if available, otherwise use module path
4. First scan to count items and determine buffer size
5. Allocate buffer for item data (size = nItemCount * 4 + nBufferSize)
6. Second scan to populate item pointers and data
7. Store global references to item array and count

Parameters:
- void: No parameters (uses global state)

Returns:
- void

Magic Numbers:
- 0x104: Path buffer size (260 bytes)
- 4: Bytes per item reference
- -1: Item count adjustment for array indexing

functions.name: ParseCommandLine
functions.signature: void ParseCommandLine(byte * pbInputString, uint * * ppdwArgumentPtrs, byte * pbOutputBuffer, int * pnInputLength, int * pnArgumentCount)
functions.comment:
Parses a command-line string into individual arguments, handling quoted strings and escape sequences.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize output length counter to 0, argument count to 1
2. If argument pointers array exists, store initial output buffer pointer
3. Parse input string character by character:
   - If string starts with quote (0x22), extract quoted substring handling escapes
   - Otherwise parse unquoted substring until space/tab/null terminator
   - Backslash (0x5c) escapes the next character when not in quotes
   - Special handling for escaped quotes: pair of quotes when escaping active
4. Build individual argument strings in output buffer with null terminators
5. Store pointers to each argument in argument pointer array
6. Return via output parameters

Parameters:
- pbInputString (byte*): Command-line string to parse
- ppdwArgumentPtrs (uint**): Array of pointers to parsed arguments (optional, NULL to skip)
- pbOutputBuffer (byte*): Buffer for parsed argument strings (optional, NULL to skip writing)
- pnInputLength (int*): Returns count of characters consumed from input
- pnArgumentCount (int*): Returns count of arguments parsed

Returns:
- void (results via output parameters)

Magic Numbers:
- 0x22 (34): Double-quote character
- 0x20 (32): Space character
- 0x9 (9): Tab character
- 0x5c (92): Backslash escape character
- 0x4: Character class flag (special/escape-able character)

functions.name: GetCachedEnvironmentStrings
functions.comment:
Retrieves cached environment strings, converting Unicode to ANSI on first call.

Algorithm:
1. Check static flag g_dwEnvStringState to determine which encoding is active
2. If flag=0, try GetEnvironmentStringsW() and cache wide strings
3. Convert wide strings to ANSI using WideCharToMultiByte()
4. If flag=2, use GetEnvironmentStrings() for ANSI directly
5. Return pointer to allocated buffer containing environment strings

Parameters:
- NONE: No parameters

Returns:
- LPSTR: Pointer to environment string buffer (heap-allocated), NULL if failure

functions.name: ExtractPEHeaderMagic
functions.comment:
Extracts PE header magic bytes from the loaded module base address.

Algorithm:
1. Clear the output buffer to 0

functions.name: CopyStringAligned
functions.comment:
Copies a null-terminated string from source to destination using optimized word-aligned copying.

Algorithm:
1. Align source pointer to 4-byte boundary by copying bytes
2. Copy 4-byte chunks while looking for null terminator
3. Detect null in chunk using formula: ~(chunk ^ 0xFFFFFFFF ^ chunk + 0x7EFEFEFF) & 0x81010100
4. When null detected, copy remaining bytes and return

Parameters:

- pszSrc (char*): Source string to copy (null-terminated)

Algorithm:

2. Scan source with word-wide NULL checks using the formula (x ^ -1 ^ (x + 0x7efefeff)) & 0x81010100
3. Copy aligned words from source, detecting partial NULLs byte-by-byte
4. Null-terminate destination and return original destination pointer

Parameters:
- pszDest (uint*): Destination buffer pointer (treated as byte array)
- pszSrc (uint*): Source string pointer (treated as byte array)

Returns:
- Original destination pointer (pszDest)

Notes:
- Uses Knuth-Morris-Pratt-style NULL detection to scan 4 bytes at once
- Handles misaligned source/destination pointers correctly
- Returns destination for potential chaining

2. If overlapping: copy backward from end to start to avoid corruption
3. If non-overlapping: copy forward from start to end
4. Align copies to 4-byte boundaries for efficiency
5. Use DWORD copies when possible, handle remaining bytes individually
6. For unaligned destinations: handle misalignment in 1-3 byte increments first

Parameters:

- pdwSrc (void*): Source buffer pointer
- nBytes (dword): Number of bytes to copy

Returns:

Magic Numbers:
- 0x7: Unroll threshold (copy at least 8 DWORDs before loop)
- 0x3: Alignment mask (checking 4-byte boundary)

functions.name: ModifyFPUControlWord
functions.signature: dword ModifyFPUControlWord(void * this, void * pThis, dword dwMaskBits, dword dwSetBits)
functions.comment:
Modifies x87 FPU control word by clearing and setting specified bits.

Algorithm:
1. Save current FPU control word to stack via FSTCW instruction
2. Call FUN_6f918310 to read current hardware FPU control word state
3. Apply mask operation: clear bits in dwMaskBits (using ~mask & current)
4. Apply set operation: set bits in dwSetBits (using result | dwSetBits)
5. Call FUN_6f9183a2 to write modified control word back to FPU
6. Restore FPU control word from stack via FLDCW instruction
7. Return the newly set control word value

Parameters:
- pThis (void*): Implicit this pointer (unused)
- dwMaskBits (dword): Bit positions to clear from FPU control word
- dwSetBits (dword): Bit positions to set in FPU control word

Returns:
- dword: The new FPU control word value after all modifications

Magic Numbers:
- 0x1/0x2/0x4/0x8/0x10/0x20: Individual control flag bits
- 0xc00/0x300/0x1000: Multi-bit rounding and exception control fields

functions.name: SetFPUControlWordMasked
functions.signature: void SetFPUControlWordMasked(void * this, void * pThis, dword dwControlMask, dword dwControlValue)
functions.comment:
Sets FPU control word with mask applied to control value.

Algorithm:
1. Receives FPU control value and mask parameters
2. Applies 0xfff7ffff mask to control value (clears bit 19)
3. Calls ModifyFPUControlWord with masked control value
4. Returns to caller

Parameters:
- this (void*): Processor context object (ECX, __thiscall)
- dwControlMask: Mask value for FPU control word bits
- dwControlValue: New FPU control word value to apply

Returns:
- void

Magic Numbers:
- 0xfff7ffff: Mask that clears bit 19 of control value

Related Functions:

functions.name: ConvertFPUControlWordBits
functions.comment:
Converts FPU control word bits from one representation to another.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize result to 0
2. For each input bit position, check if set and output corresponding FPU control bit
3. Bit mapping: Input bit 0→output bit 4, bit 2→bit 3, bit 3→bit 2, bit 4→bit 1, bit 5→bit 0
4. Bits 10-11 map to exception mask bits (8-9)
5. Bits 8-9 map to precision bits (16-17)
6. Bit 12 maps to bit 18

Parameters:
- dwCtrlWord (uint): FPU control word bits to convert

Returns:
- Converted control word value

Related Functions:
- ModifyFPUControlWord: Caller that modifies FPU state
- FUN_6f9183a2: Applies the converted control word

functions.name: ConvertFPUControlWordBits
functions.comment:
Converts x87 FPU control word bits from Storm format to Windows/CPU format.

Algorithm:
1. Map input bit positions to output bit positions using conditional ORs
2. Process individual flag bits (0x1, 0x2, 0x4, 0x8, 0x10, 0x80000) to output positions (0x20, 0x10, 0x8, 0x4, 0x1, 0x2)
3. Decode rounding mode from input bits 0x300 (0x100→0x400, 0x200→0x800, 0x300→0xc00)
4. Decode exception mask from input bits 0x30000 (default 0x300, 0x10000→0x200)
5. Map precision control bit 0x40000 to output 0x1000
6. Return converted control word

Parameters:
- dwInputCtrlWord (uint): FPU control word in Storm format

Returns:
- uint: FPU control word in Windows/CPU format (x87 hardware format)

functions.name: IsBitfieldRangeEmpty
functions.comment:
Checks if a bitfield range from nBitIndex onwards contains only empty bits.

Algorithm:
1. Check if the bit at nBitIndex in the target word is empty (0)
2. If not empty, return 0 (range contains set bits)
3. Otherwise, check all remaining words from word_index+1 to word 2 (inclusive)
4. If any remaining word is non-zero, return 0
5. If all bits in range are empty, return 1

Parameters:
- dwBitfieldPtr (uint): Pointer to array of bitfield words (32-bit each)
- nBitIndex (int): Starting bit index to check (0-63, logically 0-95 for 3 words)

Returns:
- 1 if all bits from nBitIndex onwards are empty (0)
- 0 if any bit in range is set (1)

functions.name: ClearBitAndPropagate
functions.comment:
Clear specified bit and propagate changes backward through bit array.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate word index and bit position within word (param_2 / 0x20 = word, param_2 % 0x20 = bit)
2. Clear the specified bit using bitwise AND with inverted mask
3. Check result from first word; propagate backward if success
4. Process preceding words from high to low index
5. Stop early if operation returns failure (non-zero status)

Parameters:
- pBitArray (uint *): Pointer to array of 32-bit words
- nBitIndex (dword): Zero-based bit index to clear

Returns:
- void

Related Functions:

functions.name: ClearBitfieldRange
functions.comment:

3. Check if starting bit is set and following bits are empty (via IsBitfieldRangeEmpty)
4. If conditions met, recursively clear from previous bit position
5. Clear all bits from start position onward in the current dword
6. Zero all remaining dwords up to the 3-dword limit
7. Return result from recursive call, or 0 if no recursion occurred

Parameters:
- nBitfieldBase (int): Base address of the bitfield array (3 dwords, 96 bits total)
- nBitIndex (int): Bit index to start clearing from (0-95, right-aligned)

functions.name: InitMbcsCharacterClassTable
functions.comment:
Initialize MBCS character class table for specified code page.

Algorithm:
1. Acquire critical section lock (index 0x19)
2. Resolve code page type (-3=ACP, -2=OEM, -4=default, else literal)
3. If same as current code page, return 0 (already initialized)
4. Search known code page table for predefined character ranges
5. If found: populate abCharacterClassTable from predefined ranges
6. If not found: call GetCPInfo() to get lead byte ranges
7. For MBCS: mark lead bytes with 0x04 flag, all bytes with 0x08 flag
8. Store code page metadata (locale ID, info fields)
9. Release critical section and return status

Parameters:
- nCodePageType (int): Code page specifier (-3=ANSI, -2=OEM, -4=default, or literal code page)

Returns:
- 0 on success
- -1 (0xFFFFFFFF) on GetCPInfo failure when code page required

Magic Numbers:
- 0x19: Critical section index for MBCS
- 0x30: Stride of known code page table entries
- 0x40: Size of character class table in DWORDs (256 bytes)
- 0x04: Lead byte flag in character class
- 0x08: MBCS byte flag in character class

5. Otherwise return nCodePage unchanged (flag stays 0)

Parameters:

Returns:

Magic Numbers:

- -3: CP_ACP - Use ANSI code page
- -4: Use default code page from g_nDefaultCodePage

functions.name: CoalesceFreeBlock
functions.comment:
Coalesces adjacent free blocks in custom heap allocator free-list.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate page index from block address (offset >> 15)
2. Get free-list header from page table (stride 0x204)
3. Check if current block is free (low bit = 0)
4. Attempt to merge with next block if free:
   - Unlink next block from size-bucket list
   - Combine sizes
5. Attempt to merge with previous block if free:
   - Unlink previous block from size-bucket list
   - Combine sizes
6. Insert coalesced block into appropriate size bucket
7. Update bitmap flags for bucket occupancy
8. If page becomes empty, release virtual memory

Parameters:
- pdwTable (uint*): Allocation table entry (5 DWORDs)
- nBlockAddr (int): Address of block being freed

Returns:
- void (modifies global allocator state)

Magic Numbers:
- 0x8000: Page size (32KB)
- 0x204: Page table stride (516 bytes)
- 0x144: Free-list header offset
- 0x3f (63): Max bucket index
- 0x20 (32): Bitmap split point

Structure Layout (Block Header):
| Offset | Size | Field                    |
|--------|------|--------------------------|
| -4     | 4    | dwSize (low bit = in-use)|
| -8     | 4    | dwPrevSize               |
| +4     | 4    | pNext (free list)        |
| +8     | 4    | pPrev (free list)        |

functions.name: AllocatePoolBlock
functions.comment:
Allocates a memory block from the segregated free list pool allocator.

Algorithm:
1. Align requested size to 16-byte boundary: (dwRequestSize + 0x17) & 0xFFFFFFF0
2. Calculate size class index from aligned size (shift right 4, subtract 1)
3. Build bitmask for size class (bits 0-31 for small, 32-63 for large)
4. Search allocation table entries for one with free blocks in the size class
5. If no suitable entry found, create new allocation table entry via CreateAllocTableEntry
6. Initialize pool bucket for the entry via InitializePoolBucket if needed
7. Find first free block in the appropriate size class bucket
8. Unlink block from free list, update bitmap counters
9. Split block if remainder is large enough for separate size class
10. Mark allocated block with size+1 header/footer for in-use detection
11. Return pointer to usable memory (after 4-byte header)

Parameters:
- dwRequestSize: Requested allocation size in bytes

Returns:
- void*: Pointer to allocated memory, or NULL on failure

Magic Numbers:
- 0x17 (23): Alignment adjustment (16-byte align + 8-byte header overhead - 1)
- 0x10 (16): Alignment granularity
- 0x14 (20): Allocation table entry stride (5 DWORDs)
- 0x20 (32): Boundary between low/high bitmask halves
- 0x3F (63): Maximum size class index
- 0x81 (129): Bucket stride in DWORDs
- 0x11 (17): Offset to low bitmap array
- 0x31 (49): Offset to high bitmap array
- 0x51 (81): Offset to bucket free list heads

1. Check if table is full (g_dwAllocCount == g_dwAllocCapacity)
2. If full, grow table by 0x10 entries using HeapReAlloc

4. Allocate 0x41c4 byte heap block (HEAP_ZERO_MEMORY flag 0x8)
5. Allocate 1MB virtual memory (MEM_RESERVE 0x2000, PAGE_READWRITE 0x4)

- 0x14 (20): Entry stride (5 dwords)
- 0x41c4 (16836): Heap block size

- 0x50 (80): Base table size (0x10 entries * 5 dwords)

functions.name: InitializePoolBucket
functions.comment:
Initializes a new pool bucket for memory allocation.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate bucket index by counting leading zero bits
2. Compute offset to bucket free list area
3. Initialize 63 empty doubly-linked list heads
4. Allocate 32KB via VirtualAlloc at computed address
5. Divide into 4KB pages with free block headers
6. Link blocks into free list
7. Update bucket state flags

Parameters:
- pPoolHeader (PoolHeader*): Pool header structure

Returns:
- Bucket index (0-31) on success
- -1 on allocation failure

Magic Numbers:
- 0x204: Bucket descriptor stride
- 0x144: First bucket offset
- 0x8000: 32KB bucket size
- 0x3F: 63 size class lists
- 0xFF0: Usable bytes per page

functions.name: TryResizePoolBlock
functions.signature: int TryResizePoolBlock(uint * pPoolHeader, byte * pbBlock, int nNewSize)
functions.comment:
Attempts to resize a memory block in-place within a pool allocator.

Algorithm:
1. Align requested size to 16-byte boundary (add 0x17, mask 0xFFFFFFF0)
2. Calculate region index from block offset (block - base >> 15)
3. Read current block size from header at pbBlock-4
4. If new size > current: check next block for coalescence
   a. Verify next block is free (bit 0 = 0) and combined size fits
   b. Unlink next block from free list, update bucket bitmaps
   c. If remainder exists, insert into appropriate free list
5. If new size < current: split block
   a. Optionally coalesce with free next block
   b. Insert freed portion into appropriate free list bucket
6. Update block size tags at both ends of resized block

Parameters:
- pPoolHeader (uint*): Pool header with bitmaps at [0],[1] and data at [4]
- pbBlock (byte*): Memory block address to resize
- nNewSize (int): Requested new size in bytes

Returns:
- 1 on successful resize (in-place)
- 0 if resize not possible (next block in use or combined size insufficient)

Magic Numbers:
- 0x17: Alignment adjustment for 16-byte boundary
- 0xFFFFFFF0: 16-byte alignment mask
- 0x3F (63): Maximum bucket index
- 0x20 (32): Bucket threshold for bitmap split (low/high)
- 0x204 (516): Free list stride per region
- 0x144 (324): Base offset to free lists in pool data
- 0x44 (68): Low bucket bitmap array offset
- 0xC4 (196): High bucket bitmap array offset
- 0x80000000: MSB for bitmap bit operations

functions.name: AllocateMemoryPool
functions.comment:
Allocates and initializes a memory pool for the slab allocator.

Algorithm:
1. Select pool control block (static at 0x6f922660 if g_nPoolMode=-1, else HeapAlloc 0x2020 bytes)
2. Reserve 4MB virtual address space (MEM_RESERVE, PAGE_READWRITE)
3. Commit first 64KB of reserved space (MEM_COMMIT)
4. Initialize linked list pointers (doubly-linked pool list)
5. Initialize 1024 size class entries (8 bytes each, 0x2000 total)
6. Zero first 64KB and initialize 16 page headers (4KB stride)
7. Return pool pointer or NULL on failure

Parameters:
- None (void)

Returns:
- void**: Pointer to pool control block, NULL on allocation failure

Magic Numbers:
- 0x2020: Pool control block size (8 list ptrs + 1024*8 size entries)
- 0x400000 (4MB): Virtual address reservation size
- 0x10000 (64KB): Initial commit size
- 0x400 (1024): Number of size class entries
- 0xf1 (241): Size class maximum value
- 0x1000 (4KB): Page stride for header initialization

functions.name: FreePoolNode
functions.comment:
Frees a pool node and its virtual memory, unlinking from doubly-linked list.

Algorithm:
1. Free virtual memory at ppNode[4] (offset 0x10) with MEM_RELEASE
2. If this node is the list head, update g_pPoolListHead to next node
3. If node is the static sentinel (g_PoolNodeStatic), set state to -1 and return
4. Otherwise, unlink from list: prev->next = next, next->prev = prev
5. Free the node structure via HeapFree

Parameters:
- ppNode (void**): Pointer to pool node structure to free

Returns:
- void

Node Structure Layout:
- [0x00] pNext: Pointer to next node
- [0x04] pPrev: Pointer to previous node
- [0x10] pVirtualMem: Virtual memory block to release

functions.name: ReleaseUnusedPoolPages
functions.comment:
Releases unused pool pages by decommitting virtual memory.

Algorithm:
1. Walk pool node list starting from g_pStaticPoolTail
2. For each node with valid virtual memory (not 0xFFFFFFFF)
3. Scan page table entries from high to low offset
4. If entry is 0xF0 (releasable), call VirtualFree with MEM_DECOMMIT
5. Mark freed entry as 0xFFFFFFFF and decrement g_nReleasablePages
6. Update first-free pointer if this entry is lower
7. After freeing pages, check if node is completely empty
8. If all 0x400 entries are 0xFFFFFFFF, free the entire node
9. Continue to next node until nMaxPages exhausted

Parameters:
- nMaxPages (int): Maximum number of pages to release

Returns:
- void

Magic Numbers:
- 0xF0: Page status indicating releasable
- 0xFFFFFFFF: Page status indicating freed/invalid
- 0x1000: Page size (4KB)
- 0x4000: MEM_DECOMMIT flag
- 0x400: Max entries per pool node (1024)
- 0x3FF000: Starting offset (1023 pages * 4KB)

functions.name: FindStaticPoolSlot
functions.signature: int FindStaticPoolSlot(byte * pbPtr, void * * ppPoolHeader, uint * pdwPageBase)
functions.comment:
Finds the static pool slot index for a given pointer.

Algorithm:
1. Traverse circular linked list starting from g_pStaticPoolHead
2. For each pool, check if pbPtr falls within [pPool+0x10, pPool+0x14] range
3. Return 0 if not found in any pool
4. Validate alignment: pbPtr must be 16-byte aligned (& 0xF == 0)
5. Validate page offset: (pbPtr & 0xFFF) must be >= 0x100
6. Calculate slot index = ((pbPtr - pageBase - 0x100) >> 4) + 8 + pageBase

Parameters:
- pbPtr (byte*): Pointer to find in static pools
- ppPoolHeader (void**): OUT - receives pool header pointer
- pdwPageBase (uint*): OUT - receives page-aligned base address

Returns:
- Slot index combining page base + slot offset on success
- 0 if pointer not found or invalid alignment

Magic Numbers:
- 0x10, 0x14: Pool header offsets for range start/end pointers
- 0xF: 16-byte alignment mask
- 0x100 (256): Page header size reserved at start
- 0xFFF, 0xFFFFF000: Page offset and page base masks

functions.name: ReturnPoolSlotToPage
functions.signature: void ReturnPoolSlotToPage(int * pPoolNode, int nPoolAddress, byte * pbSlotBlocks)
functions.comment:
Returns a pool slot to its containing page, updating page block counts.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate page table entry from pool node and address offset
2. Add slot's block count to page's free block counter
3. Clear slot's block count (mark slot as returned)
4. Set page status to 0xF1 (released)
5. If page is fully free (0xF0 blocks), increment releasable page counter
6. When 32 pages are releasable, trigger batch release of 16 pages

Parameters:
- pPoolNode (int*): Pool node structure containing page table at offset 0x18
- nPoolAddress (int): Address within pool to calculate page index
- pbSlotBlocks (byte*): Pointer to slot's block count (cleared on return)

Returns:
- void

Magic Numbers:
- 0x18: Offset to page table array in pool node
- 0x10: Offset to base address in pool node
- 0xC (12): Page size shift (4KB pages)
- 0x8: Page table entry stride (8 bytes per entry)
- 0xF0 (240): Max blocks per page (page fully free threshold)
- 0xF1 (241): Page status indicating released
- 0x20 (32): Releasable pages threshold to trigger batch release
- 0x10 (16): Number of pages to release in batch

functions.name: AllocateFromPool
functions.comment:
Allocates memory block of requested size from the memory pool system.

Algorithm:
1. Search active pool list (g_pPoolListHead) for suitable free block
2. For each pool, scan allocation table entries (8-byte pairs: size, limit)
3. If block found via FUN_6f91a297, subdivide and return allocated block
4. If no block in active pools, search static pool list (g_pStaticPoolHead)
5. If static pool has free pages marked -1, commit with VirtualAlloc
6. Initialize committed pages with memset and set up block headers
7. If all pools exhausted, call AllocateMemoryPool to create new pool
8. Update pool head pointer and allocation table on success

Parameters:
- dwSize (uint): Requested allocation size in bytes

Returns:
- void*: Pointer to allocated memory block (offset 0x100 from header)
- NULL: Allocation failed (no memory available)

Magic Numbers:
- 0x1000: Page size and block table stride
- 0x2018: End offset of upper allocation table in pool
- 0x18: Start offset of lower allocation table
- 0xF0: Initial free space in new block (240 bytes)
- 0xF1: Block limit marker (241)
- 0x100: Offset from block header to user data (256 bytes)
- 0x10: Maximum pages to commit at once (16)

functions.name: FindPoolFreeBlock
functions.signature: int FindPoolFreeBlock(int * pPool, uint dwBudget, uint dwSize)
functions.comment:
Searches pool for free block of requested size.

Algorithm:
1. Check if remaining space at current position can satisfy request
2. If not, scan forward for zero bytes indicating free blocks
3. Count consecutive zeros to find free block size
4. If block found >= dwSize, allocate and update pool state
5. Uses dwBudget as iteration limit to prevent infinite loops

Parameters:
- pPool (int*): Pool header [0]=current ptr, [1]=remaining, +0xF8=end
- dwBudget (uint): Maximum bytes to scan before giving up
- dwSize (uint): Requested allocation size in bytes

Returns:
- Encoded pointer offset on success (pbResult*16 - pPool*15)
- 0 on allocation failure

Magic Numbers:
- 0x3E (62): DWORDs to end boundary (0xF8 bytes)
- 0x8: Data offset from block header

functions.name: ResizePoolSlotInPlace
functions.signature: int ResizePoolSlotInPlace(PoolHeader * pPoolHdr, int * pPageSlot, byte * pbSlotSize, uint dwNewUnits)

functions.name: ShowMessageBoxWithActiveWindow
functions.signature: int ShowMessageBoxWithActiveWindow(char * lpszText, char * lpszCaption, uint dwType)
functions.comment:
Displays a message box using dynamically loaded user32.dll.

Algorithm:
1. Check if MessageBoxA is already cached
2. If not, load user32.dll via LoadLibraryA
3. Get proc addresses for MessageBoxA, GetActiveWindow, GetLastActivePopup
4. Get active window and last active popup for parent handle
5. Call MessageBoxA with resolved parent window

Parameters:
- lpszText (char*): Message text to display
- lpszCaption (char*): Dialog caption/title
- dwType (uint): MessageBox flags (MB_OK, MB_ICONERROR, etc.)

Returns:
- MessageBox result (IDOK, IDCANCEL, etc.), or 0 on failure

Globals:
- g_pfnMessageBoxA: Cached MessageBoxA function pointer
- g_pfnGetActiveWindow: Cached GetActiveWindow function pointer
- g_pfnGetLastActivePopup: Cached GetLastActivePopup function pointer

functions.name: SaveUnwindContext
functions.comment:
Saves SEH unwind context before invoking exception handlers.

Algorithm:
1. Save [EBP+8] (handler parameter) to g_dwUnwindParam
2. Save EAX (current context) to g_dwUnwindEax
3. Save EBP (stack frame) to g_dwUnwindEbp

Parameters:
- IMPLICIT: EAX contains context value to preserve
- IMPLICIT: EBP+8 contains handler parameter

Returns:
- void (context saved to global structure)

Related Functions:
- __local_unwind2: Caller that invokes exception handlers

functions.name: SehLocalUnwindHelper
functions.comment:
SEH local unwind helper that triggers scope cleanup.

Algorithm:
1. Extract scope table from exception record +0x18
2. Extract try level from exception record +0x1c
3. Call __local_unwind2 to execute cleanup handlers

Parameters:
- pExceptRec (int*): Pointer to exception registration frame

Returns:
- void

Notes:
- Registered dynamically as SEH filter/handler (no static xrefs)
- Offsets +0x18 and +0x1c are scope table and trylevel fields

functions.name: InvokeNewHandler
functions.comment:
Invokes the registered new-handler callback when memory allocation fails.

Algorithm:
1. Check if g_pfnNewHandlerCallback is registered (non-NULL)
2. If registered, call the handler with the requested allocation size
3. Return TRUE if handler succeeded (non-zero), FALSE otherwise

Parameters:
- dwSize (uint): Size of the failed allocation request in bytes

Returns:
- TRUE (1) if handler succeeded and caller should retry allocation
- FALSE (0) if no handler registered or handler failed

Related Functions:
- __nh_malloc: Calls this on allocation failure
- AllocateZeroedMemory: Calls this on allocation failure

functions.name: CompareStringsCaseInsensitive
functions.signature: int CompareStringsCaseInsensitive(byte * pbStr1, char * szStr2, uint dwMaxChars)
functions.comment:
Compares two strings case-insensitively up to nMaxChars characters.

Algorithm:
1. If nMaxChars is 0, return 0 (equal)
2. If g_dwStringCompareMode == 0, use fast ASCII case folding (A-Z -> a-z)
3. Otherwise acquire critical section 0x13 and use TransformCharacterCase for locale-aware comparison
4. Compare character by character until mismatch, null terminator, or nMaxChars reached

Parameters:
- pbStr1 (byte*): First null-terminated string
- szStr2 (char*): Second null-terminated string  
- nMaxChars (uint): Maximum characters to compare

Returns:
- 0: Strings are equal
- -1: pbStr1 < szStr2
- 1: pbStr1 > szStr2

Magic Numbers:
- 0x13 (19): Critical section index for locale operations
- 0x41-0x5A: ASCII 'A'-'Z' range for case folding
- 0x20: Offset to convert uppercase to lowercase

functions.name: LocaleAwareAtoi
functions.comment:
Converts string to integer with locale-aware character classification (atoi equivalent).

Algorithm:
1. Skip leading whitespace using character transform table (flag 0x8 = isspace)
2. Check for optional sign character ('+' 0x2b or '-' 0x2d)
3. Convert consecutive digit characters to integer (flag 0x4 = isdigit)
4. Apply sign negation if leading character was '-'

Parameters:
- szStr (char*): Null-terminated input string

Returns:
- Parsed integer value (negated if preceded by minus sign)

Magic Numbers:
- 0x2b: ASCII '+' (plus sign)
- 0x2d: ASCII '-' (minus sign)
- 0x30: ASCII '0' (digit base for conversion)
- 0x8: Character classification flag for whitespace (isspace)
- 0x4: Character classification flag for digit (isdigit)

Related Functions:
- TransformCharacterWithFlags: Used for locale-aware character classification

functions.name: GetEnvironmentVariable
functions.comment:
Searches for an environment variable value in the command-line arguments array.

Algorithm:
1. Check if command-line arguments have been processed (g_fProcessed)
2. If args array (g_ppCommandArgs) not initialized, attempt to initialize via FUN_6f91b6e7
3. Iterate through args array looking for "VARNAME=value" pattern
4. Use case-insensitive multibyte comparison (__mbsnbicoll) to match variable name
5. Return pointer to value portion (after '=') if found

Parameters:
- szVarName: Environment variable name to search for (e.g., "TZ")

Returns:
- Pointer to value string if found, NULL otherwise

Related Functions:
- FUN_6f91b6e7: Initializes command args from wide-char environment
- InitializeTimeZoneInfo: Primary caller, retrieves TZ variable

functions.name: MapWinErrorToErrno
functions.comment:
Maps Windows error code to C runtime errno.

Algorithm:
1. Store Windows error in TLS slot 3 (GetTlsWinErrorPtr)
2. Search g_adWinToErrnoMap table for matching error code
3. If found, store mapped errno in TLS slot 2 (GetTlsErrnoPtr)
4. If not found, check special ranges:
   - 0x13-0x24: ERROR_WRITE_PROTECT to ERROR_SHARING_BUFFER_EXCEEDED → EACCES (0xD)
   - 0xBC-0xCA: ERROR_INVALID_ORDINAL to ERROR_INVALID_MODULETYPE → ENOEXEC (8)
5. Default unmapped errors → EINVAL (0x16)

Parameters:
- dwWinError (DWORD): Windows error code from GetLastError

Returns:
- void: Sets TLS errno value, no return

Magic Numbers:
- 0xD (13): EACCES - permission denied
- 0x8: ENOEXEC - exec format error
- 0x16 (22): EINVAL - invalid argument (default)

functions.name: GetTlsErrnoPtr
functions.comment:
Returns pointer to errno field in thread-local storage.

Algorithm:
1. Call GetThreadLocalStorage to get TLS block pointer
2. Add offset 8 (2 DWORDs) to reach errno field
3. Return pointer to errno storage location

Parameters:
- None (uses global TLS index internally)

Returns:
- uint*: Pointer to thread's errno value at TLS offset 0x8

TLS Block Layout:
- Offset 0x0: Thread ID (DWORD)
- Offset 0x4: Default value (DWORD, init -1)
- Offset 0x8: errno value (DWORD) <- this function

functions.name: GetTlsWinErrorPtr
functions.comment:
Returns pointer to the Windows error code slot in thread-local storage.

Algorithm:
1. Get thread-local storage base via GetThreadLocalStorage()
2. Return pointer to DWORD at offset +0xC (Windows error slot)

Parameters:
- None (void function)

Returns:
- DWORD* to TLS slot storing last Windows error code

Related Functions:
- GetThreadLocalStorage: Retrieves TLS base pointer
- MapWinErrorToErrno: Uses this to store/retrieve Windows errors

functions.name: InvalidateFileHandle
functions.comment:
Invalidates a file handle entry in the CRT handle table.

Algorithm:
1. Validates handle index against g_dwHandleLimit
2. Locates entry in g_pBufferTable using index (entry size=0x24)
3. Checks if entry is valid (flag byte & 1) and open (!= -1)
4. For stdin(0)/stdout(1)/stderr(2), calls SetStdHandle to clear
5. Marks entry as invalid (-1 sentinel value)
6. Sets errno=EBADF(9) on invalid handles

Parameters:
- dwHandleIndex (uint): CRT file handle index to invalidate

Returns:
- 0: Success, handle invalidated
- -1: Failure, invalid handle (errno set to EBADF)

Magic Numbers:
- 0x24 (36): Handle table entry stride
- 0x1f (31): Mask for index within table segment
- 0xfffffff6 (-10): STD_INPUT_HANDLE
- 0xfffffff5 (-11): STD_OUTPUT_HANDLE
- 0xfffffff4 (-12): STD_ERROR_HANDLE
- 9: EBADF errno value

functions.name: GetFileHandleFromBuffer
functions.comment:
Retrieves a file handle from the internal buffer table.

Algorithm:
1. Validate buffer ID is within the handle limit
2. Calculate buffer entry location using 32-entry group indexing
3. Check if buffer entry is valid (bit 0 set in state flags)
4. If valid, return the stored file handle
5. If invalid, set errno to 9 (EBADF) and clear Win32 error

Parameters:
- dwBufferId (uint): Index into the buffer table

Returns:
- Valid file handle on success
- 0xffffffff on failure (invalid buffer ID or inactive entry)

Magic Numbers:
- 0x1f (31): Mask for entry index within 32-entry group
- 0x24 (36): Size of each buffer entry structure
- 0x9: EBADF errno value (bad file descriptor)

functions.name: LockBufferSlotCriticalSection
functions.comment:
Locks the critical section for a buffer slot, initializing it on first use.

Algorithm:
1. Extract table index (bits 5+) and slot index (bits 0-4) from handle
2. Look up buffer entry in g_pBufferTable
3. If critical section not initialized (offset+8 == 0):
   a. Acquire global critical section 0x11
   b. Double-check initialization flag (DCL pattern)
   c. Initialize critical section at offset+0xC
   d. Set initialization flag at offset+8
   e. Release global critical section
4. Enter the buffer slot's critical section

Parameters:
- dwSlotHandle (uint): Combined handle: bits 5+ = table index, bits 0-4 = slot index

Returns:
- void (locks critical section, caller must unlock)

Magic Numbers:
- 0x1F (31): Mask for slot index within table entry
- 0x24 (36): Buffer structure stride in bytes
- 0x11 (17): Global critical section index for buffer init
- 0x08: Offset to initialization flag
- 0x0C: Offset to CRITICAL_SECTION within structure

functions.name: UnlockBufferSlotCriticalSection
functions.comment:
Release critical section for a buffer slot.

Algorithm:
1. Extract slot index from buffer ID (lower 5 bits)
2. Extract table index from buffer ID (upper bits >> 5)
3. Calculate critical section address at offset 0xC in buffer entry
4. Call LeaveCriticalSection to release lock

Parameters:
- dwBufferId (uint): Buffer handle containing table and slot indices

Returns:
- void (no return value)

Magic Numbers:
- 0x1F (31): Mask for slot index (5 bits, 32 slots per table)
- 0x5: Right shift for table index
- 0x24 (36): Buffer entry stride
- 0xC (12): Offset to CRITICAL_SECTION within entry

Related Functions:
- LockBufferSlotCriticalSection: Acquire lock counterpart

functions.name: FlushBufferToFile
functions.comment:
Flushes buffer data to file and optionally syncs to disk.

Algorithm:
1. Call FlushFileBuffer to write pending data
2. If flush fails, return -1
3. If sync flag (0x40) set at offset 0xd, call FUN_6f91b7d2 to sync
4. Return 0 on success, -1 if sync fails

Parameters:
- pBuffer (int*): Buffer structure pointer

Returns:
- 0 on success
- -1 on failure (flush or sync error)

Magic Numbers:
- 0xd: Offset to flags byte in buffer structure
- 0x40: Sync-to-disk flag (FlushFileBuffers required)
- 0x10: Offset to file handle in buffer structure

functions.name: FlushFileBuffer
functions.comment:
Flushes pending write data from a file buffer to disk.

Algorithm:
1. Check if file is in write mode (flags & 3 == 2) and has data to flush (flags & 0x108)
2. Calculate data size: current position - buffer base
3. If positive data size, call BufferWriteData to write pending data
4. On success: clear dirty flag (0xFD mask). On failure: set error flag (0x20), return -1
5. Reset buffer: count = 0, current position = buffer base

Parameters:
- pFileStruct (int*): File structure pointer with fields:
  [0] current pointer, [1] count, [2] base pointer, [3] flags, [4] file handle

Returns:
- 0 on success or no data to flush
- -1 on write failure

Magic Numbers:
- 0x108: Write pending flags mask
- 0x80: Dirty/modified flag
- 0x20: Error flag
- 0xFD: Clear write mode mask

functions.name: FlushAllBuffers
functions.comment:
Flushes all active file buffers in the buffer array.

Algorithm:
1. Acquire global critical section (index 2)
2. Iterate through all buffers in g_pBufferArray
3. For each buffer with valid flags (0x83 = active|open|modified):
   - Acquire buffer-specific critical section
   - If nFlushMode=1: Flush buffer, count successes
   - If nFlushMode=0 and dirty (0x2): Flush buffer, set error on failure
   - Release buffer critical section
4. Release global critical section
5. Return success count (mode 1) or error status (mode 0)

Parameters:
- nFlushMode (int): 0=flush only dirty buffers (return -1 on failure),
                    1=flush all active buffers (return count of successes)

Returns:
- Mode 1: Count of successfully flushed buffers
- Mode 0: 0 on success, -1 if any flush failed

Magic Numbers:
- 0x83: Buffer flags mask (active|open|modified)
- 0x2: Dirty/modified flag

functions.name: UInt32Add
functions.signature: bool UInt32Add(uint dwAugend, uint dwAddend, uint * pdwResult)
functions.comment:
Add two unsigned 32-bit integers with overflow detection.

Algorithm:
1. Compute sum = dwAugend + dwAddend
2. Check overflow via comparison (sum < dwAugend || sum < dwAddend)
3. Store result in pdwResult output parameter
4. Return TRUE (1) if overflow, FALSE (0) otherwise

Parameters:
- dwAugend (uint): First operand
- dwAddend (uint): Second operand  
- pdwResult (uint*): Output pointer for sum

Returns:
- TRUE (1): Overflow occurred (result invalid)
- FALSE (0): No overflow (result valid)

Related Functions:
- ___add_12: Multi-word addition using this function

functions.name: ShiftLeft96Bit
functions.comment:
Shifts a 96-bit value left by 1 bit with carry propagation.

Algorithm:
1. Save low and mid DWORDs
2. Shift low DWORD left by 1 (multiply by 2)
3. Shift mid DWORD left by 1, OR in carry from low (bit 31)
4. Shift high DWORD left by 1, OR in carry from mid (bit 31)

Parameters:

Returns:

Related Functions:

functions.name: ShiftRight96Bit
functions.comment:
Shifts a 96-bit value right by 1 bit.

Algorithm:
1. Save middle dword (pdwValue[1])
2. Shift middle dword right, OR in MSB from high dword
3. Shift high dword (pdwValue[2]) right by 1
4. Shift low dword right, OR in MSB from saved middle value

Parameters:
- pdwValue (uint*): Pointer to 3-element uint array (96 bits total)
  - [0] = low 32 bits
  - [1] = middle 32 bits
  - [2] = high 32 bits

Returns:
- void (result stored in-place)

Related Functions:

functions.name: ConvertDigitsTo96BitFloat
functions.signature: void ConvertDigitsTo96BitFloat(byte * pbDigits, int nDigitCount, uint * pdwMantissa)
functions.comment:
Converts ASCII digit string to 96-bit extended precision float mantissa.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize 96-bit accumulator to zero, exponent to 0x404E
2. For each digit: multiply accumulator by 10 (shift*4 + original = *5, shift = *10)
3. Add current digit value (0-9) to accumulator
4. Normalize: shift left by 16 bits while high dword is zero
5. Normalize: shift left by 1 bit while high bit not set
6. Store final exponent at mantissa[10] (offset +0xA)

Parameters:
- pbDigits (byte*): Array of digit values (NOT ASCII - already converted 0-9)
- nDigitCount (int): Number of digits to process
- pdwMantissa (uint*): Output 12-byte (96-bit) mantissa buffer

Returns:
- void (result stored in pdwMantissa)

Magic Numbers:
- 0x404E: Initial exponent bias for 80-bit float
- 0xFFF0: Exponent adjustment per 16-bit shift (-16)
- 0xFFFF: Exponent adjustment per 1-bit shift (-1)
- 0x8000: High bit mask for normalization check

functions.name: ParseFloatString
functions.signature: void ParseFloatString(void * this, void * pOutput, ushort * pResult, int * pnEndPtr, byte * pbInput, int nPrecision, int nDefaultExp, int nExpAdjust, int nAllowSign)
functions.comment:
Parses a floating-point number string into internal representation.

Algorithm:
1. Skip leading whitespace (space, tab, newline, CR)
2. Parse optional sign (+/-) and set wSign
3. Collect digits before decimal point via state machine
4. Handle decimal separator from g_byCharacterSwapValue
5. Collect fractional digits after decimal
6. Parse optional exponent (E/e with +/- and digits)
7. Limit digits to 25 (0x19), track overflow count
8. Convert digit buffer to mantissa via FUN_6f91ad42
9. Apply exponent adjustments and precision scaling
10. Call FUN_6f91ba85 to finalize float representation

Parameters:
- pThis (void*): Context pointer (unused internally)
- pResult (ushort*): 12-byte output buffer for float representation
- pnEndPtr (int*): Receives pointer to first unparsed char
- pbInput (byte*): Input string to parse
- nPrecision (int): Precision control parameter
- nDefaultExp (int): Default exponent when none specified
- nExpAdjust (int): Exponent adjustment value
- fAllowSign (int): If non-zero, allows +/- before exponent

Returns:
- 0: Success
- 1: Underflow
- 2: Overflow
- 4: Invalid/empty input

Magic Numbers:
- 0x19 (25): Maximum digits to collect
- 0x1450 (5200): Maximum exponent magnitude
- 0x8000: Negative sign flag
- 0x30 ('0'): ASCII digit base

functions.name: ConvertExtendedToDecimalString
functions.signature: int ConvertExtendedToDecimalString(uint dwMantissaLo, uint dwMantissaHi, uint dwSignAndExp, int nPrecision, byte bFlags, short * pOutput)
functions.comment:
Converts 80-bit extended precision float to decimal string.

Algorithm:
1. Extract sign (0x8000) and biased exponent (0x7FFF mask)
2. Set sign char: '-' for negative, ' ' for positive
3. If mantissa/exponent all zero: output "0" and return 1
4. If exponent == 0x7FFF (special): detect INF/NaN/IND
5. Estimate decimal exponent via log10 approximation formula
6. Normalize via FUN_6f91ba85 scaling by -decimalExp
7. If exp >= 0x3FFF: increment decimalExp, divide by 10
8. Extract digits via multiply-by-10 loop (max 21 digits)
9. Round: if last digit > '4', propagate carry backward
10. Strip trailing zeros, set string length, null-terminate

Parameters:
- dwMantissaLo (uint): Low 32 bits of mantissa
- dwMantissaHi (uint): High 32 bits of mantissa  
- dwSignAndExp (uint): Sign bit 0x8000 + 15-bit exponent
- nPrecision (int): Max decimal digits (clamped to 21)
- bFlags (byte): Bit 0 = relative precision mode
- pOutput (short*): Output buffer pointer

Returns:
- 1: Normal number converted successfully
- 0: Special value (INF, NaN, IND) written to buffer

Output Buffer Layout (packed struct):
- [0-1]: Decimal exponent (short)
- [2]: Sign character '-' or ' '
- [3]: Digit count (byte)
- [4+]: ASCII digit chars (no decimal point)

functions.name: CharToUppercase
functions.comment:
Converts a character to uppercase.

Algorithm:
1. If g_dwStringCompareMode == 0 (fast ASCII mode):
   - If char is 'a'-'z' (0x61-0x7a), subtract 0x20 to convert to 'A'-'Z'
   - Otherwise return unchanged
2. If g_dwStringCompareMode != 0 (locale-aware mode):
   - Increment semaphore count, acquire critical section 0x13 if needed
   - Call FUN_6f91b5dc for locale-aware uppercase conversion
   - Release critical section or decrement semaphore count
   - Return converted character

Parameters:
- dwChar (uint): Character code to convert (ASCII or locale-specific)

Returns:
- Uppercase character code, or original if not convertible

Magic Numbers:
- 0x61 (97): ASCII 'a' lowercase start
- 0x7a (122): ASCII 'z' lowercase end
- 0x20 (32): ASCII case conversion offset
- 0x13 (19): Critical section index for locale operations

functions.name: CharToUpperLocale
functions.signature: uint CharToUpperLocale(void * this, void * pContext, uint dwChar)
functions.comment:
Converts a character to uppercase using locale-aware rules.

Algorithm:
1. If g_dwStringCompareMode is 0, use ASCII-only:
   - Convert 'a'-'z' (0x61-0x7a) to 'A'-'Z' by subtracting 0x20
2. Otherwise, check if character is single-byte (< 0x100):
   a. If g_dwCharacterTransformMode < 2, check transform table bit 2
   b. Else call TransformCharacterWithFlags with flag 2
   c. If character is not transformable, return unchanged
3. Check high byte in transform table for DBCS lead byte (bit 0x80):
   a. If not lead byte, use 1-byte conversion
   b. If lead byte, swap bytes for 2-byte conversion
4. Call LocaleMapStringWithConversion with LCMAP_UPPERCASE (0x200)
5. Return converted character (1 or 2 bytes based on result length)

Parameters:
- pContext (void*): Context pointer passed through to subroutines
- dwChar (uint): Character code to convert (may be DBCS)

Returns:
- uint: Uppercase version of input character, or unchanged if not convertible

Magic Numbers:
- 0x61 (97): ASCII 'a'
- 0x7a (122): ASCII 'z'
- 0x20 (32): ASCII case offset
- 0x100 (256): Single-byte character boundary
- 0x200: LCMAP_UPPERCASE flag
- 0x80: DBCS lead byte indicator bit
